scope: contracts/src, contracts/script, contracts/deploy, onchain packers and loader, contracts/test, docs and checklists; in the critic round also site/, registration-relayer/, launch/HOSTING-HEADERS.md, contracts/scripts/site-config.mjs, site/tools/sync_orkhanart.py
method: 10 finder lenses; 3 adversarial verifiers per finding (refute by code, by record and tests, by impact); Foundry PoC for confirmed Medium+; completeness critic and 5 gap lenses; continuation run re-verifying the 16 findings whose verifiers hit a usage limit; Glamsterdam spec research with read-only Sepolia/mainnet eth_estimateGas; empirical decoding of the real 1/1 tokenURI. findings.title: On the two mainnet RPCs in 1.json the log scan from deployBlock can never complete: publicnode refuses eth_getLogs older than ~10-12k blocks as an archive request, drpc caps the range at ~101 blocks, and rpc.js never fails over on a JSON-RPC error
findings.description: chain.js scans BidPlaced and Transfer logs from cfg.deployBlock on every fresh visit (line 339 `var first = cfg.deployBlock || 0;`, 354-360 `R.getLogsChunked(read, {...}, bFrom, to)`), through rpc.js getLogsChunked (152 `chunk = opts.chunk || 10000`; 162-165 halve on code -32005/-32602/-32614 or /range|10000|too many|limit|exceed|large/, `if (!tooMuch || chunk <= 1) throw err`). Probed read-only on 10 Oct (head 26,166,589) against the exact hosts in site/chains/1.json lines 4-7: ethereum-rpc.publicnode.com answers any eth_getLogs whose fromBlock is more than ~10,000-12,000 blocks behind head (about 1.5 days) with HTTP 403 and the JSON-RPC error {code:-32602, message:"Archive requests require a personal token..."}, for a 1-block span as much as a 10,000-block one; a 10,000-block span at the head succeeds. eth.drpc.org answers any span of 128 blocks or more, at any age, with HTTP 400 {code:35, message:"ranges over 10000 blocks are not supported on free plan"}; 101 blocks succeed. rpc.js post() treats 403 and 400 as ordinary answers (line 33 `if (res.status >= 500 || res.status === 429)` is the only transport branch) and send() moves to the next URL only on transport errors (line 48 `if (!err.transport) throw err`). So on publicnode (preferred first) the halving loop issues 14 refused requests (10000 down to 1) then throws; refresh retries scanLogs three times (chain.js 305-308), sets `S.stale = 'Can’t reach Ethereum right now. Retrying…'` (312), and repeats every 12 s poll because bidsTo stays 0. On drpc the halving settles at 78-block chunks, i.e. about 92 sequential requests per stream per day since deployment, per fresh visitor, under free-tier rate limits. Neither the probe files (contracts/audit/rpc-gas-caps-mainnet.txt measures eth_call only) nor any test covers a node that rejects a log range: the only stub is 'silently short' (site/test/wallet-safety.test.mjs 51-56). W-04 records only a deployBlock that is too late; this is the configured RPCs refusing the correct deployBlock.
findings.scenario: Launch day: deployment on day 0, startsAt two or more days later (verify, publish, inspection window, as 3-post-deploy.md orders). Any visitor opening the auction page after ~1.5 days gets the auction totals (eth_call succeeds) but an empty bid book ('No bids yet. The first one starts the 24-hour clock.', auction.js 371-372) under a live high bid, empty 'your motifs' holdings (rebuildOwned from Transfer logs), and the permanent stale note. During registration the Register button is disabled whenever status().stale is set (auction.js 297 `enabled = ... && !s.stale && !placing`), so no wallet can check in from the page at all; bidding (line 290 does not test stale) works but shows a contradictory book. Each open tab sends ~42 refused eth_getLogs to publicnode every 12 s (126 with a wallet connected), which invites a 429, after which every request fails over to drpc and the same scan runs in 78-block pieces for minutes per visitor. Nothing is lost on-chain; the site misreports the auction for everyone and blocks registration from the page.
findings.evidence: site/chains/1.json 4-7: `"rpcUrls": ["https://ethereum-rpc.publicnode.com", "https://eth.drpc.org"]`. Probe output (curl, 10 Oct): publicnode `span 1 back 10000 -> result [] [HTTP 200]`, `span 1 back 12000 -> {"error":{"code":-32602,"message":"Archive requests require a personal token..."}} [HTTP 403]`, `span 10000 back 100000 -> same 403`; drpc `span 101 back 0 -> result [] [HTTP 200]`, `span 128 back 0 -> {"error":{"message":"ranges over 10000 blocks are not supported on free plan","code":35}} [HTTP 400]`, `span 100 back 1000000 -> result [] [HTTP 200]`. rpc.js 33: `if (res.status >= 500 || res.status === 429) { ... e.transport = true; throw e; }`; 48: `catch (err) { last = err; if (!err.transport) throw err; }`; 164: `if (!tooMuch || chunk <= 1) throw err;`. chain.js 339: `var first = cfg.deployBlock || 0;`; 306-307: `try { await scanLogs(bn); break; } catch (e) { if (tries >= 2) throw e; ... }`; 312: `S.stale = 'Can’t reach ' + ... + ' right now. Retrying…';`. auction.js 297: `enabled = !a.registered && !a.youAreTreasury && !s.writesDisabled && !s.error && !s.stale && !placing;`. contracts/AUDIT.md 385 (W-04) speaks only of 'A deployBlock that is too late'.
findings.fix: Pick a read RPC (keyed or archive-capable) that serves eth_getLogs over the whole auction span and add it to connect-src per HOSTING-HEADERS.md step 3; make rpc.js fail over on a JSON-RPC refusal of a log range; add a test with a node that answers -32602/403 and one that caps the span at 100 blocks; or feed the book from the contract's own counters instead of logs.

votes.reason: Confirmed end to end, including a fresh read-only probe today (head 26,166,637) against the exact hosts in site/chains/1.json:5-6. ethereum-rpc.publicnode.com: eth_getLogs with fromBlock 10,000 back -> `result [] [HTTP 200]`; 12,000 / 20,000 / 100,000 / 1,000,000 back (span 1, 78, 100 or 10,000) -> `{"error":{"code":-32602,"message":"Archive requests require a personal token..."}} [HTTP 403]`. eth.drpc.org: any age works but span 127, 128, 200 and 10,000 -> `{"error":{"message":"ranges over 10000 blocks are not supported on free plan","code":35}} [HTTP 400]`, spans 101, 100, 78 succeed (threshold is between 102 and 126, slightly below the finding's "128"; the halving still lands on 78). Code path: site/rpc.js:33 `if (res.status >= 500 || res.status === 429) {...e.transport = true...}` is the only transport branch, so 403/400 bodies parse as ordinary JSON-RPC answers; rpc.js:56 `if (res.error) throw RpcError(...)`; rpc.js:48 `catch (err) { last = err; if (!err.transport) throw err; }` never fails over to the second URL. rpc.js:152 `chunk = opts.chunk || 10000`, 162-165: -32602 counts as `tooMuch`, so on publicnode the loop issues 14 refused requests (10000 -> 1) and then `if (!tooMuch || chunk <= 1) throw err`. site/chain.js:339 `var first = cfg.deployBlock || 0;` and 356 `bFrom = Math.max(first, S.bidsTo ? S.bidsTo - REORG + 1 : first)`: with bidsTo still 0 every scan restarts at deployBlock; 305-308 retry scanLogs 3 times (42 requests without a wallet, 126 with one, matching the finding), 312 `S.stale = 'Can't reach ' + ... + ' right now. Retrying…'`; S.live (totals) was already set at 290-296 before the log loop, so totals show while the book stays empty; 220-226 `schedule()` repeats every `pollMs` = 12000 (line 79). site/auction.js:297 `enabled = !a.registered && ... && !s.stale && !placing;` disables Register whenever stale is set; line 290 (bidding) does not test stale; 371-372 render "No bids yet. Timing: publicnode's cutoff is ~10-12k blocks (~33-40 h) after deployment; the inspection window is at least 24 h (1-pre-deploy.md:102) and the auction has no fixed end, so the cutoff is crossed during registration or bidding regardless of the lead chosen. The only reason this is not Critical is that nothing on-chain is affected and rpcUrls plus the connect-src line (launch/HOSTING-HEADERS.md:20,38,90,113) can be changed after deployment; until then every fresh visitor sees an empty book and the stale note, and no wallet can register from the page.

votes.fix: Before launch: (1) replace or prepend in site/chains/1.json a read RPC that serves eth_getLogs over the full auction span at the deploy age (a keyed/archive-capable endpoint or one verified by an eth_getLogs probe like the one above, with the probe output filed in contracts/audit/), and add that host to connect-src in launch/HOSTING-HEADERS.md and the handed-over headers; (2) in site/rpc.js, let getLogsChunked (or send) move to the next URL when a JSON-RPC error is a log-range/archive refusal (code -32602 on fromBlock only, HTTP 403/400 bodies, drpc code 35) instead of only halving, and halve only when the smaller span can succeed; (3) add tests with a node that answers -32602/403 for any fromBlock older than N blocks and one that caps spans at ~100 blocks, asserting the book still fills and status().stale clears; (4) optionally decouple registration from the log scan (auction.js:297) since register needs only the eth_call reads that succeed.

findings.title: The mainnet KILIM_GRIDS gate is a byte-substring test on an unhashed manifest boolean; nothing proves the page uses the grids
findings.description: The chain-1 refusal `mainnet: the artwork does not read KILIM_GRIDS` (lines 322-326) reads `.artwork.readsGrids` from build-page/manifest.json. The packer sets that flag as `'readsGrids': GRIDS_GLOBAL in artwork` (onchain/pack_page.py:179, GRIDS_GLOBAL = b'KILIM_GRIDS' at line 57): a byte search, satisfied by a comment, a dead branch or a string literal. The flag is in no hash: `expected` pins the artwork's sha256 (lines 357-360), the five section hashes and the goldens, but the manifest file itself is unhashed and `runStore`/`runContracts` never run `check:stores`, so a manifest edited to `true` by hand passes both phases on chain 1 with every hash matching. The only test that opens the page, onchain/test/page.test.mjs lines 130-137, asserts that `KILIM_GRIDS` is defined with the right value in the document, which the loader guarantees for any artwork (loader.html writes the global itself); it never checks that the drawing came from it. onchain/ARTWORK-ONCHAIN.md:52 nevertheless calls that test 'Proof that the stored page is the artwork ... starts with the grids handed in', and contracts/README.md:27 says the script refuses 'an artwork that never reads KILIM_GRIDS'. docs/STORAGE.md:38 is the only place that says 'names it at all'.
findings.scenario: Actor: the art session fixing blocker #2 before the freeze. It adds `const G = window.KILIM_GRIDS || DATA` (or merely a comment naming KILIM_GRIDS) and keeps drawing from the inline DATA.symbols copy. pack_page.py writes readsGrids: true, `pnpm -s expected` pins that file, test:page passes, deploy:dry passes, runStore and runContracts on chain 1 pass. The 1/1 is deployed forever with the published claim 'provably draws the motifs the motif tokens show' being false, exactly the V-03 condition the gate was added to refuse.
findings.evidence: DeployKilim.s.sol:322-326 `if (block.chainid == MAINNET_CHAIN_ID && !(vm.keyExistsJson(pg, ".artwork.readsGrids") && vm.parseJsonBool(pg, ".artwork.readsGrids"))) revert Refused("mainnet: the artwork does not read KILIM_GRIDS");`. pack_page.py:176-179 `# readsGrids: whether the page names KILIM_GRIDS at all.` ... `'readsGrids': GRIDS_GLOBAL in artwork`. page.test.mjs:134-137 `assert.ok(grids.defined, 'KILIM_GRIDS is not defined in the artwork document'); ... assert.equal(store.grids.toString('hex'), await page.evaluate('KILIM_GRIDS'));` (the loader defines it, not the artwork). README.md:27 'and an artwork that never reads `KILIM_GRIDS`'. The `expected` block (lines 348-360) covers artwork/still/loader sha256 and the hashes, never manifest.json or the boolean. AUDIT.md:354 (V-03) records the fix as 'the deploy script refuses a page that does not read them'.
findings.fix: Make the proof differential instead of lexical: in page.test.mjs pack the same artwork twice (real grids vs. synthetic grids, as `packTemp` already can), open both, and assert the rendered canvas / a motif-derived DOM value differs, and that the real-grids run equals a run of the bare artwork file; keep the lexical flag only as a hint. Have the deploy script compare `keccak256(bytes(manifest.json))` or at least the boolean against a value carried in `expected` (so the manifest is pinned like the files), and reword README.md:27 and ARTWORK-ONCHAIN.md:52 to 'names KILIM_GRIDS' until the differential test exists.

votes.reason: Confirmed on every cited line. (1) The gate is lexical: /Users/orkhan/Documents/ChatGPT/kilim/onchain/pack_page.py:57 `GRIDS_GLOBAL = b'KILIM_GRIDS'`, :179 `'readsGrids': GRIDS_GLOBAL in artwork`, with the comment at :176 saying so ("whether the page names KILIM_GRIDS at all"). A comment, a string literal or `const G = window.KILIM_GRIDS || DATA` satisfies it. (2) The deploy script only reads that boolean: /Users/orkhan/Documents/ChatGPT/kilim/contracts/script/DeployKilim.s.sol:322-326 `if (block.chainid == MAINNET_CHAIN_ID && !(vm.keyExistsJson(pg, ".artwork.readsGrids") && vm.parseJsonBool(pg, ".artwork.readsGrids"))) revert Refused("mainnet: the artwork does not read KILIM_GRIDS");`. `_requireExpected` (:342-360) pins gridsHash, namesHash, prefixHash, headHash, tailHash, both goldens, motifSource, artwork, still and loader sha256, never the manifest or the boolean; the script has no access to the artwork text (it reads only manifests and chunk files, :290-291, :406-418), so it cannot recompute the flag. (3) The page test proves the loader, not the artwork: /Users/orkhan/Documents/ChatGPT/kilim/onchain/loader.html:1 writes `'<script>KILIM_GRIDS='+JSON.stringify(GRIDS)+'</'+'script>'` into any artwork; /Users/orkhan/Documents/ChatGPT/kilim/onchain/test/page.test.mjs:130-137 asserts only that `KILIM_GRIDS` is defined, is 65,536 lowercase hex chars and equals store.grids, which holds for an artwork that never touches it; the only other assertion is `#art[data-renderer]` being set (:122-128). The synthetic fixture /Users/orkhan/Documents/ChatGPT/kilim/onchain/test/fixtures/synthetic-artwork.html itself only regex-tests the global and draws fixed rectangles, so even the fixture does not model "drawing from the grids". The packer test /Users/orkhan/Documents/ChatGPT/kilim/onchain/test/test_pack.py:321-328 pins the lexical behaviour (it flips the flag by `artwork.replace(b'KILIM_GRIDS', b'SOMETHING_ELSE')`). (4) The scenario is concrete and made likelier by the project's own guidance: /Users/orkhan/Documents/ChatGPT/kilim/onchain/ARTWORK-ONCHAIN.md:22 tells the art session to keep "its own inline grids only as the fallback", i.e. exactly the `window.KILIM_GRIDS || DATA` shape; if the draw path keeps consuming DATA.symbols, the flag is true, test:page passes, deploy:dry passes, and runStore/runContracts on chain 1 pass with every hash matching. Because the inline copy and KILIM_GRIDS carry identical data for the real artwork, the artist's visual check (ARTWORK-ONCHAIN.md:53 "The artist looks at it too") cannot distinguish either; only a differential run with synthetic grids could. The 1/1 would then be deployed forever with README.md:20 "so the 1/1 provably draws the same motifs the motif tokens show" false, which is the V-03 condition the gate was added to refuse; V-03's fix column (/Users/orkhan/Documents/ChatGPT/kilim/contracts/AUDIT.md:354 "the deploy script refuses a page that does not read them") and /Users/orkhan/Documents/ChatGPT/kilim/contracts/README.md:27 ("an artwork that never reads `KILIM_GRIDS`") overstate it; /Users/orkhan/Documents/ChatGPT/kilim/contracts/docs/STORAGE.md:38 ("whether the page names it at all") is the accurate wording. Partial refutation of one sub-claim: the hand-edited-manifest angle is weak. `pnpm -s check:stores` (/Users/orkhan/Documents/ChatGPT/kilim/contracts/scripts/stores.mjs:21,39 passes `--check`; /Users/orkhan/Documents/ChatGPT/kilim/onchain/pack_page.py:242-244 compares `manifest['artwork']` including readsGrids against a fresh build) would catch an edited flag, and it is a by-hand step in /Users/orkhan/Documents/ChatGPT/kilim/contracts/checklists/2-deploy.md:33; also the only actor who could edit it is the artist forging his own manifest. The lexical-pass angle needs no forgery and nothing catches it. Severity stays Medium, consistent with V-03 whose recorded fix this shows to be incomplete; no funds are at risk, the harm is a permanently false provenance claim and an immutable deployment that would have been refused had the gate meant what the docs say.

findings.title: Deploy script and forge simulation are pinned to Cancun prices; on a Glamsterdam chain (Sepolia today, mainnet at an unset date) every chunk broadcast would be sent with ~7.8M gas against ~38M needed, and the three contracts' code deposit (15-17M state gas each) is absent from the plan
findings.description: foundry.toml:9 `evm_version = "cancun"` governs both the test EVM and the EVM forge uses to simulate `forge script` broadcasts; forge 1.7.1 (built 2026-05-08) contains no Glamsterdam gas schedule at all (the binary has 0 occurrences of "glamsterdam"; EIP-8037/8038 are still Last Call). `forge script` sets each broadcast's gas limit from its own simulation times `--gas-estimate-multiplier` (default 130%) unless `--skip-simulation` is given; the documented commands (checklists/2-deploy.md:17-22) pass neither. Under EIP-8037 code deposit is CPSB = 1,530 gas/byte of state gas plus 120 x 1,530 for the new account, and block validity is `gas_used = max(execution, state) <= block.gas_limit`; EIP-7825's 16,777,216 cap applies to execution gas only. A full chunk (24,575 data bytes + 0x00 = 24,576 code bytes) therefore needs 37,601,280 + 183,600 of state gas plus execution, where the script measures 'at most 5,992,449' (docs/STORAGE.md:96) and the 8M policy (DeployKilim.s.sol:78, :880, :913-:931) passes. Sepolia has run Glamsterdam since 2026-10-06 13:53 UTC (EIP-7773 activation table; the repo knows: checklists/1-pre-deploy.md:139, :212), yet checklists/2-deploy.md:12 says the Sepolia rehearsal 'uses the two phases exactly as mainnet does' with the same commands. The docs also scope the repricing to the store only (docs/STORAGE.md:103, checklists/1-pre-deploy.md:213 'Deploy the chunks before Glamsterdam'); the three contracts' runtime code (build-manifest: KilimAuction 11,216 B, KilimMotifs 10,891 B, KilimOneOfOne 9,981 B) would cost 17,160,480 / 16,663,230 / 15,270,930 state gas instead of 2.24M / 2.18M / 2.00M today, plus 97,920 instead of 20,000 per new storage slot (the 1/1 constructor stores about 46 chunk addresses), so the contracts phase also becomes a set of block-sized transactions and the `_measured` figures and `_intrinsic`'s 53,000 base (EIP-2780 makes intrinsic gas resource-based) describe nothing on that chain. The chunk layout cannot be re-cut cheaply: KilimMotifs.sol:21 fixes 767 grids per chunk in the contract, and a re-cut page changes every CREATE2 address.
findings.scenario: Actor: the artist runs the documented Sepolia rehearsal (`runStore()` with `--broadcast --slow`, no `--skip-simulation`, no `-g`) on Sepolia today. forge's Cancun simulation reports ~6.0M per chunk, the script logs 'under 8M', forge signs chunk 0 with a ~7.8M gas limit; on Sepolia-Glamsterdam the CREATE2 frame runs out of state gas at code deposit, the transaction fails, `--slow` stops the run after burning ~7.8M gas, and no chunk exists. The same happens on mainnet for the store, and for the three contracts, if Glamsterdam activates before the respective phase is sent; with `--resume` or a higher multiplier set blindly, 46 transactions of ~38M each are what the store actually costs.

[default: 130]`, `--skip-simulation  Skips on-chain simulation`. EIP-8037 (fetched 2026-10-10, status Last Call, deadline 2026-11-01): `| CPSB | 1530 |`, `| STATE_BYTES_PER_NEW_ACCOUNT | 120 |`, `| TX_MAX_TOTAL_GAS_LIMIT | 4,294,967,295 (2^32 - 1) |`, `the transaction gas limit set in EIP-7825 only applies to execution-gas`, `gas_used = max(block_output.block_execution_gas_used, block_output.block_state_gas_used)`. findings.title: No public build can bid: the orkhanart target composes a read-only auction page with a hard-coded 'Coming soon' button, the only bidding UI is dev-only, the build gate refuses live configs, and three documents tell the operator the opposite
findings.description:
Two independent blocks stand between site-config and a page that can send a bid. (1) build.py 273-274 fails every non-dev build whose chain config has addresses (`fail('Native ETH migration is pending; public builds must remain previews with no deployed addresses.')`), and site/test/orkhanart.test.mjs 95-106 pins that refusal ('public builds reject deployed legacy contracts until native ETH migration'), so lifting the gate also means editing a test. (2) Even with the gate gone, build.py 341 and 347 compose the public auction page from `auction-info.part.html` and the 8-line `auction-info.js`: that page has `` (part line 28), `
Coming soon. The date will be announced.
` (19), 'The reserve, rounding, allocation limits and claim and refund timing will be published before bidding opens.' (35) and the footer 'Kilim · date to be announced' (37), all static; auction-info.js only draws the 1,024 motifs and never reads CHAIN. chain.js 1115 still creates CHAIN and runs init() against the live contracts, whose result nothing renders. The working bidding page (`auction.part.html` + `auction.js`, 215 + 403 lines, with register, bid, claim, settle, withdraw) is used only under `--dev` (build.py 341, 347), and `--dev` with `--target orkhanart` is refused (254-255). The chosen landing's own auction page (landing-departure/auction.html) has no chain adapter either (landing-departure/README.md: 'the live state is in the markup ... filled from a typed view the chain adapter (site/chain.js) will provide'). Meanwhile README.md 17 claims 'Setting the addresses (pnpm site-config) and rebuilding turns the same pages into the live auction', site-config.mjs 105-106 prints 'Next: python3 site/build.py, then publish site/index.html and auction.html ... pnpm site:sync-orkhanart', and checklists/3-post-deploy.md 21 says 'then rebuild with site/build.py and deploy': each of those commands fails at build.py 274 on launch day. No checklist item says to lift the gate or to swap the auction page; the site review's finding 5 ('lift the gate in its own reviewed commit ... run the site tests on the live build') is not in any checklist. The live auction page is tested only as the dev build on anvil (site/test/pages.test.mjs 176-186, `build(['--dev', ...])`).
findings.scenario: Operator runs `pnpm -s site-config --chain 1 --auction ... --tx ...` (succeeds, writes 1.json), then `python3 site/build.py` or `pnpm site:sync-orkhanart` as instructed: both exit 1 with 'Native ETH migration is pending'. Under time pressure the gate line is deleted; the build then passes and the sync ships an auction page whose only button says 'Coming soon' and is disabled, whose note says the date will be announced, while the landing shows the real opening date from startsAt (landing-chain.js). No visitor can register, bid, claim, settle or withdraw from orkhan.art/kilim/auction; the first bid has to be sent by hand through an explorer. Swapping build.py 341/347 to the dev page is mechanically small (auction.part.html and auction.js carry no dev-only identifiers) but has never been built or tested for the public target, so copy, links and the FORBIDDEN list are unverified on the page that would actually take bids.

README.md 17: 'Setting the addresses (`pnpm site-config`) and rebuilding turns the same pages into the live auction.' 3-post-deploy.md 21: '...then rebuild with `site/build.py` and deploy.' orkhanart.test.mjs 104: `assert.match(r.stderr, /Native ETH migration is pending/);`. Lines 72-73 only say to drop XFO 'if it breaks a page of orkhan.art that is meant to be framed', contradicting line 22 in the same document.
findings.scenario: Launch day, two possible outcomes. findings.title: The kill switch (writesDisabled/notice) is a rebuild-and-republish across two repos and an unknown deploy pipeline, is blocked today by the build gate, never reaches tabs already open, and has no end-to-end test; the checklists call it tested and minutes-fast
findings.description: The operator levers live only in the page: build.py embeds the chain config as `var KILIM_CHAINS = ...` (config_js 160-164, CHAIN_BUNDLE 337) and chain.js reads `cfg.writesDisabled` / `cfg.notice` from that embedded copy at create() (74, 511), never from the network. Flipping it therefore means: edit site/chains/1.json, run build.py --target orkhanart (which today refuses any live config at 273-274, so the switch cannot even be built while the auction is live until W-02 is fixed), run sync_orkhanart.py into a local branch of the orkhan.art repo (which 'never deploys', sync docstring 11-13), commit, push, and have the Hetzner Next.js host rebuild or redeploy, a pipeline this repo does not describe and whose checkout is not reachable from here. A visitor with the auction page already open keeps bidding on the old embedded config until they reload; nothing polls for a new config. The only test is the adapter refusing writes when a config object says writesDisabled (site/test/chain.test.mjs 511-520). 3-post-deploy.md 29 ('Test the kill switch: disable the buttons, post a banner, then restore') and 1-pre-deploy.md 197 ('a tested way to switch off the site's bid button and post a banner within minutes') describe a capability that has not been exercised through the publish path and whose latency nobody has measured; HOSTING-HEADERS.md gives no Cache-Control guidance for /kilim, so a proxy cache in front of Next.js could keep serving the old page after the deploy.
findings.scenario: Mid-auction incident (the balance alert of 3-post-deploy.md 35 fires). The on-call person edits 1.json, runs the build: refused by the gate (or, after the gate is lifted, succeeds), syncs, commits, pushes, then waits for someone with access to the orkhan.art host to deploy. Visitors who already have the page open keep seeing an enabled bid button and keep sending bids; new visitors see the banner only after the deploy lands and any proxy cache expires. The 'within minutes' promise is not met and no rehearsal has shown how long it takes.

JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(raw)) : null;`; 511: `if (cfg.writesDisabled) throw KilimError('WritesDisabled', cfg.notice || 'Transactions are paused on this site for now.');`. sync_orkhanart.py 12-13: 'It never runs git add, commit, checkout, merge or push, never builds or starts the Next.js app, and never deploys anything.' README.md 49: '`notice`, `writesDisabled` and `void` are the operator levers (banner, kill switch, refuse an address): edit, rebuild, republish.' 3-post-deploy.md 29: '- [ ] Test the kill switch: disable the buttons, post a banner, then restore. It stops the site, not the auction.' 1-pre-deploy.md 197: 'a tested way to switch off the site's bid button and post a banner within minutes'. chain.test.mjs 511: `const paused = make({ writesDisabled: true, notice: 'Paused for maintenance.' });`.

findings.title: Bid page checks balance against the bid only, while its fixed 1,500,000 gas limit makes wallets require bid + 1.5M x maxFee up front; contradicts checklist 1-pre-deploy line 150
findings.description: The contract's refund gas floor (EnglishAuction.sol line 243: `if (gasleft() < REFUND_GAS + REFUND_GAS / 63 + DEFERRED_REFUND_RESERVE) revert InsufficientGas();`, i.e. 452,380 at the refund) led the site to send every bid with a fixed limit (site/chain.js line 18: `var BID_GAS = 1500000n, SETTLE_GAS = 1200000n;`, used at line 705 `gas: BID_GAS`). A node or wallet refuses to sign/broadcast a transaction unless the account holds value + gasLimit x maxFeePerGas, so a bidder must hold the bid plus 1.5M x maxFee even though only ~250k (first bid) to ~545k (outbidding bid) is charged. The page's pre-flight check at line 701 compares the balance to the amount alone: `if (q.balance < q.amount) throw KilimError('InsufficientEth', 'The bid needs ' + fmtEth(q.amount) + ' plus gas.');`. checklists/1-pre-deploy.md line 150 requires the opposite: 'Check the wallet's ETH balance against the full new bid plus gas'. The registration copy (chain.js line 954, 3-post-deploy.md line 53) tells supporters to hold 0.01 ETH, which is far below what the fixed limit needs. No ETH or token is at risk; the contract is unaffected. It is reported because the launch audience (supporters holding about 0.01 ETH, the only balance the gate asks for) cannot place the 0.01 ETH opening bid through the page at ordinary fee levels, and the page's own check will not tell them why.
findings.scenario: Actor: a supporter who registered holding 0.015 ETH. State: registrationCount == 100, no bid yet, base fee 20 gwei (wallet maxFeePerGas about 25 gwei). The supporter asks the page to bid the 0.01 ETH reserve. chain.js line 701 passes (0.015 >= 0.01). The page builds the transaction with gas 1,500,000 (line 705), so the wallet/node requires 0.01 + 1,500,000 x 25 gwei = 0.0475 ETH and rejects it ('insufficient funds for gas * price + value') before signing. Actual execution would have cost about 250,000 gas (AuditGaps.t.sol line 285 sends a first bid with 250,000) = 0.00625 ETH. Outcome: the bid is never sent, with no contract error to decode; the same wallet would have succeeded with a 300,000 limit for a first bid.
findings.evidence: site/chain.js line 18: `var BID_GAS = 1500000n, SETTLE_GAS = 1200000n;`; line 701: `if (q.balance < q.amount) throw KilimError('InsufficientEth', 'The bid needs ' + fmtEth(q.amount) + ' plus gas.');`; line 705: `return { calls: [{ label: 'Bid ' + fmtEth(q.amount), to: cfg.auction, value: q.amount, gas: BID_GAS,`. contracts/checklists/1-pre-deploy.md line 150: 'a fixed gas limit of 1,500,000 (R-08; an outbidding bid needs about 545,000 as a transaction) rather than a bare estimate. Check the wallet's ETH balance against the full new bid plus gas'. contracts/checklists/3-post-deploy.md line 53: 'the wallet only has to hold 0.01 ETH at that moment'. contracts/src/auction/EnglishAuction.sol line 243 (the floor the limit exists for). Reasoning: Ethereum nodes enforce balance >= value + gasLimit x gasFeeCap at admission (go-ethereum txpool 'insufficient funds for gas * price + value'); the page's check omits the gas term, so the contradiction with the checklist is live code, not a doc nit.
findings.fix: In site/chain.js plan(): read the current fee (eth_gasPrice / baseFeePerGas, already fetched for claims at lines 809-816) and require q.balance >= q.amount + BID_GAS x maxFee, naming the ETH to hold in the error; or use a two-tier limit (about 300,000 when highestBidder() == address(0), 1,500,000 otherwise; the InsufficientGas path at line 959 already tells a bidder to resend if a leader appears in between). Update the supporter copy (chain.js line 954, checklists 3-post-deploy.md line 53) to state the balance the fixed limit needs at a typical fee. Add a site test that a balance equal to the bid is refused with the gas term named.

findings.title: Runbook and script natspec say a reverted third creation is recoverable with runAuction(); a mined-but-reverted (or replaced) creation consumes nonce n+2, runAuction() refuses, and both token contracts are permanently without a minter
findings.description: checklists/2-deploy.md line 52 and the natspec of DeployKilim.deployAuction (script/DeployKilim.s.sol line 481) both state that if the third creation (KilimAuction) was "lost (dropped, replaced or reverted)" then "nothing is void" and `runAuction()` completes the deployment at nonce n+2. That is true only for a creation that was never mined. An Ethereum transaction that is mined and reverts still increments the sender's nonce, and so does a mined replacement at the same nonce. After either, the deployer sits at n+3; deployAuction's own guard (line 497: `if (nonce != c.deployerNonce + 2) revert Refused("deployer nonce is not the published one plus two");`) refuses, and the address both tokens hold as `minter` (computeCreateAddress(deployer, n+2)) can never receive code from this deployer. KilimMotifs (3,210,743 gas) and KilimOneOfOne (6,750,528 gas) then have a minter that will never exist: `mintMotifs` and `mint` revert with `Unauthorized` forever, exactly the state test/review/PrizeGasBudget.t.sol lines 485-498 demonstrate for a consumed n+2 ("tokens built for a slipped nonce can never mint; both must be redeployed"). The published addresses and the motif layout (`motifOf` depends on the KilimMotifs address) are void, the same outcome the checklist reserves for a lost first or second creation (lines 53-56). The only inclusion-time revert in a correctly simulated KilimAuction constructor is EnglishAuction.sol line 99 `config.startsAt <= block.timestamp` (every other clause, including the minter/motifs binding at KilimAuction.sol lines 80-83, is deterministic given the config and the already-deployed tokens), plus an out-of-gas creation. The runbook accepts any nonzero `minLeadSeconds` on chain 1 (line 41: "the script accepts any nonzero value"), so a short inspection window with a Ledger-signed third transaction that waits in the pool past `startsAt` is the plausible path to a mined revert. The regression test `testCompletesADeploymentWhoseThirdCreationWasLost` (test/DeployKilim.t.sol line 378, `assertEq(vmd.getNonce(DEPLOYER), n + 2);`) covers only the dropped case; no test exercises the reverted or replaced case, and the refusal message the operator would meet is not mentioned in the runbook.
findings.scenario: Actor: the artist deploying on chain 1 with a small inspection window (e.g. minLeadSeconds 600, startsAt 15 minutes out). State: KilimMotifs and KilimOneOfOne mined at nonces n and n+1 with minter = address(n+2); the KilimAuction creation is signed with a fee that leaves it in the pool past startsAt, then mined and reverted with InvalidConfiguration (EnglishAuction.sol line 99). Outcome: the deployer is at n+3; following checklist line 52 the operator runs `--sig 'runAuction()'`, which refuses with "deployer nonce is not the published one plus two"; no command can put code at address(n+2); both token contracts are dead on mainnet under the names Motif Bazaar and The Unwoven Kilim, and the full first-or-second-lost restart (new nonce, new layout, new inspection window, ~10M gas of token deployments) is required, contrary to the runbook's "nothing is void".
findings.evidence: checklists/2-deploy.md:52: "**If only the third (the auction) was lost** (dropped, replaced or reverted) and the first two are mined: nothing is void. The two token contracts name the address at nonce n + 2 as their minter, and the auction can still be deployed there. ... run the same command with `--sig 'runAuction()'`: it requires the deployer at n + 2". script/DeployKilim.s.sol:481-485: "/// @notice Completes a deployment whose third creation was lost (dropped, replaced or reverted) ... Needs the published nonce n in the config, the deployer at n + 2". script/DeployKilim.s.sol:496-497: `uint256 nonce = vm.getNonce(c.deployer); if (nonce != c.deployerNonce + 2) revert Refused("deployer nonce is not the published one plus two");`. src/auction/EnglishAuction.sol:97-103: `if (config.treasury == address(0) || config.treasury == address(this) || config.startsAt <= block.timestamp || config.duration > 30 days ... ) revert InvalidConfiguration();`. src/KilimAuction.sol:80-83: `if (motifs_.minter() != address(this) || oneOfOne_.minter() != address(this) || address(oneOfOne_.motifs()) != config.motifs) revert InvalidConfiguration();` (the tokens bind to the address, which is fixed by the nonce). test/review/PrizeGasBudget.t.sol:489-498: `vmp.setNonce(address(this), uint64(vm.getNonce(address(this)) + 1)); vm.expectRevert(...); new KilimAuction(c); address minter = KilimMotifs(c.motifs).minter(); assertEq(minter.code.length, 0); ... emit log_string("(a) tokens built for a slipped nonce can never mint; both must be redeployed, the chunks survive");`. test/DeployKilim.t.sol:377-378: `(KilimMotifs k, KilimOneOfOne o) = _deployTwoTokens(c); assertEq(vmd.getNonce(DEPLOYER), n + 2);` (only the never-mined case). checklists/2-deploy.md:41: "On chain 1, `minLeadSeconds` must be nonzero. **By hand:** it is the window that was announced; the script accepts any nonzero value." Reasoning: the EVM increments the sender's nonce for every included transaction, successful or reverted, and a replacement transaction at the same nonce is also included; only a transaction that never enters a block leaves the deployer at n+2.
findings.fix: Reword checklists/2-deploy.md line 52 and the deployAuction natspec to say the completion path exists only for a third creation that was never mined (dropped from the pool, deployer still at n+2); state explicitly that a mined-but-reverted or a mined replacement at n+2 voids both tokens exactly like a lost first creation and belongs to the lines 53-56 procedure. Add a test in test/DeployKilim.t.sol that advances the deployer to n+3 after the two tokens (a reverted or any other mined transaction) and asserts `deployAuction` refuses with "deployer nonce is not the published one plus two" and that `KilimMotifs(k).minter().code.length == 0`. Operationally: set `minLeadSeconds` on mainnet to hours, not minutes, and have the script refuse chain 1 when `startsAt - block.timestamp` is below a fixed margin (for example 1 hour) so a pool delay cannot reach the constructor's `startsAt <= block.timestamp` clause; add a by-hand line to re-check `startsAt` against the current time right before signing the third transaction.

findings.title: deliverPrizeToWinner lets any third party preempt the winner's claimPrize(to); the stuck-token outcome is neither tested nor disclosed
findings.description: `deliverPrizeToWinner()` (KilimAuction.sol:229-236) is permissionless and runs whenever `settled && !prizeClaimed`; it mints to `highestBidder` and sets `prizeClaimed`, after which the winner's `claimPrize(to)` reverts `PrizeAlreadyClaimed` (L217). The only test of the ordering, GasFloors.t.sol:199-223, documents preemption as a side note (`// The winner's own claim is spent with it.` L221-222: `assertTrue(!winner.run(abi.encodeCall(auction.claimPrize, (ALICE))))`) and uses a `ProbeWallet` that can call out. No test covers the harmful shape: a winning contract whose hook failed at settle on gas (not on a revert), that accepts ERC-721 when given more gas, and that has no path to transfer the token on. For such a winner the intended remedy is `claimPrize(to)` to an address that can hold it; any observer who sees `PrizeDeliveryFailed` can front-run that with `deliverPrizeToWinner()` and lock the 1/1 inside the winner's contract for good. docs/NATIVE-ETH.md:103, README.md:90 and checklists/3-post-deploy.md:82 describe the function as a rescue only and never say it removes the winner's choice of recipient. V-15 in AUDIT.md:185 records the rescue, not the race. Under the projected Glamsterdam prices (AUDIT.md:228: a hook writing one new slot no longer fits in 500,000) the failing-on-gas shape becomes common, so the window in which the race matters widens to any receipt-logging contract that cannot forward tokens.
findings.scenario: Actor: any address (cost: one transaction). State: the winner is a contract whose onERC721Received writes a storage slot (fails at settle under the 500,000 allowance after the repricing, succeeds with more gas) and exposes no ERC-721 transfer; settlement emitted PrizeDeliveryFailed; the winner prepares `claimPrize(coldWallet)`. Outcome: the third party calls `deliverPrizeToWinner()` first, the 1/1 is minted into the winner's contract and can never leave it; the winner's `claimPrize` reverts PrizeAlreadyClaimed; nothing can be changed after deployment.
findings.evidence: KilimAuction.sol:229-236: `function deliverPrizeToWinner() external nonReentrant { if (!settled) revert NotSettled(); if (prizeClaimed) revert PrizeAlreadyClaimed(); address winner = highestBidder; prizeClaimed = true; oneOfOne.mint(winner); ... }` — no caller restriction, no winner opt-in, no delay after PrizeDeliveryFailed. GasFloors.t.sol:216-222: `vm.prank(BOB); auction.deliverPrizeToWinner(); ... // The winner's own claim is spent with it. assertTrue(!winner.run(abi.encodeCall(auction.claimPrize, (ALICE))));` is the only place the preemption appears, with a wallet that could have claimed itself. docs/NATIVE-ETH.md:103: `anyone can also call deliverPrizeToWinner(): it sends the 1/1 to the winner's own address with the gas the caller gives` — no mention that it forecloses claimPrize(to).
findings.fix: Decide and test. Either (a) disclose the race in NATIVE-ETH.md/README/checklists and add a test in GasFloors.t.sol with a receiver that accepts but cannot transfer, showing the 1/1 stuck after a third-party `deliverPrizeToWinner()` (so the property is at least pinned and the artist has accepted it), or (b) restrict `deliverPrizeToWinner()` to `msg.sender == highestBidder` or to callers after a grace period following settlement, and add the negative test `vm.prank(CAROL); vm.expectRevert(Unauthorized.selector); auction.deliverPrizeToWinner();` plus the existing positive tests re-run from the winner. Memory rule: take the secure option.

For the preemption to hurt, the winner must be a contract that (1) accepts ERC-721 in onERC721Received when given more gas, (2) can call auction.claimPrize(to) with a chosen recipient, and (3) has no way to move the token on. (2) and (3) contradict each other for every real wallet class: a Safe, an ERC-4337 account or any contract with an execute/arbitrary-call path that can issue claimPrize(coldWallet) can equally issue oneOfOne.transferFrom(self, coldWallet, 1) (KilimOneOfOne.sol:436-438 only refuses the 1/1 itself, the minter and the motif contract as recipients, so a transfer out to a cold wallet is allowed). The only contract fitting all three is a purpose-built bidder with a hardcoded claimPrize passthrough and no transfer function, i.e. the bidder's own wallet-design error, the class already disclosed as F-19 (AUDIT.md:79) and in checklists/1-pre-deploy.md:190 ("Bid only from a wallet that can send transactions later ... The 1/1 is the exception since the review round: ... anyone can send it again with deliverPrizeToWinner()"). Even then the outcome is the token at the address the winner chose to bid from, which is the documented design: KilimAuction.sol:223-228 ("It goes to the winner's own address and nowhere else ... A winning contract whose receiver needs more, and that cannot call claimPrize itself, would otherwise never get the 1/1"), NATIVE-ETH.md:103, README.md:90, 3-post-deploy.md:82. findings.title: _measured is not the transaction's gas: it adds script-frame memory expansion and double-counts CREATE intrinsics (over), and measures warm chunk accounts (under); the policy can refuse a transaction that fits
findings.description: `_deployThree` times `new KilimOneOfOne(...)` with `gasleft()` inside the script frame (lines 588-598) and `_measured` adds `_intrinsic(creationCode ‖ args)` = 53,000 + 2·words + calldata (lines 676-683, 928-934). Three distortions: (1) Solidity's `new` copies ~12 KB of creation code plus the ABI-encoded Page struct into the script frame's memory, which at that point already holds the whole store (loadStore reads 1.21 MB of chunks, `_concat` copies them again, the dry run of the store copied them a third time), so the quadratic memory term alone adds hundreds of thousands of gas that a real creation transaction never pays; (2) the CREATE opcode inside the measured region already charges 32,000 and the EIP-3860 2/word, which `_intrinsic` charges again; (3) every chunk address was touched by `loadStore` (`a.code.length`, `keccak256(a.code)`, lines 395-397) so the constructor's 51 extcodecopy/extcodesize reads are warm (100) where a mainnet tx finds them cold (2,600): about 127,500 under-counted for the 1/1, 7,500 for the motifs, plus the cold token reads in the auction's constructor. AUDIT.md:418 records the net effect from the one live anvil run: KilimOneOfOne 6,276,216 on anvil versus 6,750,528 reported by the dry run (+7.6%), KilimAuction 2,929,640 versus 3,396,594 (+15.9%), 'and is the figure the 8M policy is checked against'. For the chunk path `_create2` (lines 913-926) the same `_intrinsic` is used with `- 32_000`, leaving 2·words of EIP-3860 that a call transaction does not pay (about 1,538 gas over per chunk; harmless). The tokenURI read gas (`_readGas`, lines 761-769) is likewise measured with every chunk warm, so the published 4,625,534 is about 130,000 below a marketplace's cold eth_call. Checklist 2-deploy.md:43 says the broadcast gas limit 'comes from Ethereum's own estimate plus margin'; for Ethereum mainnet forge takes it from its own per-transaction re-simulation times 1.3 (eth_estimateGas is used only for chains flagged with a different gas calculation), which is faithful per transaction but is not what the policy compares.
findings.scenario: Actor: the operator on deploy day with a store whose true 1/1 creation costs 7.6M-7.9M on chain. The dry run reports ~8.1-8.5M (today's 8,087,087 on the 283 KB still, which by the anvil ratio is ~7.5M on chain) and `_gasPolicy` reverts `KilimOneOfOne deployment gas`: a refusal on a number the chain would not charge. The inverse cannot send anything above the real 16,777,216 cap today, but a store tuned to pass at 7.99M in the dry run would read ~130,000 gas higher on a cold mainnet eth_call than the published figure.
findings.evidence: DeployKilim.s.sol:588-598 `g = gasleft(); d.oneOfOne = new KilimOneOfOne(minter, c.auction.treasury, d.motifs, _page(s), ...); g -= gasleft();` then line 600-605 `_measured(g, type(KilimOneOfOne).creationCode, _oneOfOneArgs(...), "KilimOneOfOne deployment gas")`; 680 `uint256 g = executionGas + _intrinsic(bytes.concat(creationCode, args));`; 930 `g = 53_000 + 2 * ((data.length + 31) / 32);`. Warm state: 395 `if (a.code.length != 0 && keccak256(a.code) != keccak256(bytes.concat(hex"00", data)))` runs for every chunk before any measurement, and the snapshot/revert (464-471) does not reset the access list of the simulation. AUDIT.md:418 'Measured there: KilimMotifs 3,210,743, KilimOneOfOne 6,276,216, KilimAuction 2,929,640 (the in-memory dry run reports the last two higher, 6,750,528 and 3,396,594, and is the figure the 8M policy is checked against).'
findings.fix: Measure each creation from a fresh frame: a tiny helper contract `Deployer.create(bytes initcode)` deployed in the snapshot, called with the creation data, so memory starts empty; count the transaction intrinsic once (21,000 + calldata, with 32,000 + 2·words already inside the measured CREATE); add 2,500 per distinct chunk/contract address the constructor touches (or run the dry run in a fresh `vm.snapshotState` after `vm.cool`-style resets if the forge version offers them). Apply the same cold allowance to `_readGas`, and reword 2-deploy.md:43 (forge's own re-simulation times 1.3, not eth_estimateGas). Record in STORAGE.md that the policy figure is an over-estimate of the 1/1 creation by about 7% and an under-estimate of cold reads by about 130,000.

findings.title: 'Lost third transaction' guidance is wrong in both directions: a reverted or replaced third creation cannot be completed, and a dropped first or second does not spend the nonce
findings.description: The doc comment on deployAuction (481-485), checklists/2-deploy.md:51 and README.md:27 say runAuction completes a deployment whose third creation was 'lost (dropped, replaced or reverted)' and that then 'nothing is void'. Only a dropped (never mined) transaction leaves the deployer at n+2. A reverted creation and a replacement with other content both consume nonce n+2 (the deployer is then at n+3) and the address the two tokens name as `minter` can never receive code from this deployer; the script correctly refuses (line 497 `nonce != c.deployerNonce + 2` → 'deployer nonce is not the published one plus two', and test/review/PrizeGasBudget.t.sol:485-498 shows the tokens are then unmintable), so the two live mainnet contracts named Motif Bazaar and The Unwoven Kilim are void after all, while the checklist tells the operator the opposite and gives no procedure for that case. Conversely 2-deploy.md:53 says 'If the first or the second was lost: the published nonce is spent, and with it the addresses and the motif layout'; for a dropped first or second creation the nonce is not spent, the published addresses are still reachable, and the right action is a fresh `runContracts` run (which passes: latest == pending == n). The `--resume` paragraph (2-deploy.md:25, 'a transaction that was dropped from the pool has to be removed from that file before it is sent again') is written for the idempotent store phase but sits under both commands; applied to the contracts phase it would try to send n+1 with n unspent (forge's sequential nonce check then errors out, so nothing wrong is sent, but the operator is misdirected on the day).
findings.scenario: Actor: the operator after `runContracts` with --slow. Case A: the third creation is mined and reverts (gas limit too low from a stale estimate, or a node hiccup), nonce n+3. The operator follows 2-deploy.md:51, runs runAuction, is refused 'deployer nonce is not the published one plus two', and has no written procedure; the two token contracts stay live on mainnet with a dead minter and the checklist still says 'nothing is void'. Case B: the first creation is dropped from the pool (never mined), nonce still n. The operator follows 2-deploy.md:53, publishes a new nonce and new addresses and restarts the inspection window unnecessarily, or edits the broadcast file per line 25 and gets a forge nonce error.
findings.evidence: DeployKilim.s.sol:481-482 `/// @notice Completes a deployment whose third creation was lost (dropped, replaced or reverted) after the first two succeeded.`; 497 `if (nonce != c.deployerNonce + 2) revert Refused("deployer nonce is not the published one plus two");`. 2-deploy.md:51 '**If only the third (the auction) was lost** (dropped, replaced or reverted) and the first two are mined: nothing is void.' 2-deploy.md:53 '**If the first or the second was lost:** the published nonce is spent'. 2-deploy.md:25 'a transaction that was dropped from the pool has to be removed from that file before it is sent again.' PrizeGasBudget.t.sol:486-487 '(a) A plain transaction from the deployer uses nonce n+2: the auction lands at n+3 and refuses; the tokens name an address that can never get code by CREATE from this deployer.'
findings.fix: Reword the three places: runAuction completes only a *dropped* (never mined) third creation; a reverted or replaced third creation consumes n+2 and voids both tokens, handle it under 'If anything is wrong' (mark the two addresses void, republish). Add: a dropped first or second creation leaves the published nonce intact, rerun `runContracts` without --resume after confirming on an explorer that nothing from the wallet is queued. Move the --resume/dropped-transaction paragraph under the store command only, and state that the contracts phase is never resumed after removing a transaction from the broadcast file.

votes.reason: Confirmed on both directions; the finding is documentation-only and nothing wrong can be sent, so Low stands. (1) Reverted/replaced third creation: every mined transaction increments the sender's nonce whether or not it reverts, so after a reverted or differently-replaced third creation the deployer sits at n+3. /Users/orkhan/Documents/ChatGPT/kilim/contracts/script/DeployKilim.s.sol:497 `if (nonce != c.deployerNonce + 2) revert Refused("deployer nonce is not the published one plus two");` then refuses runAuction, and no CREATE from this deployer can ever land at n+2, so the two tokens' immutable `minter` is dead (test/review/PrizeGasBudget.t.sol:485-498 pins exactly this: `assertEq(minter.code.length, 0)` and both mints revert `Unauthorized`). Yet DeployKilim.s.sol:481-482 says "lost (dropped, replaced or reverted)" and checklists/2-deploy.md:52 says "**If only the third (the auction) was lost** (dropped, replaced or reverted) and the first two are mined: nothing is void." The checklist even contradicts itself: 2-deploy.md:25 acknowledges that reverted creations are "spent" ("the other two are still spent on creations that revert"). Only the dropped (never mined) case is completable, which is the only case the V-07 tests model (test/DeployKilim.t.sol:368-391 sets the deployer to exactly n+2 via `_deployTwoTokens`, never n+3). The operator in the reverted case is sent to runAuction, refused, and has no written path; the correct path is the "If anything is wrong" section (2-deploy.md:86-93), but the two orphaned tokens there are harmless (nothing can mint, no auction takes bids), so no funds are at risk. (2) Dropped first or second creation: 2-deploy.md:53 "the published nonce is spent" is false for a never-mined transaction; `vm.getNonce` still returns n and `_requireNothingPending` (DeployKilim.s.sol:450-456, 530-532) passes once the pool is empty, so a fresh `runContracts` without --resume is the right action and the checklist instead orders a republish and a restarted inspection window (unnecessary but not unsafe). (3) The --resume paragraph at 2-deploy.md:25 ("a transaction that was dropped from the pool has to be removed from that file before it is sent again") sits above both commands; applied to the contracts phase it would have forge send n+1 while the chain is at n, which forge's nonce check rejects, so misdirection only. Minor citation slip in the finding: the "If only the third" item is 2-deploy.md:52, not 51. AUDIT.md:418 already notes `runAuction()` and `--resume` have never been run live, which is consistent with the gap.

votes.reason: The code is correct and the documentation is wrong in both directions, as the finding says. (1) /Users/orkhan/Documents/ChatGPT/kilim/contracts/script/DeployKilim.s.sol:481-482 "/// @notice Completes a deployment whose third creation was lost (dropped, replaced or reverted)" and checklists/2-deploy.md:52 "**If only the third (the auction) was lost** (dropped, replaced or reverted) and the first two are mined: nothing is void." But DeployKilim.s.sol:496-497 `uint256 nonce = vm.getNonce(c.deployer); if (nonce != c.deployerNonce + 2) revert Refused("deployer nonce is not the published one plus two");` runs before the code check at line 505. A reverted creation, or a replacement (cancel) at nonce n+2, consumes the nonce; the deployer is at n+3; the CREATE address for (deployer, n+2) can never receive code; runAuction refuses. DeployKilim.t.sol:402-404 shows exactly this refusal at n+3, and PrizeGasBudget.t.sol:486-493 shows that in that state `KilimMotifs(c.motifs).minter()` has no code and both `mintMotifs` and `mint` revert Unauthorized, with the test's own log at 494: "tokens built for a slipped nonce can never mint; both must be redeployed, the chunks survive". So after a reverted or replaced third creation the two live token contracts are void, contrary to "nothing is void", and 2-deploy.md gives no procedure for that case (only line 53 for first/second, and the generic "If anything is wrong" does not exist in this section). Only the dropped (never mined) third is completable, which is what the test at 368-400 pins. (2) 2-deploy.md:53 "**If the first or the second was lost:** the published nonce is spent" is wrong for a dropped (never mined) first creation: the nonce stays n, and deployContracts (DeployKilim.s.sol:450-459) passes when latest == published == pending, so a plain rerun of runContracts without --resume is the right action; republishing nonce/addresses and restarting the inspection window is unnecessary. For a reverted first creation the line is right. (3) 2-deploy.md:25 "a transaction that was dropped from the pool has to be removed from that file before it is sent again" is phrased for the idempotent store phase but sits above both commands; for the contracts phase removing the dropped creation from the broadcast file and resuming would attempt n+1 before n and skips the script's simulation and refusal checks (pending-nonce check at line 457 does not run under --resume). The forge-side nonce error that stops it is not verifiable read-only here; the misdirection is. README.md:27 "`runAuction()` completes a deployment whose third transaction was lost" and docs/STORAGE.md:89 repeat the over-broad claim without "(dropped, replaced or reverted)", so they are imprecise rather than wrong. Severity Low: the script refuses in every wrong case so nothing incorrect is sent; the harm is a false "nothing is void" statement and a missing procedure on deploy day, and a reverted creation under --slow with forge's estimate-plus-margin gas limit is unlikely. Fix as the finding proposes: restrict the three "lost" statements to a dropped (never mined) third creation; add the reverted/replaced-third case (deployer at n+3: both tokens void, mark the two addresses void, republish nonce and addresses, restart the window); add the dropped-first-or-second case (nonce intact: confirm nothing queued on an explorer, rerun runContracts without --resume); move the --resume/dropped paragraph under the store command and state the contracts phase is never resumed from an edited broadcast file. AUDIT.md V-07's remediation column should then say "completes a dropped third creation".

findings.title: pack_page --check's 'another zlib' path accepts a store with a missing or stale animation.html, stray chunk files or stale informational golden fields, and says so with a false message on the same zlib
findings.description: main() takes the lenient `same_store_other_zlib` path whenever `check_outputs` reports any problem at all, not only when the deflate stream differs or the recorded zlib version differs. `same_store_other_zlib` compares prefix.bin, head.bin, the tail's loader-with-placeholder and decompressed artwork, the tail chunks, tailHash, golden.tokenURI and a fixed key list, but never `animation.html`, stray files under `chunks/`, or `golden.animationUrl`, `golden.page` and `blob`. So on the same machine (same zlib, same tail) a store whose `animation.html` is missing, stale or hand-edited, or whose `chunks/` holds leftovers, passes `--check` with 'holds the same page, compressed by another zlib (this one is 1.2.12)', which is untrue. `check:stores` is the gate `deploy:dry` runs first (package.json:18).
findings.scenario: Actor: the operator on deploy day. The artist reviews `onchain/build-page/animation.html` as ARTWORK-ONCHAIN.md:52 instructs ('The artist looks at it too'); that file is an older copy left from a previous pack or a manual edit while prefix/head/tail/chunks are current. `pnpm -s check:stores` returns 0 and prints the 'another zlib' message; the artist signs off on a page that is not the one in the chunks. The chain is unaffected (the deploy script reads only the manifest and chunk files), so the harm is a wrong review and a misleading check, not a wrong deployment.
findings.evidence: pack_page.py:272-276: `problems = check_outputs(a.out, outputs); if problems and same_store_other_zlib(a.out, outputs): print('pack_page --check: %s holds the same page, compressed by another zlib (this one is %s); its hashes are the ones to publish' ...); return 0`. same_store_other_zlib (219-250) reads only `prefix.bin`, `head.bin`, `tail.bin`, `manifest.json` and the tail chunk files named by the manifest; the compared manifest keys are `('artwork', 'still', 'grids', 'loaderTemplate', 'name', 'description', 'externalUrl', 'pad')` and `sections[prefix|head]`; `animation.html`, `golden.animationUrl`, `golden.page`, `blob` and stray `chunks/*` are never looked at. check_outputs (pack_motifs.py:286-302) does report 'missing/differs animation.html' and 'stray chunks/...', but those problems are discarded on line 274.
findings.fix: Enter the lenient path only when `json.loads(manifest)['blob']['zlibVersion'] != zlib.ZLIB_VERSION` and the problems are confined to `tail.bin`, `chunks/tail_*.bin`, `animation.html` and `manifest.json`; inside it also require `animation.html == head + hex + b"'" + pad + rest_stored`, no stray chunk files, and `golden.animationUrl`/`golden.page` recomputed from the stored tail. Add a test: same zlib, delete animation.html, expect `--check` to return 1.

findings.title: pack_motifs sorts records by `number` while the artwork indexes DATA.symbols by position; an out-of-order page would pack silently with grids and names shifted against what the page shows
findings.description: `motifs_from_data` accepts the records in any order and sorts them by `number` before packing, so motif n's grid and name on-chain are the record whose `number` is n. The artwork never uses `number` to find a record: it reads `fe=DATA.symbols` and `fe[$.title-1]` (index.html:194), and once it reads KILIM_GRIDS it will take motif n at hex characters (n-1)*64 while keeping names and metadata from `DATA.symbols[n-1]`. Today `symbols[i].number == i+1` for all 1,024 (checked), so there is no mismatch; the packer simply does not enforce the invariant the page relies on, and a page that is reordered during the pre-freeze cleanup would pack without a word.
findings.scenario: Actor: the art session re-exporting DATA with the symbols grouped (e.g. by name) and `number` kept. pack_motifs writes grids.bin in number order (correct for the contract), the manifest reports 1,024 motifs and no problem, test:pack and the dry run pass. The deployed page then labels and lays out motif n with `symbols[n-1]`, a different drawing from the one `KilimMotifs.grid(n)` and the motif NFT show; the 'same motifs' claim fails in a way no check sees.
findings.evidence: pack_motifs.py:94-97: `out.sort(key=lambda g: g[0]); numbers = [g[0] for g in out]; if numbers != list(range(1, MOTIF_COUNT + 1)): raise PackError(...)` (only the set of numbers is checked). index.html:194 `fe=DATA.symbols,...fe[$.title-1].name`; index.html:119 `function geometry(rows){ ... rows.forEach((r,y)=>[...r].forEach((v,x)=>{if(v==='1')` (position-based, no `number` lookup). ARTWORK-ONCHAIN.md:22: 'motif n is characters (n-1)*64 to n*64'. Verified today: `all(r['number']==k+1 for k,r in enumerate(symbols))` is True.
findings.fix: Refuse (or at least report in the manifest) a page whose records are not already in `number` order: `if [r['number'] for r in records] != list(range(1, 1025)): raise PackError('DATA.symbols must be in motif order: the page indexes them by position')`, and add the case to test_rejects_bad_pages.

findings.title: Three review-record tests assert less than their AUDIT.md row says: a conditional-only gas sweep, an any-reason revert, and a bare expectRevert
findings.description: All tests named in the 'Fixed, with tests' tables (F-01, F-02, V-01..V-21) and 'Closed by tests' (F-15..F-18) exist and, read in full, check the stated property; none is vacuous. Three are weaker than their row. (1) F-02 `testLowGasSettleCannotSkipThePrize`: the loop at lines 142-152 asserts only inside `if (ok)` / `else`; nothing requires that any gas limit in 60,000..700,000 settled, so if the settle floor ever rose above 700,000 the sweep would pass without examining the window just above the floor where a settle could succeed but the delivery lack gas; the closing `auction.settle()` at line 153 runs with full gas and cannot catch that. The cold variant in `AuditGaps.t.sol:423-439` does assert `delivered != 0` and sweeps to 900,000. (2) V-01 `testMainnetRefusesContentItsConfigDoesNotName` line 575 uses `vm.expectPartialRevert(DeployKilim.Refused.selector)` for 'the real page store is other content than this config names': any `Refused(...)` passes, including today's unrelated 'KilimOneOfOne deployment gas'; the specific reason is deterministic ('expected prefixHash', the first page field `_requireExpected` compares, lines 350) and could be pinned. The zero-valued `expected` field is exercised only through `deployStore` off chain 1 (lines 281-284), never through `deployContracts` or on chain 1, though the row says 'a zero in it ... in both phases'. (3) V-15 `testSendingThePrizeAgainToAWinnerThatRefusesChangesNothing` line 207 uses bare `vm.expectRevert()` where the expected error is OZ's `ERC721InvalidReceiver(address)` bubbled from `KilimOneOfOne.mint`; the following state assertions and the accepting-winner path at line 216 constrain it, so it is weak, not vacuous.
findings.scenario: Actor: a future change that raises the settle floor (for example a larger PRIZE_GAS after the EIP-8037 decision at checklist 1 line 212) or a bug making `deliverPrizeToWinner` revert for every winner before the mint. Outcome: (1) the F-02 sweep passes with no settle examined above 700,000; (2) a wrong refusal reason on mainnet content still passes V-01's last check; (3) a wrong-reason revert passes line 207 and is caught only indirectly at line 216.

votes.reason: The three tests pin what their AUDIT.md rows say; the finding's two concrete "a wrong reason would pass" scenarios do not hold, and its proposed fix for (3) names the wrong error. (1) F-02: AUDIT.md:330 states exactly what the test asserts ("every settle gas limit from 60,000 to 700,000 either reverts with nothing settled or delivers the 1/1"), and AUDIT.md:52 names only the floor; the row is not stronger than the test. Today the floor is PRIZE_GAS + PRIZE_GAS/63 + 50_000 = 557,936 (src/KilimAuction.sol:195) and settle() needs about 585,836, so the sweep at test/GasFloors.t.sol:142 (step 4,000, ceiling 700,000) exercises the `if (ok)` branch (lines 145-147) about 28 times; it is not vacuous now. The "window where a settle succeeds but the delivery lacks gas" cannot exist by construction: line 195 checks gasleft against the same PRIZE_GAS symbol that line 196 forwards (`try this.deliverPrize{gas: PRIZE_GAS}()`), so EIP-150's 63/64 always leaves the full PRIZE_GAS; raising PRIZE_GAS moves both together. The only residue is the hard-coded 700,000 ceiling, which would silently stop sampling successes if PRIZE_GAS rose above about 630,000; but test/AuditGaps.t.sol:408-421 (`testColdHookBudgetToday`, bounds 385,000..389,000 derived from PRIZE_GAS at line 419) and :423-439 (`assertTrue(delivered != 0)` at 438, sweep to 900,000) fail loudly on any PRIZE_GAS change, forcing the gas tests to be revisited together. (2) V-01: the finding says "any Refused passes, including today's unrelated 'KilimOneOfOne deployment gas'". That refusal is unreachable here: in deployContracts (script/DeployKilim.s.sol:443-452) `loadStore(c)` runs at line 447 and `_requireExpected` is called inside it at line 320, before `_requireStored` (448), the nonce checks and the dry-run `_deployThree` (466) where `_gasPolicy`/`_create2` (881, 922-925) raise the gas refusal. Within loadStore, the only earlier text refusals (lines 292-318) cannot fire because the real build-page manifest and the fixture carry identical name/description/externalUrl (both "The Unwoven Kilim" / "A generative ASCII carpet drawn from the 1,024 Kilim motifs." / ""), and the test's `_mainnetConfig` (test/DeployKilim.t.sol:448-455) reads those texts from the fixture via `_config(pageStore)` (lines 72-96) while only `c.pageStore` is switched at line 574. gridsHash and namesHash come from the same motif store, so the first mismatch is deterministically "expected prefixHash" (fixture 0xd716..., real 0x394f...). The partial match is looser than it could be, but no unrelated reason can satisfy it. The "zero in both phases" row (AUDIT.md:352) holds by code: `_expect` at script line 364 is one function (`want == bytes32(0) || want != have`) reached from both phases through loadStore (deployStore line 244, deployContracts line 447) and does not consult the chain id; the zero case at test lines 281-284 pins that function once, which suffices for the claim. (3) V-15: the finding's fix (`ERC721InvalidReceiver(address(winner))`) is wrong. ProbeWallet reverts with `require(!rejectNft, "NFT rejected")` (test/AuditGaps.t.sol:55), and OZ 5.6.1 ERC721Utils.checkOnERC721Received re-raises a non-empty reason verbatim (node_modules/@openzeppelin/contracts/token/ERC721/utils/ERC721Utils.sol:38-45), so the bubbled error is `Error("NFT rejected")`; applying the proposed fix would make the test fail. The bare `vm.expectRevert()` at GasFloors.t.sol:207 is in practice constrained: lines 205-206 rule out NotSettled and PrizeAlreadyClaimed (src/KilimAuction.sol:230-231), no reentrancy is in flight, so the only remaining revert source in deliverPrizeToWinner (lines 229-236) is `oneOfOne.mint` -> `_safeMint` -> the receiver; and the row's "reverts with nothing changed" (AUDIT.md:366) is pinned by lines 209-210 (`!prizeClaimed`, `!minted()`) and the later success at 216-219. No defect, no false safety claim, no launch decision affected.

votes.reason: All three readings of the tests are accurate, but the gap between each test and its AUDIT.md row is smaller than the finding presents, and nothing under the launch configuration depends on it. (1) F-02: test/GasFloors.t.sol:142-152 has no success counter and line 153 `auction.settle();` runs at full gas, as stated. Yet the property is pinned floor-relative elsewhere: test/review/PrizeGasBudget.t.sol:184 `uint256 private constant SETTLE_FLOOR = PRIZE_GAS + PRIZE_GAS / 63 + 50_000;`, :373 `for (uint256 gasLimit = SETTLE_FLOOR - 2_000; gasLimit <= SETTLE_FLOOR + 30_000; gasLimit += 100)` with a Burner winner using the whole warm budget (:365-369), :379 `assertTrue(auction.prizeClaimed());` on every success and :397 `assertTrue(lowestOk != type(uint256).max);`. This sweep moves with PRIZE_GAS, so the scenario "a larger PRIZE_GAS makes the GasFloors sweep vacuous" is caught by PrizeGasBudget, and AuditGaps.t.sol:132-144 and :426-438 also assert `delivered != 0` up to 900,000. Today's floor is 557,936 (src/KilimAuction.sol:195 `if (gasleft() < PRIZE_GAS + PRIZE_GAS / 63 + 50_000) revert InsufficientGas();` with PRIZE_GAS 500,000 at :48), inside the 60,000..700,000 sweep, so the window is examined now. AUDIT.md:52 cites only GasFloors for F-02 while AUDIT.md:403 separately records PrizeGasBudget's "settle floor exact with no bare out-of-gas". (2) V-01: test/DeployKilim.t.sol:575 `vm.expectPartialRevert(DeployKilim.Refused.selector);` accepts any Refused reason, and the zero case at :281-284 (`_spoil(c, field, bytes32(0)); _expectRefused(...); script.deployStore(c, SENDER);`) runs only deployStore off chain 1 inside testAConfigThatNamesItsContentIsHeldToIt (:268). But zero and mismatch share one check, script/DeployKilim.s.sol:364 `if (want == bytes32(0) || want != have) revert Refused(string.concat("expected ", what));`, reached via `_requireExpected` (:342-360) in both phases, and the mismatch path is tested on chain 1 in both phases at test/DeployKilim.t.sol:562-571 (`_expectRefused(string.concat("expected ", name)); script.deployStore(...); _expectRefused(...); script.deployContracts(c);`). So AUDIT.md:352 "a zero in it and any mismatch, in both phases" holds by code path, with the zero case under-tested rather than untested. (3) V-15: test/GasFloors.t.sol:207 `vm.expectRevert();` is bare, but :209-210 (`assertTrue(!auction.prizeClaimed()); assertTrue(!auction.oneOfOne().minted());`) and :216-219 (BOB's deliverPrizeToWinner succeeds, ownerOf(1) == winner) bound what the revert can be; AUDIT.md:366 "reverts with nothing changed if the wallet refuses it" is what the test checks. The finding's proposed fix for (3) is wrong: ProbeWallet refuses with test/AuditGaps.t.sol:55 `require(!rejectNft, "NFT rejected");`, and OpenZeppelin 5.6.1 node_modules/@openzeppelin/contracts/token/ERC721/utils/ERC721Utils.sol:38-46 re-raises non-empty reason data (`revert(add(reason, 0x20), mload(reason))`), raising ERC721InvalidReceiver only when `reason.length == 0`; KilimAuction.deliverPrizeToWinner (src/KilimAuction.sol:229-236) does not wrap the call. The pinned revert would therefore be `Error("NFT rejected")`, and `vm.expectRevert(abi.encodeWithSelector(IERC721Errors.ERC721InvalidReceiver.selector, address(winner)))` would make the test fail. Net: a hygiene finding about test precision, not a defect; no launch decision changes, since the only claim at risk (settle floor coverage after a PRIZE_GAS change) is already pinned by PrizeGasBudget.

findings.title: Seller's shill ladder has zero capital cost: K-07 and K-01 combine so the treasury can take all 1,000,000 motifs and keep the 1/1 for gas, undisclosed
findings.description: K-07 records only that 'A seller can still bid from other wallets; that is undetectable on-chain.' Every disclosure of the self-outbid ladder (AUDIT.md:60, docs/NATIVE-ETH.md:87, checklists/1-pre-deploy.md:35, 184) prices the ladderer's downside as 'If nobody outbids it, it has bought the 1/1 at that price.' For the seller that price is zero: the winning bid is paid to the treasury (EnglishAuction.sol:172 `proceedsDue = highestBid;`, :181-189 `withdrawProceeds`), there is no fee, and the only on-chain guard is the literal treasury address (EnglishAuction.sol:203 `if (msg.sender == treasury) revert TreasuryCannotBid();`). So a wallet the artist controls can (a) fill the 100 registrations and start the clock (F-03), (b) climb 93 minimum rungs to 93.862 ETH in about 12.1M gas, reserving all 1,000,000 motifs, (c) extend the close at will in the last 10 minutes against any collector at no risk, and (d) if it ends as the winner, pay 93.862 ETH to itself and keep the 1/1 plus the whole motif supply. If a collector outbids it (minimum 103.249 ETH after the full ladder), the seller is refunded, keeps 1,000,000 motifs and receives 103.249 ETH of proceeds; the collector's winning bid earns 0 motifs. The Kilim Bazaar rules rely on the opposite claim: 'Supply limits the top on its own ... the auction can never issue more than eleven times the winning bid in motifs' (launch/KILIM-BAZAAR-RULES.md:41, 63) and 'A motif is a motif: from a winning bid, an outbid bid or the market, it counts the same' (:57). Nothing in AUDIT.md, NATIVE-ETH.md, README.md:82 or the terms list in checklists/1-pre-deploy.md:184 says that the seller's shill has no downside, or that the whole Kilim Bazaar supply can be pre-mined by the seller for gas. The only real constraint is about 94 ETH of liquidity for the auction's length, which returns as proceeds. (Realization gas is the one brake: claiming is about 27,982 gas per motif, about 28G gas for the pool, 28 ETH at 1 gwei; credits never expire so it can wait for cheap gas.)
findings.scenario: Actor: the artist (or anyone holding the treasury key) from a second wallet S2. State: bidding open. S2 bids 0.01, 0.011, 0.013 ... 93.862 ETH (93 bids, about 12.1M gas, one or two transactions), reserving motif ids 1..1,000,000. Outcome A: no collector bids above 93.862 ETH; settle() mints the 1/1 to S2 and withdrawProceeds returns the 93.862 ETH to the treasury; net cost gas. Outcome B: a collector bids 103.249 ETH and wins with motifReward 0; S2 is refunded 93.862 ETH and keeps 1,000,000 motifs; the treasury receives 103.249 ETH. In both outcomes every other bidder's motifs are a rounding error against a supply the seller owns, and the published terms said nothing about it.
findings.evidence: AUDIT.md:153 "The treasury address cannot bid or register (`TreasuryCannotBid`). If nobody outbids it, it has bought the 1/1 at that price."; docs/NATIVE-ETH.md:109 "The treasury address can neither register nor bid."; EnglishAuction.sol:203 `if (msg.sender == treasury) revert TreasuryCannotBid();`; EnglishAuction.sol:172 `proceedsDue = highestBid;`; KilimAuction.sol:135 `return Math.min(Math.min(amount / MOTIF_PRICE, maxMotifsPerBid), motifCap - motifsAllocated);`. findings.title: KILIM-BAZAAR-RULES formula for the winner's id range and the 'Master costs the winning bid in motifs' rule fail whenever the winning bid's reward was capped
findings.description: The rules say the Kilim Bazaar contract will read the winner's id range as `motifsAllocated − highestBid / 0.001 ETH + 1 … motifsAllocated` and price the Master at `highestBid` in motifs, 'the winner's own Master, which nobody else can make' (:26, :43). The auction grants `rewardForBid = min(amount / MOTIF_PRICE, maxMotifsPerBid, motifCap - motifsAllocated)` (KilimAuction.sol:135), so the winning bid's reward is below `highestBid / 0.001 ETH` whenever the pool runs short, and 0 once it is empty (NATIVE-ETH.md:89 'bids still count for the 1/1 and earn nothing'). Then the formula either underflows or points at ids reserved by earlier bidders, and the Master costs more motifs than the winner's bid earned (possibly all of them when the winner earned 0). Even the minimum-step ladder itself shows it: its 93rd rung of 93.862 ETH earns only 61,893 of 93,862 nominal motifs, so `motifsAllocated − 93,862 + 1 = 906,139` lands inside the 92nd rung's range. Separately, the auction keeps `_creditRanges` private (KilimAuction.sol:44) and exposes only `unclaimedMotifRanges` (:181), so once the winner claims, no on-chain reader can recover the winning bid's range; only the `BidPlaced` log (:130) carries `firstMotifId` and `motifReward`. Because the auction is immutable, whatever the Bazaar contract needs from it must be a getter before the freeze.
findings.scenario: Actor: the future Kilim Bazaar contract following :79. State: pool exhausted by a 93-rung ladder (ids 1..1,000,000 reserved), a collector wins at 103.249 ETH with motifReward 0. Outcome: Master price 103,249 motifs; the winner holds none from the bid; the formula gives ids 896,752..1,000,000, which belong to the ladderer, so the 'woven from the winning bid' tag can be earned by the ladderer and never by the winner. Milder state: 2,000 motifs left, winning bid 5 ETH earns 2,000; the formula names 5,000 ids, 3,000 of them someone else's.
