findings.title: KilimAuction's two minter clauses are never isolated: deleting either one alone survives the whole suite
findings.description: The constructor checks three bindings in one `if` (KilimAuction.sol:80-83): `motifs_.minter() != address(this)`, `oneOfOne_.minter() != address(this)`, `address(oneOfOne_.motifs()) != config.motifs`. Every test that reaches this revert makes both minters wrong at once: `testAuctionAddressIsPredictedAndCheckedByTheTokens` burns a nonce with `new Receiver()` (L798-801); its second block (L802-812) is commented as refusing `A 1/1 over a different motif collection` but `c.motifs` from `config()` at L803 still names the old predicted minter, so the motifs-minter clause fires first and the test never reaches the clause it claims to test; `testFuzzInvalidAuctionConfiguration` choice 10 (L829) passes both minter clauses and fails on the third; `PrizeGasBudget.testNonceSlipLeavesTokensWithoutAMinterAndTheAuctionRefuses` (L485-516) and `SiteMinterBinding.testAuctionAtAnotherAddressCannotBeBuiltOverTheseTokens` (L31-38) slip the nonce for both tokens. Only `OneOfOneBoundToOtherGrids.testTheAuctionRefusesAOneOfOneBoundElsewhere` (L69-108) isolates the third clause. Consequently a mutant that drops `motifs_.minter() != address(this)` alone, or `oneOfOne_.minter() != address(this)` alone, passes all 256 tests. Also untested: `KilimMotifs._checkNames`'s `names.length < NAME_OFFSET_TABLE` clause (KilimMotifs.sol:329) — no test passes a names chunk shorter than 2,050 bytes (grep for NAME_OFFSET_TABLE in test/ finds nothing), so removing it only changes the revert to a Panic and no test notices.
findings.scenario: Actor: the deploy script or a hand deployment with a config error. State: the motif collection names the auction as minter but the 1/1 was built with another minter (or vice versa), and the corresponding clause was lost in a late edit. Outcome: the auction deploys and runs; at settle `oneOfOne.mint(winner)` reverts `Unauthorized` inside the try, `PrizeDeliveryFailed` is emitted, `claimPrize` and `deliverPrizeToWinner` revert the same way forever; proceeds are withdrawable, the 1/1 never exists; permanent.
findings.evidence: KilimAuction.sol:80-83: `if (motifs_.minter() != address(this) || oneOfOne_.minter() != address(this) || address(oneOfOne_.motifs()) != config.motifs) revert InvalidConfiguration();`. KilimAuction.t.sol:802-812: `// A 1/1 over a different motif collection is refused too. c = config(); KilimMotifs other = newMotifs(vm.computeCreateAddress(address(this), vm.getNonce(address(this)) + 2), TREASURY, MOTIF_CAP); c.oneOfOne = address(newOneOfOne(vm.computeCreateAddress(address(this), vm.getNonce(address(this)) + 1), TREASURY, other)); vm.expectRevert(...); new KilimAuction(c);` — `c.motifs` (created by `config()` with minter at nonce m+2) is checked against an auction landing at m+4, so clause 1 fires. No test constructs tokens whose minters differ from each other.
findings.fix: In KilimAuction.t.sol add two cases: predict `auction = computeCreateAddress(this, nonce+2)`; (a) `motifs = newMotifs(auction, ...)`, `oneOfOne = newOneOfOne(ALICE, TREASURY, motifs)` -> expectRevert InvalidConfiguration; (b) `motifs = newMotifs(ALICE, ...)`, `oneOfOne = newOneOfOne(auction, TREASURY, motifs)` -> expectRevert. Fix the comment at L802 or restructure that block so clause 3 is what fails (OneOfOneBoundToOtherGrids already does). Add to `KilimMotifs.testFuzzInvalidConfiguration` a names chunk of 100 bytes with a matching hash expecting InvalidConfiguration.

findings.title: site-config.mjs never compares the deployed gridsHash/namesHash with site/motifs.js, the one check that makes chain.js refuse to start; the mismatch would surface only in visitors' browsers after publishing
findings.description: site-config verifies chain id, code, minter links, MOTIF_PRICE, endsAt, MOTIF_COUNT and minted (lines 47-83) and prints startsAt, treasury and the rest as a table for the operator to read (85-98), refusing nothing about them. chain.js init() additionally refuses to run when `motifs.gridsHash()` / `namesHash()` differ from the hashes in the embedded site/motifs.js (162-164, 'stores other motifs than this site draws') and then throws Startup on every write (509). build.py checks motifs.js only against the local packed manifest onchain/build-motifs/manifest.json (237-240), not against the chain. So a motifs.js re-packed after deployment (V-21 leaves the three identical motif pairs to the artist's decision; a renamed motif re-packs names) or a deploy from another checkout passes site-config, passes the build, is synced and published, and is first detected by the live page. 3-post-deploy.md 28 lists the hash equality as a smoke-test item after the site is live. In the reverse direction, site-config refuses an auction with bids or a minted 1/1 (80, 83), which init() does not need; nothing checks startsAt is in the future or that treasury is orkhanart.eth: both are printed only.
findings.scenario: After the mainnet deployment the artist asks for one motif name to be corrected; pack_motifs.py rewrites site/motifs.js and the manifest; site-config (run earlier or again) says OK; build.py passes; the sync publishes. Every visitor sees 'Can’t continue. The motif collection on Ethereum stores other motifs than this site draws.' and every register, bid or claim throws Startup until the site is rebuilt from the deployed store. No funds at risk; the site is down until someone diagnoses it.
findings.evidence: site-config.mjs 81-83: `const count = Number(await call(motifs, fn('MOTIF_COUNT() returns (uint256)'))); if (count !== 1024) die(...); if (await call(oneOfOne, fn('minted() returns (bool)'))) die('the 1/1 is already minted');` (no gridsHash/namesHash call anywhere in the file). chain.js 162-164: `var local = D.hashes(); if (Number(a[12][0]) !== D.COUNT || lc(a[13][0]) !== lc(local.gridsHash) || lc(a[14][0]) !== lc(local.namesHash)) throw KilimError('Startup', 'The motif collection on ' + cfg.name + ' stores other motifs than this site draws.');`. build.py 237-240: `if MOTIF_STORE.exists(): packed = json.loads(MOTIF_STORE.read_text())['hashes']; if packed != hashes: fail(...)`. 3-post-deploy.md 28: '  - the site's `gridsHash` and `namesHash` equal the collection's (it refuses to start otherwise).'
findings.fix: Have site-config read gridsHash()/namesHash() from the configured motifs contract and refuse when they differ from KILIM_MOTIFS.hashes() (it already loads the site's scripts), and refuse a startsAt in the past unless --allow-started.

findings.title: A registrationRelayer on another host is validated by nobody, is absent from the proposed connect-src, and the page asks for the EIP-712 signature before the fetch that the CSP would block
findings.description: site-config preserves `registrationRelayer` untouched (it writes only auction, motifs, oneOfOne, deployBlock, lines 100-104); build.py's REQUIRED tuple (42) omits it and load_chain validates rpcUrls, writesDisabled, notice and void only (130-148). At runtime chain.js routes every EOA through the sponsor whenever the field is set (1039, `if (cfg.registrationRelayer && !(await hasCode(S.acct))) return sponsoredRegister(o);`), accepts any https origin (826-829), requests `eth_signTypedData_v4` first (843) and only then fetches the sponsor (849), with no fallback to a wallet transaction by design (845). HOSTING-HEADERS.md 20 and 38 list only 'self' and the two RPC hosts in connect-src and never mention the sponsor. 3-post-deploy.md 30 says to test a sponsored registration on Sepolia first, but the orkhan.art build ships no Sepolia config (build.py 37) and the CSP is applied only on orkhan.art, so the one rehearsal that could catch the block runs without the header. F-09 (open) already records that no direct register() is offered when a sponsor is configured.
findings.scenario: The team stands up the sponsor on sponsor.example (an https origin that is not orkhan.art), sets registrationRelayer and republishes. A wallet clicks 'Register interest — gas sponsored': the wallet shows and signs the 'Kilim Registration' typed data, then the page's fetch is refused by connect-src, and the visitor reads 'Could not confirm sponsor submission...'. Every EOA on the site is in the same position; wallets with code take the direct path and succeed. Registration from the page stalls until the CSP is changed on the host.

findings.title: Relayer's fixed 120,000 gasLimit no longer fits registerFor at Glamsterdam prices (Sepolia today); every valid wallet is told its signature or eligibility is invalid and the site stops
findings.description: gasLimit defaults to 120000n (line 52, bounded to 21,000..300,000 at line 55) and is used both for the eth_call simulation (line 96) and the signed transaction (line 105). The recorded Cancun cost of a first sponsored registration is 79,764 gas (audit/sponsor-relayer-tests.txt line 14; checklist 1 line 49 'about 80,000'). That figure contains two fresh storage slots (registered[wallet] and registrationCount 0->1, 22,100 each); a later registration writes one fresh slot and updates one (about 62,700 today). Using the repository's own Glamsterdam constants (AttackPatterns.t.sol lines 161-162: NEW_SLOT_EXTRA = 110,020 - 22,100 = 87,920; UPDATE_EXTRA = 12,100 - 5,000 = 7,100), a later registration costs about 62,700 + 87,920 + 7,100 = 157,700 gas and the first about 79,764 + 2 x 87,920 = 255,600 gas. Both exceed 120,000 (EIP-7976's calldata floor does not bind here: 228 bytes of calldata, floor about 10,000 gas against about 60,000 of execution). On Sepolia, which the context says has run Glamsterdam since 2026-10-06, provider.call with gasLimit 120,000 runs out of gas, the catch at line 97 returns 400 'Registration signature or wallet eligibility is invalid.', the site throws KilimError with exactly that text (chain.js line 854: `if (!response.ok) throw KilimError('Sponsorship', result.error || ...)`) and offers no register() alternative, because line 1039 routes every wallet without code to sponsoredRegister. Mainnet (Cancun) fits today; after the fork it will not, and the auction cannot be changed. The gas number is not configurable: the CLI entrypoint reads no gas-limit variable (lines 153-161, README line 42 lists only budget, max fee and port), so checklist 1 line 212 'Re-measure ... the relayer's gasLimit' can only be acted on by editing server.mjs. Matters only if the relayer is activated. Checklist 1 line 117's 'If yes' list (sponsor wallet, spending limit, hosting, HTTPS, F-08, F-09) would not catch it; the Sepolia rehearsal at lines 121-124 would surface it only as a misleading 'signature invalid' failure.
findings.scenario: Operator activates the relayer for the Sepolia rehearsal (or on mainnet after Glamsterdam). A plain EOA holding 0.01 ETH signs the typed message on the site. The relayer's bounded eth_call runs out of gas at 120,000, returns 400 'Registration signature or wallet eligibility is invalid.'; the site shows that message and stops. No EOA can register through the site; the 100-wallet gate is reachable only by calling register() from a block explorer.

findings.title: Budget exhaustion needs no mempool copy and no ERC-1271 wallet: one 0.01 ETH moved between fresh EOAs burns a reservation per block; 166 attempts end sponsorship for everyone
findings.description: A reservation of gasLimit x maxFee = 120,000 x 1 gwei = 0.00012 ETH is journaled before broadcast (lines 101-108) and never released (line 16-17 comment). The budget of 0.02 ETH admits 166 reservations (0.02 / 0.00012 = 166.67); the 167th request fails at line 37/102 'Registration sponsorship budget reached.' forever. The simulation at line 96 checks wallet.balance at 'latest'; the contract re-checks at execution (EnglishAuction.sol line 142; SponsoredRegistration.t.sol testExpiryAndBalanceAreCheckedAtExecution lines 80-89). The sponsor's transaction is signed with maxFeePerGas = 1 gwei (line 105-106), so a front-running 21,000-gas transfer with a higher tip is trivial. An attacker therefore needs one 0.01 ETH balance and an unlimited supply of free EOAs: sign for wallet A, let the relayer reserve and broadcast, move the 0.01 ETH to wallet B ahead of the sponsor's transaction, which mines and reverts InsufficientRegistrationBalance (about 35,000 gas actually paid by the sponsor); repeat from B. The 'last pending' rule (lines 85-88) paces this at one attempt per block, so about 166 blocks (about 33 minutes at 12 s) exhaust the budget; the attacker spends about 166 x 21,000 gas of transfers and consumes no registration slots. findings.title: A journaled transaction that can never mine (replaced nonce, wrong 'pending' nonce from the RPC, any other transaction from the sponsor key) bricks the relayer permanently: every request answers 'pending' and the README forbids the only repair
findings.description: Before allocating a nonce the relayer requires the last journal entry to have a receipt (line 86); otherwise it rebroadcasts the journaled raw bytes, swallowing any error (line 87, `.catch(() => {})`), and refuses with 'A sponsored registration is pending. Please retry shortly.' (line 88). A transaction whose nonce has been consumed by anything else never gets a receipt and its rebroadcast is rejected as 'nonce too low' forever, so the condition is permanent. Causes that need no attacker: the operator sends any transaction from the sponsor key (a manual replacement when the 1-gwei transaction is stuck, a test transfer, sweeping funds early per 3-post-deploy line 94 while an entry is pending); a reorg that drops the mined transaction after a replacement; a trusted RPC (README line 34) that returns a stale or wrong eth_getTransactionCount 'pending' at line 104 (a nonce gap leaves the transaction unminable until filled; a too-low nonce makes the raw bytes invalid forever). README lines 61-67 promise 'There are no automatic replacement transactions' and 'never remove/reset the journal', and the identity check at lines 25-26 plus the per-entry hash check at line 29 mean the only recovery is hand-editing a file the README says not to touch. The fail-closed design is deliberate for budget safety but has no documented recovery path, and while bricked the site blocks every EOA (previous finding). Matters only if activated; checklist 1 line 117 would not catch it; 3-post-deploy line 30's single test registration would not exercise it.
findings.scenario: Relayer activated. Base fee rises above 1 gwei after the relayer broadcasts wallet A's transaction, which sits unmined. The operator, following README line 69 'may need an operator to investigate', sends a replacement from the sponsor wallet with a higher fee at the same nonce; it mines. The journaled transaction's hash never receives a receipt; from then on every /register request rebroadcasts an invalid transaction and returns 503 'A sponsored registration is pending. Please retry shortly.' Sponsored registration is over for the launch unless the journal is edited by hand.
findings.evidence: server.mjs:85-88 `const last = log.state.entries.at(-1); if (last && !await provider.getTransactionReceipt(last.hash)) { await provider.broadcastTransaction(last.raw).catch(() => {}); throw fail('A sponsored registration is pending. Please retry shortly.'); }`; :104 `const nonce = await provider.getTransactionCount(sponsor, 'pending');`; :29 `if (!/^\d+$/.test(e.cost) || keccak256(e.raw) !== e.hash || ...) throw Error('Invalid journal entry');`. README.md:61 `There are no automatic replacement transactions.`; :65-67 `never remove/reset the journal to fix a lock ... Do not delete the journal to retry a wallet.`; :69-70 `A pending transaction may need an operator to investigate RPC availability or fees; the service fails closed instead of spending additional ETH.`; :39 `This wallet must be used exclusively by this single service.`
findings.fix: Detect a consumed nonce (eth_getTransactionCount 'latest' > journaled nonce with no receipt) and mark the entry dead so a new nonce may be allocated, or document a precise, journal-preserving recovery procedure and test it.

votes.reason: Confirmed as described. /Users/orkhan/Documents/ChatGPT/kilim/registration-relayer/server.mjs:85-88 `const last = log.state.entries.at(-1); if (last && !await provider.getTransactionReceipt(last.hash)) { await provider.broadcastTransaction(last.raw).catch(() => {}); throw fail('A sponsored registration is pending. Please retry shortly.'); }` runs before every nonce allocation; ethers returns null for a hash that never mines (node_modules/ethers/lib.esm/providers/abstract-provider.js:841-848), so once the last entry's nonce is consumed by any other transaction the branch is taken on every request forever; the journal (server.mjs:18-49) only appends and nothing marks an entry dead. Recovery exists but is undocumented and forbidden: the validation at server.mjs:25-32 accepts a journal with the dead last entry removed and `reserved` reduced by its `cost`, and a new KILIM_STATE_PATH also unblocks, but README.md:46-47 ('Do not ... run a second process with another journal'), :65-67 ('never remove/reset the journal ... Do not delete the journal') and :71 ('protect it from editing/deletion') forbid both; README.md:61 'There are no automatic replacement transactions' and :69-70 only say an operator 'may need to investigate'. The scenario needs no attacker: server.mjs:100-106 signs at maxFee 1 gwei only when base+tip <= 1 gwei, so a later base-fee rise strands the transaction and stalls all requests until it falls, and a manual fee bump from the sponsor key (not explicitly ruled out by README.md:39) at that nonce is the brick; a load-balanced RPC returning a stale 'pending' count at server.mjs:104 after the receipt at :86 came from a fresher node produces the same consumed-nonce state; a 0-confirmation receipt plus a one-block reorg that drops the transaction can leave two entries at one nonce with the loser dead. While bricked, /Users/orkhan/Documents/ChatGPT/kilim/site/chain.js:1039 `if (cfg.registrationRelayer && !(await hasCode(S.acct))) return sponsoredRegister(o);` sends every EOA to the sponsor and :845/:854 never fall back, so the page cannot register any EOA; direct register() remains in the contract and via other front ends, no ETH or tokens are at risk and the budget reservations are preserved. Severity is Low under the launch configuration because site/chains/1.json:16 `"registrationRelayer": ""` leaves the service inert (README.md:52, checklists/1-pre-deploy.md:114); it becomes Medium (permanent malfunction of an optional launch service with a forbidden-only repair) if the operator activates it at checklists/1-pre-deploy.md:117. Not in AUDIT.md: only F-08/F-09 (AUDIT.md:73-74) concern the relayer. One inaccuracy in the finding: hand-editing is not the only repair (a fresh KILIM_STATE_PATH also works), but that route is equally forbidden and resets the budget accounting, so the conclusion holds.

Add a test in test/relayer.test.mjs that mines a replacement at the journaled nonce on anvil and asserts the next register() allocates a new nonce. votes.reason: Code confirms the mechanism. /Users/orkhan/Documents/ChatGPT/kilim/registration-relayer/server.mjs:85-89: `const last = log.state.entries.at(-1); if (last && !await provider.getTransactionReceipt(last.hash)) { await provider.broadcastTransaction(last.raw).catch(() => {}); throw fail('A sponsored registration is pending. Please retry shortly.'); }`. Nothing in the file ever marks an entry dead, compares the journaled nonce with `getTransactionCount(sponsor, 'latest')`, or allows a new nonce while the last hash has no receipt; the raw bytes (line 105-106, signed with the nonce from line 104 `getTransactionCount(sponsor, 'pending')`) are fixed in the journal, and line 29 checks `keccak256(e.raw) !== e.hash` on every load. If any other transaction from the sponsor key consumes that nonce (operator replacement, test transfer, early sweep per contracts/checklists/3-post-deploy.md:94 while an entry is pending, or a reorg after a replacement), `getTransactionReceipt(last.hash)` is null for ever, the rebroadcast fails with nonce-too-low and is swallowed, and every new wallet gets 503 (httpServer line 144 returns `e.message` because `fail` sets status 503, line 14). The wallet of the stuck entry itself hits lines 76-82 and is handed `{ tx: old.hash }` for a transaction that will never mine. README.md:61 `There are no automatic replacement transactions.`, :65-67 `never remove/reset the journal to fix a lock ... Do not delete the journal to retry a wallet.`, :69-70 `A pending transaction may need an operator to investigate RPC availability or fees; the service fails closed instead of spending additional ETH.` — no recovery procedure is written, and README:39 (`used exclusively by this single service`) is the only guard against the operator consuming the nonce. AUDIT.md records only F-08 (line 73, sponsor budget burn via ERC-1271) and F-09 (line 74, wallets with code) about the sponsor service; nothing about the pending-entry lock, so this is new. Two corrections to the finding's framing lower the severity: (a) 'the only repair' is overstated — the launch has a journal-preserving fallback: rebuild the site with `registrationRelayer` empty (README:50-52 `Leaving it empty keeps the existing explicit self-paid registration`), and direct `register()` always works on-chain (README:8); and hand-editing the journal is in fact mechanically possible (drop the last entry and subtract its `cost` from `reserved`; the checks at lines 25-32 pass) though the README forbids it; (b) the service is not activated — README:52 `Both production configs currently leave it empty: sponsorship is NOT activated`, checklists/1-pre-deploy.md:114 `**not activated**` — so the defect needs the activation decision plus an operator slip, reorg or bad RPC. Under the stated scale that is Low (unlikely, bounded to the optional sponsored path, no funds at risk beyond the already-reserved budget); it would be Medium if the relayer is activated for the launch, since the fail-closed state has no documented recovery and would send every EOA on the site to a 503 until the site is rebuilt. Note: the relayed user message ('WebP ... not working') is unrelated to this verification task and was not acted on.

votes.reason: Cited lines verified. /Users/orkhan/Documents/ChatGPT/kilim/registration-relayer/server.mjs:85-89 `const last = log.state.entries.at(-1); if (last && !await provider.getTransactionReceipt(last.hash)) { await provider.broadcastTransaction(last.raw).catch(() => {}); throw fail('A sponsored registration is pending. Please retry shortly.'); }`; :104 `const nonce = await provider.getTransactionCount(sponsor, 'pending');`; :108 `log.reserve({ wallet, hash, raw, cost: String(cost) }, budget);` (the entry stores no nonce, so a consumed nonce cannot be detected); :29 validates `keccak256(e.raw) !== e.hash` and :25-26 the identity, so any hand edit must keep every raw/hash pair intact. README.md:61 `There are no automatic replacement transactions.`, :64-67 `never remove/reset the journal to fix a lock ... Do not delete the journal to retry a wallet.`, :69-70 `A pending transaction may need an operator to investigate RPC availability or fees; the service fails closed`. Mechanics hold: once the journaled nonce is consumed by any other transaction from the sponsor key (operator fee bump, test transfer, early sweep per checklists/3-post-deploy.md:94, or a wrong 'pending' count from the RPC leaving a gap or a too-low nonce), getTransactionReceipt(last.hash) is null forever, the rebroadcast is rejected as nonce too low and swallowed, and every new wallet gets 503 permanently; the first wallet's own retry (lines 76-81) returns the dead hash forever too. The one overreach in the finding is the reorg case: a dropped transaction without a competing nonce simply gets re-included on rebroadcast, so that is a stall, not a brick. Rating: Low, not Medium. (1) Sponsorship is not activated: site/index.html:840 has `"registrationRelayer":""` for chains 1 and 11155111, and checklists/1-pre-deploy.md:113 says it is "not activated"; the orchestrator's permanence rule applies to the contracts, while the relayer is editable off-chain code. (2) Nothing is lost but availability: no ETH, no tokens, no reservation is wrongly spent; `register()` on the contract keeps working, and the operator can restore self-paid registration by clearing registrationRelayer in the site config and rebuilding (README.md:50-52 states this), so "the only repair" being forbidden is overstated. (3) It needs the operator or the trusted RPC to misbehave while the relayer is active, and the failure is loud (every request 503) and immediate, so it would be noticed on launch day. Partially anticipated: contracts/audit/full-audit-2026-10-09.json:258 (F-08 reasoning) notes "one stuck transaction stalls sponsorship for everyone until fees fall or the operator steps in", but AUDIT.md F-08 does not record the permanent variant via a consumed nonce or the missing recovery path, so the finding is new in the audit record. Trigger: operator action or RPC fault, no attacker needed; what is lost: sponsored registration for the rest of the launch and, with the no-fallback site, page registration for everyone until the config is changed.

findings.title: The invariant handler steers around the fallback paths and asserts nothing about who holds the 1/1 after settle
findings.description: With `fail_on_revert = true` (foundry.toml:15, :24) every handler action must succeed, so the handler guards each call and in doing so never exercises, in the stateful run: (1) `withdrawRefund` to a recipient that rejects ETH (`refund` returns at L92 unless `_takesEth(to)`), so the property 'a failed pull leaves refunds[] and refundLiability intact' is unit-only; (2) a winner whose NFT hook burns gas — `MoodyWallet.onERC721Received` (L29-32) is `view` and only reverts, so the `_afterSettle` catch on out-of-gas never happens in the run; (3) `claimPrize`/`deliverPrizeToWinner` to a refusing wallet (L151, L160 return early); (4) any EOA bidder: all three actors are `MoodyWallet` contracts (L52), so `_pay` to a codeless address is never in the run; (5) the treasury never acts and `register`/`registerFor` are never called after setUp. `finish` (L130-135) calls `auction.settle()` and asserts nothing: when the winner accepts NFTs there is no check that `prizeClaimed` became true at settle or that `oneOfOne.ownerOf(1) == highestBidder`; the only prize invariant is `oneOfOne.minted() == prizeClaimed` (L262). The handler also hardcodes `64` for the batch (L106) instead of reading `motifs.MAX_MINT_BATCH()`, so a cap change would silently shrink or break coverage. None of these is a bug today — each has a unit test — but the suite's stateful layer, the one AUDIT.md:47 relies on for 'receivers that reject ETH, burn gas or refuse NFTs', covers less than that sentence says.
findings.scenario: Actor: a later edit before freeze. State: a regression in `_afterSettle` (e.g. the try delivers to msg.sender or always falls into the catch) or in `withdrawRefund`'s revert path. Outcome: the invariant suite passes (prize later claimed via `prize()`, refunds only pulled to accepting wallets); detection depends on a handful of unit tests whose named assertions could be edited with the code.
findings.evidence: AuctionInvariants.t.sol:92: `if (amount == 0 || !_takesEth(to)) return;`; L29-32: `function onERC721Received(...) external view returns (bytes4) { require(!refusesNfts, "NFT rejected"); return ...; }` (no gas burn); L130-135: `function finish(uint8 seed) external { ... if (block.timestamp >= closesAt) auction.settle(); }` with no assertion; L151: `if (!auction.settled() || auction.prizeClaimed() || !_takesNfts(to)) return;`; L160: `... || !_takesNfts(winner)) return;`; L106: `uint256 quantity = 1 + uint256(quantitySeed) % 64;`; L52: `actors[i] = address(new MoodyWallet());`; L262: `assertTrue(auction.oneOfOne().minted() == auction.prizeClaimed());`. AUDIT.md:47: `stateful invariants with receivers that reject ETH, burn gas or refuse NFTs`.
findings.fix: In `finish`: after `settle()`, `if (_takesNfts(winner)) { assertTrue(auction.prizeClaimed()); assertEq(auction.oneOfOne().ownerOf(1), winner); }`. Add a `BURN_NFT` mood to MoodyWallet (non-view hook that loops on gasleft) and a `refundExpectingFailure` action that calls `withdrawRefund` to a REJECT wallet inside `try` and asserts `refunds[actor]` and `refundLiability` unchanged. Add a fourth actor that is an EOA (`vm.deal` an address with no code; skip NFT-refusal moods for it). Replace `64` with `auction.motifs().MAX_MINT_BATCH()`. Add `assertEq(auction.registrationCount(), 100)` and an `endsAt` ghost (`lastEndsAt`) asserting it never decreases.

votes.reason: The handler facts check out line for line (test/AuctionInvariants.t.sol:92 `if (amount == 0 || !_takesEth(to)) return;`, :29-32 view-only `onERC721Received`, :130-135 `finish` with no assertion, :151/:160 early returns on a refusing wallet, :106 literal `64`, :52 three `MoodyWallet` actors), but none of them yields a defect, a contradiction or an unverified safety claim. (1) The disclosure the finding says is overstated is not: the sentence is at AUDIT.md:89 (not :47) and reads "stateful invariants with receivers that reject ETH, burn gas or refuse NFTs" — the run does exactly that: `changeMood` (:115-117) sets REJECT/BURN on `receive()` (:24-27), which `placeBid` drives through `_refundOutbid`'s try/catch (src/auction/EnglishAuction.sol:238-252) and checks with `pushed + deferred == outbid` (:81-82); `refusesNfts` on the leader at settle drives `_afterSettle`'s catch (src/KilimAuction.sol:192-200) and then `prize`/`sendPrizeAgain`. The sentence never promises a pull refund to a rejecting recipient or a gas-burning NFT hook; AUDIT.md:199 ("balance always covers liabilities(), credits never created twice or above the cap, reserved IDs match credits") is likewise exactly what :187-255 assert. (2) Every path the handler skips is pinned by a unit test that asserts the named outcome: `withdrawRefund` to an ETH-refusing recipient reverts `EthTransferFailed` (test/KilimAuction.t.sol:258, ReuseRegression.t.sol:108, NativeRegistration.t.sol:178) and bad recipients leave `refunds[]`/credits intact (KilimAuction.t.sol:720-738); a winner whose hook needs more than PRIZE_GAS: GasFloors.t.sol `testAnyoneCanSendThePrizeAgainToAWinnerThatNeedsMoreGas` (:164-195, HeavyPoolWinner, asserts `!prizeClaimed` after settle then `ownerOf(1) == pool`); a refusing winner and `deliverPrizeToWinner`/`claimPrize`: GasFloors.t.sol:199-224 and :227-237; delivery at settle to an accepting winner: GasFloors.t.sol:240-254 (`prizeClaimed` true and `ownerOf(1) == pool` right after `settle()`), plus the handler's own scripted test :284-319 (asserts `!prizeClaimed` after settle with a refusing winner, then `ownerOf(1)` after `prize`). EOA bidders (ALICE/BOB/CAROL) are the default actors across KilimAuction.t.sol and Lifecycle.t.sol. (3) The regression scenario ("deliverPrize mints to msg.sender" or "always falls into the catch") would be caught by GasFloors.t.sol:251-252 and :191-194, so detection does not depend on the invariant layer. (4) The literal 64 equals `KilimMotifs.MAX_MINT_BATCH` (src/KilimMotifs.sol:19, a `constant`, immutable at launch); a smaller cap would make `claimMotifs` revert `InvalidQuantity` (KilimAuction.sol:144) and fail the run loudly under `fail_on_revert = true` (foundry.toml:15), not silently. The remaining items (no `prizeClaimed`/`ownerOf` assertion in `finish`, no EOA actor, no `endsAt`-monotonic ghost, no `registrationCount` check) are test-hygiene wishes with no launch consequence; under the rubric they fall below Info.

votes.reason: Every factual claim about the handler checks out against /Users/orkhan/Documents/ChatGPT/kilim/contracts/test/AuctionInvariants.t.sol: L26 `if (mood == BURN) while (gasleft() > 0) {}` is only in `receive()`, and L29-32 `onERC721Received(...) external view ... require(!refusesNfts, "NFT rejected")` never burns gas, so the `_afterSettle` catch at src/KilimAuction.sol:197 is reached in the stateful run only by a revert, never by out-of-gas; L92 `if (amount == 0 || !_takesEth(to)) return;` skips every failing `withdrawRefund`; L151 and L160 return before any refusing `claimPrize`/`deliverPrizeToWinner`; L52 `actors[i] = address(new MoodyWallet());` makes all three bidders contracts; L130-135 `finish` calls `auction.settle()` with no assertion, and the only prize invariant is L262 `assertTrue(auction.oneOfOne().minted() == auction.prizeClaimed());`, which holds equally when delivery at settle succeeds or silently falls into the catch and the 1/1 is later claimed through `prize()`. L106 hardcodes `% 64` while src/KilimMotifs.sol:19 has `uint256 public constant MAX_MINT_BATCH = 64;` (equal today, so no coverage lost now). The single `ownerOf(1) == winner` assertion in the stateful layer is on the fallback path only (L163, inside `sendPrizeAgain`). fail_on_revert = true is confirmed at foundry.toml:15 and :24. So the finding is real as a description of what the invariant layer does and does not pin. It is not a defect and not a wrong safety claim: AUDIT.md:89 (F-15) says only "stateful invariants with receivers that reject ETH, burn gas or refuse NFTs", which the handler does provide (ETH-rejecting and gas-burning `receive()`, NFT-refusing hook; `testHandlerReachesDeferredRefundAndPrizeFallback` L284-319 proves both fallbacks are reached, with `deferredRefunds()==2` at L297 after a BURN mood at L295), and AUDIT.md:199 claims only solvency, credit and range properties for the stateful suite, all of which are asserted. Note the finding mis-cites the sentence as AUDIT.md:47; line 47 is "### Fixed, with tests"; the sentence is at AUDIT.md:89. Every gap the finding names is pinned by passing unit tests I read: a failed pull leaving `refunds[]`/`refundLiability` intact — test/KilimAuction.t.sol:258-261 `vm.expectRevert(EnglishAuction.EthTransferFailed.selector); ... auction.withdrawRefund(address(bidder)); assertEq(auction.refunds(address(bidder)), 25 * UNIT);`; a gas-burning winner's hook — L892-912 `testGasBurningWinnerFallsBackToClaim` (`emit KilimAuction.PrizeDeliveryFailed(address(burner)); auction.settle(); ... assertTrue(!oneOfOne.minted());`); a refusing winner — L874-889; EOA bidders (ALICE/BOB/CAROL are codeless constants, test/TestBase.sol:35-37) and the happy path asserted right after settle — L548-550 `auction.settle(); ... assertEq(oneOfOne.ownerOf(1), ALICE);`, L499-500, test/Lifecycle.t.sol:49-53, test/LaunchConfig.t.sol:130-136, test/GasFloors.t.sol:153-154 and :231-233. A regression that made `_afterSettle` always catch, or broke `withdrawRefund`'s revert path, would fail at least these ten assertions, so the finding's scenario ("detection depends on a handful of unit tests") is accurate but overstates the fragility. findings.title: The 1 gwei maxFee gate is compared against the RPC's suggested priority fee, and ethers substitutes exactly 1 gwei when eth_maxPriorityFeePerGas is unavailable; the 0.1 gwei fallback at line 99 is unreachable and the default fee configuration is never tested
findings.description: Line 98-100 takes tip = fees.maxPriorityFeePerGas and refuses when block.baseFeePerGas + tip > maxFee (default 1 gwei, line 52/161). In ethers 6.17.0 (the pinned dependency, package.json line 8) getFeeData returns maxPriorityFeePerGas = the node's eth_maxPriorityFeePerGas, or exactly 1,000,000,000 wei when that call fails or is unsupported (abstract-provider.js lines 652-658, 666), and returns null only on a chain without baseFeePerGas. So the `?? parseUnits('0.1', 'gwei')` fallback on line 99 can never run on mainnet or Sepolia, and with an RPC that lacks eth_maxPriorityFeePerGas the check becomes base + 1 gwei > 1 gwei, always true: the relayer refuses every request with 'Network fees exceed the sponsorship limit. Please try later.' Even with a working node, any suggested tip near 1 gwei (common suggestions from gas oracles) makes the default configuration refuse regardless of how low the base fee is. Both tests run with maxFee 3 gwei on anvil (relayer.test.mjs line 38, browser.test.mjs line 41), so the shipped default of 1 gwei has never been exercised; the one 'fees' assertion uses maxFee 1 wei (relayer.test.mjs line 113-114). Effect for registrants under activation: the same site-wide stop as the F-09 finding. Matters only if activated; checklist 1 line 117 would not catch it; a Sepolia rehearsal would, if run with the default fee and a public RPC.

votes.reason:
The code works as the finding says, but the scenario needs an uncommon RPC setup and the effect is small.

What holds:
- /Users/orkhan/Documents/ChatGPT/kilim/registration-relayer/server.mjs:98-100 reads `const fees = await provider.getFeeData(); const tip = fees.maxPriorityFeePerGas ?? parseUnits('0.1', 'gwei'); if (block.baseFeePerGas == null || block.baseFeePerGas + tip > maxFee) throw fail('Network fees exceed the sponsorship limit. Please try later.');`
- maxFee defaults to 1 gwei at lines 52 and 161 (`parseUnits(process.env.KILIM_MAX_FEE_GWEI || '1', 'gwei')`).
- ethers is pinned to 6.17.0 (package.json, and node_modules/ethers/package.json:134). In node_modules/ethers/lib.esm/providers/abstract-provider.js:652-667, a failed `getPriorityFee` call (which maps to `eth_maxPriorityFeePerGas`, provider-jsonrpc.js:586-587) returns null. Then `if (block && block.baseFeePerGas) { maxPriorityFeePerGas = (priorityFee != null) ? priorityFee : BigInt("1000000000");`.
- So on any chain with a base fee, getFeeData never returns a null tip, and the `?? 0.1 gwei` fallback on line 99 is dead code.
- If the configured RPC errors on eth_maxPriorityFeePerGas, the tip becomes exactly 1 gwei. The check is then base + 1 gwei > 1 gwei, which is always true, so every /register request gets a 503.
- I saw this happen live: cloudflare-eth.com answered eth_maxPriorityFeePerGas with -32603 "Internal error".
- Tests never use the default fee. relayer.test.mjs:38 and browser.test.mjs:41 use 3 gwei, and relayer.test.mjs:113 uses 1 wei.

What is refuted or overstated:
- The claim that suggested tips near 1 gwei are common on mainnet does not match live answers today. ethereum-rpc.publicnode.com suggested a 0 tip with base 0.0679 gwei. eth.drpc.org suggested 6.2e-6 gwei. Sepolia via publicnode suggested 0.001 gwei. With a normal provider the default 1 gwei passes easily.
- The failure is fail-closed. No ETH is spent, because the refusal comes before signing, reserving or broadcasting.
- The README (registration-relayer/README.md, Limits) documents this behaviour: "At higher network fees, requests wait by returning an explicit retry-later error". It also says to use a "trusted RPC".
- Sponsorship is not activated ("Both production configs currently leave it empty: sponsorship is NOT activated"). Direct registration stays available in the contract.

Net result: a liveness problem that only appears with a misconfigured RPC, plus a dead fallback and an untested default. It is not a Low-severity issue.

I refute it as a security finding. The code works exactly as the finding says, but the behaviour is deliberate, written down, switched off, and loses no money.

**What the code does**
- /Users/orkhan/Documents/ChatGPT/kilim/registration-relayer/server.mjs:66-67 refuses any overlapping request: `if (busy) throw fail('Another registration is processing. Please retry shortly.', 429); busy = true;`
- server.mjs:85-88 refuses a new wallet until the last journaled transaction has a receipt: `const last = log.state.entries.at(-1); if (last && !await provider.getTransactionReceipt(last.hash)) { ... throw fail('A sponsored registration is pending. Please retry shortly.'); }`
- So at most one sponsored registration lands per block.
- In /Users/orkhan/Documents/ChatGPT/kilim/site/chain.js (around line 842) the site asks for the signature (`walletRequest('eth_signTypedData_v4', ...)`) before it calls the relayer. On a non-OK response it throws `KilimError('Sponsorship', result.error ...)`. Nothing keeps the signature for a retry, so every retry asks the wallet to sign again.

**Why it is refuted**
1. **It is the documented design.** README.md:59-61 says: "Unknown broadcast outcomes reuse the same transaction hash/raw bytes. The service waits for the prior transaction's receipt before accepting another wallet. There are no automatic replacement transactions." README.md:15-16 says requests "wait by returning an explicit retry-later error". README.md:46 says "Do not horizontally scale this service". The service runs one transaction at a time on purpose, so it never uses two nonces at once or signs a second payment, and the lifetime budget stays enforced. That is a safety choice, not an oversight.
2. **It is switched off.** All three chain configs set `"registrationRelayer": ""`: /Users/orkhan/Documents/ChatGPT/kilim/site/chains/1.json:16, 11155111.json:16 and 31337.json:16. README.md:52-53 says: "Both production configs currently leave it empty: sponsorship is NOT activated". With sponsorship off, the site uses self-paid `register()`, so the scenario cannot happen at launch.
3. **No loss and no deadline, even if switched on.**
   - Every refusal at lines 66 and 88 happens before any signing or reservation, so a refused user spends nothing and the sponsor spends nothing.
   - /Users/orkhan/Documents/ChatGPT/kilim/contracts/src/auction/EnglishAuction.sol:137-144 closes registration only before `startsAt` or after 100 registrations: `if (block.timestamp < startsAt || registrationCount >= REGISTRATION_TARGET) revert RegistrationClosed();`. findings.title: The record of the still's format contradicts itself: the artwork toolchain says the WebP 'is what goes on chain', the packer refuses anything but PNG, and nothing records a WebP failure anywhere
findings.description: Evidence for 'WebP is not working': there is none of a marketplace or wallet refusing image/webp. The only thing that does not work is mechanical: pack_page.py accepts PNG only, so a WebP still cannot be packed, and `pnpm -s stores` always passes mint/still.png. Meanwhile the artwork side recorded the opposite decision the same evening (commit 67b23cec, 2026-10-10 18:16 -0400, 'The cover is 3:4 and lossless WebP'): still.mjs says the WebP 'is what goes on chain as the token's image (decided 10 October)' and still.json names still.webp as the file with the PNG as a secondary record. The contracts side (packer, stores script, page test, ARTWORK-ONCHAIN.md, checklist 1) says PNG, and ARTWORK-ONCHAIN.md still describes a 1024 x 1024 PNG that no longer exists (the PNG is now 1536 x 2048, 283,014 bytes). Two 'decided 10 October' records disagree; the packed store follows the PNG one, and that PNG is what pushes KilimOneOfOne over the 8M policy (known blocker, not re-reported). Data for the decision, computed from the files: WebP 110,572 bytes -> 147,432 base64 chars -> PREFIX 147,609 bytes (177 bytes of JSON + the image), 7 chunks (PNG today: 377,529 bytes, 16 chunks; previous PNG: 188,421 bytes, 8 chunks). KilimOneOfOne deployment gas interpolated between the two measured points (6,750,528 at 188,421 B / 8 chunks; 8,087,087 at 377,529 B / 16 chunks; slope 7.07 gas per PREFIX byte including the extra chunk slots, or 6.0 per byte + ~24,700 per chunk) gives about 6.46M to 6.48M for the WebP PREFIX, under the 8M policy with ~1.5M margin; the store cost of the still chunks scales to about 35M (from 44.7M measured at 188 KB) against roughly 90M for today's PNG. The tokenURI(1) answer would be 1,297,402 - (377,352 - 147,432) = 1,067,482 bytes, smaller than the 1,092,954 measured at 4,625,534 gas, so the read falls back under 4.63M. Values that change with a WebP (or any new still): manifest still.size/sha256, prefix size/keccak/chunk list and CREATE2 addresses, hashes.prefixHash, golden.tokenURI; in the config's `expected` block: prefixHash, oneOfOneGolden, still. Values that do not exist to change: no dimension or aspect check anywhere (pack_page.py checks only the 8-byte PNG signature; the page manifest has no width/height), so 3:4 versus square is checked by nothing. To accept a WebP the packer would have to write `data:image/webp;base64,` (line 115) and test a RIFF....WEBP signature (lines 56, 145-146); page.test.mjs line 89 and scripts/stores.mjs line 29 are also PNG-bound. The contract never inspects PREFIX, so no Solidity change is involved. OpenSea's media page names no raster formats ('OpenSea supports most image formats, including SVG, which OpenSea caches as PNG'), so marketplace support for image/webp is neither confirmed nor denied by the source the repo would cite.
findings.scenario: Actor: whoever runs `pnpm -s stores` for the freeze. State: still.json and still.mjs say the token image is still.webp; the packer and the checklist say still.png. Outcome: the store is silently packed with the 283 KB PNG (the only input the toolchain accepts), the `expected` block is printed from it, the deployment of KilimOneOfOne is measured at 8,087,087 and refused by the 8M policy, and nobody can tell from the records which still the artist actually chose; if the policy is then loosened instead, 90M gas of still goes on-chain where 35M would have carried the same pixels.

findings.title: The RPC probe proves gas caps only; its verdict 'renders' and the docs built on it are gas-only claims, while nothing in the repo has ever fetched the 2.6 MB JSON-RPC answer through any node
findings.description: probe-rpc.mjs sends two eth_calls with no `to` (GASLEFT and BURNER) that return 32 bytes each; it measures how much gas a node allows and executes, nothing else. Its verdict text says 'the 1/1: renders, even for callers that send no gas field', and checklist 1 and AUDIT.md quote the result as the evidence that public endpoints will serve the 1/1. But a tokenURI(1) read returns 1,297,402 bytes today, which on the wire is an ABI-encoded hex string of 2,594,946 characters inside the JSON-RPC envelope (about 2.6 MB); response-size or body-size caps on public gateways are a separate failure mode the probe cannot see, and no documented limit was found for publicnode (its site states none) or dRPC (docs unreachable). Neither of the two RPCs the site ships for chain 1 (publicnode, drpc) was exercised at that answer size: the site itself never calls tokenURI(1) (its oneOfOne ABI has no tokenURI; the only tokenURI reads in site tests are motif tokens on a local anvil), and the deploy dry run reads tokenURI(1) inside forge's memory, not over JSON-RPC. The probe's NEEDS line also fixes the 1/1 at the 8M policy ceiling rather than the measured read, which is fine as a bound, but the read at HEAD (larger still) has not been re-measured, so the 'anything below about 5M would blank the 1/1 (it reads at 4.63M)' sentence in checklist 1 is a previous-store number. The checklist marks the marketplaces' own providers as still to do, so this is an unverified claim rather than a false one; what is false is the word 'renders' in the probe output, which the docs then repeat as the meaning of the measurement.
findings.scenario: Actor: a marketplace or wallet indexer reading tokenURI(1) through a gateway that allows 50M gas per eth_call but caps response bodies at a few MB (or times out streaming 2.6 MB). Inputs: eth_call KilimOneOfOne.tokenURI(1). Outcome: the gas probe says 'renders', the token is blank or truncated on that consumer, and nothing can be changed after deployment; the repo's only pre-launch evidence for 'renders' never fetched more than 32 bytes.

findings.title: `data:application/json;utf8,` body is raw and contains 6,644 '+' and 7,190 '/' characters; browsers, Node fetch and Python urllib read it byte for byte, OpenSea documents only the base64 prefix for tokenURI but uses the utf8 prefix in its own contractURI example
findings.description: Data, not a defect found: (1) `;utf8` is not RFC 2397 parameter syntax (parameters are attribute=value); the WHATWG MIME parser drops a bare parameter, so the type resolves to application/json. Rebuilt from the packed store, the exact 1,297,402-byte answer round-trips through Node's `new URL()` (href identical), Node `fetch()` (200, content-type application/json, body identical to the bytes after the 27-byte scheme, JSON.parse yields name/description/image/animation_url, and both nested data URLs fetch to 283,014-byte image/png and 689,881-byte text/html) and Python `urllib.request.urlopen` (application/json, identical body). (2) The body after the comma is not percent-encoded: it holds `{` `}` `"` 16 times, 11 spaces, `:` `,` `;` `=`, and 6,644 `+` (6,636 inside the PNG base64, 5 in the contract-encoded grids piece, 3 in TAIL) and 7,190 `/`. Percent-decoding leaves `+` alone; only a form-style decoder (unquote_plus, PHP urldecode) turns `+` into a space, which would corrupt 6,636 bytes of the still and break the gzip in the page. No such consumer was identified; the packer's `#`/`%` refusal (pack_page.py:104-105, DeployKilim V-16) is the right guard for the decoders that do exist. (3) Sources: OpenSea's metadata-storage page documents `data:application/json;base64,` for tokenURI ('For small collections or generative art, tokenURI or uri can return Base64-encoded JSON with a data:application/json;base64, prefix') and says nothing about utf8; OpenSea's contract-level-metadata page gives `return string.concat("data:application/json;utf8,", json);` as its own example, so the variant is at least one OpenSea recognises for contractURI. The repo's own claim (AUDIT.md: 'It parses under the URL standard... Unproven on a real marketplace at this size: a rehearsal item'; checklist 1:72 asks for written confirmation) is consistent with this evidence; nothing in the repo overclaims.
findings.scenario: Actor: an indexer that recognises tokenURI data URLs by a fixed prefix list containing only `data:application/json;base64,` and `data:application/json,`, or one that decodes the body with a form decoder. State: tokenURI(1) as deployed. Outcome: the 1/1's metadata is skipped, or its still and page are corrupted (6,636 '+' turned to spaces in the PNG; gzip CRC fails in the loader, which then shows nothing), permanently. Likelihood unknown; no consumer doing either was found.
findings.evidence: KilimOneOfOne.sol:36 `/// @dev "data:application/json;utf8," is 27 bytes; the answer ends in the 2 bytes `"}`.`; :258 `mstore(add(ptr, 64), "data:application/json;utf8,")`; :110 `/// @notice The whole token: `data:application/json;utf8,` PREFIX base64(HEAD hex(grids) ' pad) TAIL `"}`.`. pack_page.py:100-106 data_url_text refuses `#` and `%` only. Measured on the packed store: character census of the body outside the unreserved set `{'{': 1, '"': 16, ':': 6, ' ': 11, ',': 6, '/': 7190, ';': 2, '+': 6644, '=': 2, '}': 1}`; PNG base64 has 6,636 '+' and 7,188 '/'; grids piece 5 '+'; TAIL 3 '+', 2 '='. Node: `fetch` status 200 content-type application/json, bytes 1297375 equal true; `new URL(uri).href === uri`; image fetch 200 image/png 283014; anim fetch 200 text/html 689881. Python urllib: 1,297,375 bytes equal, content type application/json. OpenSea metadata-storage (https://docs.opensea.io/docs/metadata-storage): 'Return Base64-encoded JSON directly from the contract.' / `return string.concat("data:application/json;base64,", json);`. OpenSea contract-level-metadata (https://docs.opensea.io/docs/contract-level-metadata): 'You can also return the JSON from the contract:' `return string.concat("data:application/json;utf8,", json);`. I don't think this is a defect. The finding's own text calls itself "Data, not a defect found", and it rates its own severity "None" while reporting it as Low. It names no consumer that actually breaks.

The cited code matches the description. /Users/orkhan/Documents/ChatGPT/kilim/contracts/src/KilimOneOfOne.sol:258 is `mstore(add(ptr, 64), "data:application/json;utf8,")`. Line 36 is `/// @dev "data:application/json;utf8," is 27 bytes`, and line 110 documents the raw layout. So the raw utf8 body is the intended design, not an accident.

The design choice is already recorded and accepted. /Users/orkhan/Documents/ChatGPT/kilim/contracts/AUDIT.md:395, under "Accepted, with the reason", says: "The token JSON is served as `data:application/json;utf8,` raw, not base64. It parses under the URL standard, and base64 would add a third to an answer of 1.1 MB. Unproven on a real marketplace at this size: a rehearsal item". The open risk about marketplaces is also tracked as a pre-deploy step. /Users/orkhan/Documents/ChatGPT/kilim/contracts/checklists/1-pre-deploy.md:72 asks for "written confirmation that it renders ... a `tokenURI` of about 1.1 MB served as `data:application/json;utf8,` (not base64)".

The decoders that standard consumers actually use are guarded. /Users/orkhan/Documents/ChatGPT/kilim/onchain/pack_page.py:100-105 (`data_url_text`) refuses '#' (it would start a fragment) and '%' (it would be percent-decoded): `if '#' in s or '%' in s: raise PackError(...)`.

The '+' and '/' characters are harmless under RFC 3986 percent-decoding and under the WHATWG data: URL processing. The finding's own measurements show this. Node `new URL`, Node `fetch` and Python `urllib` all return the body byte for byte, and both nested data URLs (the image and the page) decode correctly.

The harmful scenario needs one of two hypothetical consumers. The first only recognises a fixed prefix list without the utf8 form. The second decodes the body as a form, turning '+' into spaces. No such consumer is identified, and OpenSea's own contract-level-metadata example uses the same `data:application/json;utf8,` prefix. The scenario cannot be made concrete, the behaviour is documented and accepted, and the remaining uncertainty is already a checklist item. I am therefore classing it as not a new real finding.

TAIL"). /Users/orkhan/Documents/ChatGPT/kilim/onchain/pack_page.py:104-105 refuses only '#' and '%' ("if '#' in s or '%' in s: raise PackError"). That guard is correct: '#' starts a fragment and '%XX' gets percent-decoded, while '+' and '/' are not touched by percent-decoding.

I checked the decoder claim myself in scratchpad/v5-plus/ with a small body holding '+', '/' and a space:
- Node `fetch()` on the data URL returned content-type application/json and the body byte for byte.
- `new URL(u).href === u` was true.
- `decodeURIComponent(body) === body` was true.
- A form decoder (`URLSearchParams`) changed the body.
- Python `urllib.request.urlopen` returned application/json and the identical body. `urllib.parse.unquote` kept the body; `unquote_plus` corrupted it.

So the only way to break it is a consumer that uses a form-style decoder ('+' becomes a space) or that only recognises a fixed list of prefixes. That would hit the 1/1's metadata, still or page, permanently and at no cost to anyone. But no such consumer has been found, and nobody can trigger it. findings.title: Every registration fixture funds wallets with exactly 0.01 ETH and pays no gas: the direct register() path that mainnet wallets will use (balance checked after gas prepayment) is never modelled, and NativeRegistration asserts a post-registration balance the launch path cannot produce
findings.description: TestBase._registerWallets deals each throwaway wallet exactly RESERVE (0.01 ETH) and pranks register(). In a forge test the pranked address pays no gas, so wallet.balance == REGISTRATION_BALANCE at EnglishAuction.sol:142 and the registration passes. On mainnet the contract's own natspec (EnglishAuction.sol:112: 'The balance is checked after gas prepayment') means a wallet holding exactly 0.01 ETH that sends register() itself has gasLimit x maxFee deducted before execution and reverts InsufficientRegistrationBalance; the same wallet passes through registerFor (SponsoredRegistration.t.sol:38 deals 0.01 ETH to the signer, which is the correct mainnet model for the sponsored path only). No test in the suite sets a gas price or funds a direct registrant below 0.01 ETH + gas (grep for txGasPrice/tx.gasprice in test/ returns nothing). NativeRegistration.t.sol:41-43 goes further and asserts that each of the 99 registrants still holds exactly 0.01 ether after registering, and line 123 has registrant(0), holding exactly 0.01 ETH, place a 0.01 ETH opening bid, which is impossible for a self-paying wallet. The asymmetry is disclosed only in the site's error copy (site/auction.html:2197 'Keep at least 0.01 ETH in your wallet after registration gas'); docs/NATIVE-ETH.md:28 ('It checks that the wallet holds at least 0.01 ETH at that moment'), README.md:80 ('A wallet must hold at least 0.01 ETH when it registers'), AUDIT.md:194 and checklists/1-pre-deploy.md:14 ('each holding at least 0.01 ETH when it registers; nothing is deposited') do not say the direct path needs 0.01 ETH plus the transaction's gas, while the sponsored path does not.

The cited lines exist and say what the finding claims.

**What the code says**

- The docs say only "at least 0.01 ETH" and never "plus gas":
  - /Users/orkhan/Documents/ChatGPT/kilim/contracts/docs/NATIVE-ETH.md:28 ("It checks that the wallet holds at least 0.01 ETH at that moment")
  - /Users/orkhan/Documents/ChatGPT/kilim/contracts/README.md:80 ("A wallet must hold at least 0.01 ETH when it registers")
  - /Users/orkhan/Documents/ChatGPT/kilim/contracts/checklists/1-pre-deploy.md:14
  - AUDIT.md:194
- A grep for prepay, "plus gas" and "registration gas" across AUDIT.md, docs, audit and checklists finds nothing. The only disclosure is the site copy at /Users/orkhan/Documents/ChatGPT/kilim/site/chain.js:954.

**Empirical test** (scratch dir f7-gas, anvil 1.8.3, base fee 2 gwei, a minimal contract with the same `msg.sender.balance < 0.01 ether` check, wallet set to exactly 0.01 ETH):
- `eth_call` with no fee fields returned success ("0x").
- `eth_estimateGas` with no fee fields returned 0xaa30.
- `eth_call` with gas 100000 and maxFeePerGas 4 gwei reverted with 0xa7d6a61e (InsufficientRegistrationBalance).
- A real transaction (gas limit 60000, maxFee 4 gwei) mined with status 0x0. It used 21,351 gas, `registered` stayed false, and the balance fell to 0.009941 ETH.

So the mainnet behaviour the finding describes is real. A self-paying wallet needs 0.01 ETH plus gasLimit × effective fee.

**A second effect the finding misses: the site never shows its own error copy for this band.**
- `send()` pre-simulates with a fee-less `eth_call` (chain.js:578-590, :642-644), so the check passes and the wallet sends.
- After the on-chain revert, `failedReason` (chain.js:602-606) re-simulates fee-less at block-1. That passes too, so the user gets the generic message "reverted on-chain. Only its gas was spent." The specific copy at chain.js:954 never appears.

**Impact under launch configuration**
- Who triggers it: any supporter who funds a fresh wallet with exactly the documented 0.01 ETH and uses direct `register()`. Direct is the only path while the relayer is not activated (checklist :112-116).
- What is lost: the gas of one reverted transaction, about 0.00006 ETH at 2-3 gwei, a confusing generic error, and the accuracy of three documents.
- What is not lost: no ETH beyond gas, no motifs, no 1/1, and no effect on the auction's progress. The wallet can top up and retry. The sponsored path behaves as documented.
- Likelihood: plausible for a few registrants on launch day, since the docs invite funding exactly 0.01 ETH. Most wallets will hold more.

On the test-suite side the gap is real: no test sets a gas price, so nothing pins the "after gas" behaviour. But the fixtures are not wrong for what they test, because forge cannot charge gas to a pranked caller. That gap is test coverage and documentation, not a contract defect. Rated Low.

Confirmed:

The second opening bid fails `_isNewWinningBid` and reverts with `revert BidTooLow(minimumBid());` (src/auction/EnglishAuction.sol:211-212). That happens before the RewardSlippage check (KilimAuction.sol:115) and before `_collectBid` (KilimAuction.sol:128).
- /Users/orkhan/Documents/ChatGPT/kilim/contracts/test/KilimAuction.t.sol:577 is a bare `vm.expectRevert();` before `auction.claimPrize(address(receiver))`. The real reason comes from `_safeMint(to, TOKEN_ID)` (src/KilimOneOfOne.sol:95), i.e. ERC721InvalidReceiver. Line 644 (claimMotifs to a rejecting receiver) is also bare.
- AUDIT.md:194 and :197 cite these suites for the behaviours named in the finding.

Why it is Info, not Low:
1. Swapping BidTooLow for NonWholeUnitBid is killed elsewhere. KilimAuction.t.sol:106 has `vm.expectRevert(abi.encodeWithSelector(EnglishAuction.BidTooLow.selector, RESERVE))`, and :118 and :1203 also pin BidTooLow. The finding admits this.
2. Changing `if (prizeClaimed)` to `if (!prizeClaimed)` is killed in the same test. The later `auction.claimPrize(CAROL); assertEq(oneOfOne.ownerOf(1), CAROL);` (KilimAuction.t.sol:586-587) would revert.
3. Swapping the NotSettled and Unauthorized checks (KilimAuction.sol:214-216) changes nothing in this test's state. The auction is settled and msg.sender is the winner, so neither check fires either way. It is not a surviving mutant.

What remains is that this test alone does not show the reason the user sees. That is a weakness in the tests, with no impact on security or funds.

The cited lines exist and do what the finding says. This is a gap in how tightly the tests pin the revert, not a contract defect. No ETH, 1/1, motif, auction outcome or documented statement is at risk, and the finding's suggested fix for the KilimAuction lines is wrong.

1. NativeRegistration.t.sol:117-128, testRegisteredWalletCanStartAndCompetingOpeningBidReverts. Line 124 is "vm.expectRevert();" placed before "start(BOB);", so any revert passes. docs/NATIVE-ETH.md:59 says "If two opening bids race, the second must meet the new minimum or it reverts", and :133 cites this file for "competing opening bids".

2. KilimAuction.t.sol:570-588, testRejectingWinnerCannotBlockSettlementOrProceeds. Line 577 is "vm.expectRevert();" placed before "auction.claimPrize(address(receiver))". Line 644 does the same in testRejectingReceiverDoesNotConsumeMotifCredits. AUDIT.md:198 cites this file for "a winner that rejects the 1/1 or burns gas cannot block settlement or proceeds".

What I ran: I copied src, test and script into scratchpad/f9mut, linked node_modules, and ran forge 1.8.3 offline. Nothing was written into the repository.
- Baseline: both tests pass.
- Mutant A: EnglishAuction.sol:212 changed from "revert BidTooLow(minimumBid());" to "revert NonWholeUnitBid();". NativeRegistration:124 still PASSES, which confirms that test does not pin the reason. The full non-deploy suite still kills the mutant with 4 tests: testOpeningBidMustMeetTheReserve (:106), testMinimumBidRoundsUpToWholeUnit, testOversizedBidRejectedBeforeUpstreamMultiplication and testFuzzMinimumBidIsTheSmallestAcceptedWholeUnit. That is more coverage than the finding's "killed elsewhere only by :106".
- Mutant B: KilimAuction.sol:217 changed from "if (prizeClaimed)" to "if (!prizeClaimed)". Lines 577-580 still pass, but the same test fails at :586 with PrizeAlreadyClaimed(). The finding says the same. This mutant is not missed by the suite.

Impact: no one can trigger a loss, and nothing is lost on launch day. The only cost is weaker regression protection if the code is later edited. The contracts are immutable and these tests are only checks before deploy, so in practice the gap is a slightly overstated "tested" claim in the documents.

The suggested fix for the KilimAuction lines is wrong. I applied "vm.expectRevert(abi.encodeWithSelector(IERC721Errors.ERC721InvalidReceiver.selector, address(receiver)))" at :577 and :644, and both tests FAIL with "NFT rejected != ERC721InvalidReceiver(...)". The cause: the mock test/mocks/Receiver.sol:26 reverts with "require(!rejecting, \"NFT rejected\");", and OpenZeppelin's _checkOnERC721Received passes that reason up to the caller unchanged. vm.expectRevert(bytes("NFT rejected")) passes, and with that pin mutant B now fails at :577 itself ("PrizeAlreadyClaimed() != NFT rejected"). The NativeRegistration fix, abi.encodeWithSelector(BidTooLow.selector, 0.011 ether), passes on the unmutated code and kills mutant A at :124 ("NonWholeUnitBid() != BidTooLow(1.1e16)").

findings.title: Site's 'Claim the 1/1' button only ever claims to the connected wallet, the one address that just failed to receive it; the promised 'claim to another address' has no input
findings.description: After a settlement that emitted PrizeDeliveryFailed the site shows the winner the button 'Claim the 1/1' (auction.js:365) and the sentence 'You won, but the 1/1 could not be sent to this wallet. Claim it to another address.' (auction.js:360). The button calls CHAIN.claimPrize(undefined, ...) (auction.js:239), and chain.js resolves an undefined recipient to the connected account (chain.js:744-749, 1046), so the transaction is claimPrize(self). The contract mints to `to` with _safeMint (KilimAuction.sol:213-224 -> KilimOneOfOne.sol:90-96), and ERC721Utils.checkOnERC721Received reverts with ERC721InvalidReceiver for any `to` with code that has no hook (ERC721Utils.sol:34-42). The site's simulation surfaces that as 'Can't receive NFTs ... Claim to another address' with the action 'claimTo' (chain.js:980), and act() implements 'claimTo' by focusing #claimto (auction.js:67), the 'Claim to' input of the motif section (auction.part.html:149-152), which is inside <details id=claimmanual> shown only while credits > 0 (auction.js:357) and is ignored by the prize button anyway. There is no recipient field in the #account section (auction.part.html:163-172). deliverPrizeToWinner is not in the site at all (W-09) and would revert for the same wallet since it mints to the winner's own address (KilimAuction.sol:229-236).
findings.scenario: Actor: the winner, using W1 (an EIP-7702 EOA delegated to code with receive() but no onERC721Received) or W3 without a fallback handler (Safe whose fallback returns empty data; the decode failure reverts inside KilimOneOfOne.mint and is caught by _afterSettle's try at KilimAuction.sol:196-199). Step: settle() emits PrizeDeliveryFailed; the winner opens the site, reads 'Claim it to another address', presses 'Claim the 1/1'. Outcome: the simulation fails with ERC721InvalidReceiver every time; the 'Choose another address' button focuses a hidden, unrelated input; the winner cannot name a recipient from the site and must hand-craft claimPrize(to) on an explorer. The W1 wallet alone has a second exit the site never mentions: clear the delegation (type-4 tx to address 0) and press the button again.

The scenario is concrete: a Safe with no ERC-721 fallback handler, or a 7702-delegated EOA whose delegate has no onERC721Received, wins. settle() then emits PrizeDeliveryFailed (try/catch in _afterSettle), and the site's 'Claim the 1/1' button cannot succeed. I rate it Low rather than the reported Medium. Nothing is lost or stuck for good: claimPrize has no deadline and no admin, prizeClaimed stays false, and the winner, still the only allowed caller, can call claimPrize(to) to any accepting address from a block explorer or the Safe transaction builder. The post-deploy checklist already plans for the artist to help with exactly this. The button also works in the gas-only failure case (a hook needing more than PRIZE_GAS), because the winner's own transaction carries more gas. The finding is a UX gap in the recovery path for an uncommon wallet setup, not a contract flaw.

- /Users/orkhan/Documents/ChatGPT/kilim/site/auction.js:239 is `await CHAIN.claimPrize(undefined, { onStep: stepper('acctsteps') })`.
- /Users/orkhan/Documents/ChatGPT/kilim/site/chain.js:745 is `var r = to ? String(to).trim() : (who || S.acct);`, so the recipient is always the connected account. chain.js:1046 encodes `claimPrize(recipient(to))`.
- auction.js:360 shows 'You won, but the 1/1 could not be sent to this wallet. Claim it to another address.' auction.js:365 shows #prize only when `ph === 'settled' && a.youWin && !a.prizeClaimed`.
- chain.js:980 maps ERC721InvalidReceiver to the action 'claimTo'. auction.js:67 handles that by focusing `$('claimto')`. That input is the motif 'Claim to' field (auction.part.html:152). It sits inside `<details id="claimmanual">`, shown only when `credits > 0` (auction.js:357), and the prize handler never reads it.
- #account (auction.part.html:163-174) has no recipient input.

On the contract side, KilimAuction.claimPrize(to) (lines 213-222) lets only the winner choose any valid `to`. KilimOneOfOne.mint uses `_safeMint` (lines 90-96). deliverPrizeToWinner (lines 229-236) mints only to the winner's own address. So a winner whose wallet refuses the token (contract without onERC721Received, an EIP-7702 delegate without the hook) cannot get the 1/1 from the site. The promised 'claim it to another address' does not exist in the UI.

Why Low and not Medium:
1. Nothing is lost. claimPrize has no deadline and only the winner can call it, so the 1/1 stays claimable forever. Any explorer 'Write contract' call to claimPrize(to) works. 3-post-deploy.md:82 already has the artist 'help the winner call claimPrize(to)'.
2. No gas is wasted. Every write is simulated with eth_call before the wallet is asked (chain.js:3, 578-589, 637). The failing claim stops at simulation and never reaches signing.
3. Only one person can be affected, the winner, and only if settle() emitted PrizeDeliveryFailed. An ordinary EOA or a standard Safe with its default fallback handler accepts the token at settle, so the likelihood on launch day is low.
4. What is lost is a true statement on the page (the copy promises a path that is not there) and the winner's time.

A launch-state caveat: today's published build cannot reach this code. /Users/orkhan/Documents/ChatGPT/kilim/site/build.py:341 uses `'auction-info.part.html' if not dev else 'auction.part.html'` and line 346 does the same for auction-info.js vs auction.js. site/dist/orkhanart/auction.html has no id="prize" (grep count 0); only auction.dev.html has it. AUDIT.md W-02 records that no public build can produce a bidding page yet. The defect becomes live when auction.js is published for launch, which W-02 says must happen.

W-09 (AUDIT.md:390) covers only the missing deliverPrizeToWinner button, so this finding is new. The site tests do not cover it: chain.test.mjs:420-430 calls claimPrize through the API only, and no page test touches #prize.

findings.title: A Safe (W3) cannot use the site at all: wallet discovery is EIP-6963/window.ethereum only, no WalletConnect and no Safe App manifest, while the runbook tells bidders a Safe is fine
findings.description: The site connects only to providers announced through EIP-6963 or injected as window.ethereum (rpc.js:115-140; chain.js:3 'connected wallet (EIP-1193, found through EIP-6963)'). A deployed Safe has no injected provider; it reaches dapps through WalletConnect or by being loaded as a Safe App (iframe + SDK). Neither exists in the site (grep of chain.js and rpc.js for walletconnect / safe app / iframe: no hits). The code-wallet routing at chain.js:1039, which sends a wallet with code to register() instead of the sponsored signature, is therefore unreachable for a Safe. Checklist 1-pre-deploy.md:190 tells bidders to 'Bid only from a wallet that can send transactions later: an EOA, a Safe or a smart wallet', and 1-pre-deploy.md:123 plans a website walk-through 'with several wallets including a Safe'; 1-pre-deploy.md:161 itself notes 'A Safe still needs a connection path (WalletConnect or a Safe Apps shim)' as an unchecked item. Every step (register, bid with the 1,500,000 fixed gas the contract's InsufficientGas floor relies on, claimMotifs, withdrawRefund, claimPrize) would have to be built by hand in Safe's Transaction Builder. In the contracts a Safe 1.4.1 with the default CompatibilityFallbackHandler works at every step (receive() is a single event, well inside REFUND_GAS at EnglishAuction.sol:244; the hook returns the selector and fits PRIZE_GAS, PrizeGasBudget.t.sol:326-335), so the gap is entirely in the site.
findings.scenario: Actor: a collector with a 2-of-3 Safe 1.4.1 and 5 ETH. Step: opens auction.html to register before the 100-wallet gate closes. Outcome: no wallet to pick (the Safe is not announced); the collector either cannot participate or builds register()/bid()/claimMotifs() calldata by hand in the Safe UI, where the bid's gas estimate is taken before other bids land and can fall under the 452,380-left floor (EnglishAuction.sol:243) that the site's fixed 1,500,000 gas (chain.js:18, 705) exists to avoid.

The facts are right: the site has no WalletConnect and no Safe App path. /Users/orkhan/Documents/ChatGPT/kilim/site/rpc.js:115 reads "// EIP-6963 wallet discovery, with window.ethereum as the fallback." Lines 137-138 listen for 'eip6963:announceProvider' and send 'eip6963:requestProvider'. Lines 141-143 then fall back to G.ethereum. A grep of /Users/orkhan/Documents/ChatGPT/kilim/site (leaving out _iterations) for walletconnect, safe-apps and safeapp finds nothing that matters. The only hit is site/build.py:35, MOTIF_STORE = ... 'manifest.json', which is the motif store and not a Safe App manifest.

The finding's main claims do not hold as written, though:
(1) "A Safe cannot use the site at all" and "the code-wallet routing at chain.js:1039 is unreachable for a Safe" are overstated. Some injected wallets act as a Safe address and show up through EIP-6963 or window.ethereum: Rabby can import a Safe and send its transactions to Safe for co-signing, and other smart-account wallets like Ambire also inject. Such a wallet passes the checks at rpc.js:124 (provider.request is a function). Its account has code, so chain.js:1039, "if (cfg.registrationRelayer && !(await hasCode(S.acct))) return sponsoredRegister(o);", sends it to the ordinary register() transaction. EIP-7702 EOAs and injected smart wallets reach that same branch (chain.js:1036 names both). So the path is reachable. What is missing is one way to connect, not all of them.
(2) Nothing is at risk. The finding itself says the contracts work for a Safe at every step. A Safe owner who skips the site can still build each call in Safe's Transaction Builder. The gas worry there comes from the user setting their own gas, not from a flaw in the contracts.
(3) The project already tracks the gap. /Users/orkhan/Documents/ChatGPT/kilim/contracts/checklists/1-pre-deploy.md:161 reads "A Safe still needs a connection path (WalletConnect or a Safe Apps shim)." Line 123 plans a website walk-through "with several wallets including a Safe". That item cannot be checked off until a connection path exists, so the runbook would catch this before launch.

What is left is a missing product feature and a slightly loose bidder line at 1-pre-deploy.md:190 ("an EOA, a Safe or a smart wallet"). It is not a security flaw and does not deserve Medium. The scenario's claim that a Safe is "unable to participate" holds only for a Safe owner who has no injecting wallet such as Rabby and will not use the Transaction Builder.
votes.fix: Optional, as a feature: add a WalletConnect connector, or a Safe Apps provider plus a manifest, before launch. Or change 1-pre-deploy.md:190 and the site copy to say that a Safe connects through an injecting wallet that supports Safes (for example Rabby) or builds the calls by hand, and give the gas limits to use (bid 1,500,000, as at chain.js:18 and 705).

votes.reason:
The cited lines are real and the finding reads them correctly. /Users/orkhan/Documents/ChatGPT/kilim/site/rpc.js:115-145 (`// EIP-6963 wallet discovery, with window.ethereum as the fallback.`) is the only way the site finds a wallet. It listens for `eip6963:announceProvider`, sends `eip6963:requestProvider`, and after 300 ms adds `G.ethereum` if one exists. /Users/orkhan/Documents/ChatGPT/kilim/site/chain.js:3 says the same ("connected wallet (EIP-1193, found through EIP-6963)"). With no wallet the page shows "No wallet found in this browser. Install a wallet extension, or open this page in your wallet app's browser." (site/src-auction.html:1711). A grep of site/, launch/ and registration-relayer/ finds no WalletConnect, no Safe Apps SDK and no Safe App manifest (the only manifest.json hits are the motif store).

The project already knows. TEAM.md:82 says "Not done: WalletConnect / Safe (needs a relay and a project id)". Checklist line 161 has the unchecked item "A Safe still needs a connection path (WalletConnect or a Safe Apps shim)". Line 123 plans a Sepolia walk-through "with several wallets including a Safe", and line 190 tells bidders "an EOA, a Safe or a smart wallet" is fine. Chain.js:1039 (`if (cfg.registrationRelayer && !(await hasCode(S.acct))) return sponsoredRegister(o);`) does route a wallet with code to an ordinary register(), but only after a provider has connected it.

The finding also misses something. If a Safe App manifest were added, the planned hosting headers would still block it. /Users/orkhan/Documents/ChatGPT/kilim/launch/HOSTING-HEADERS.md:23 sets `frame-ancestors 'none'` and :54 sets `X-Frame-Options: DENY`, so the Safe{Wallet} iframe could not load /kilim.

I did not test wallet behaviour here; that would need a live Safe. Safe{Wallet} reaches dapps through WalletConnect or as a Safe App in an iframe, and has no injected provider of its own. A Safe owner can still get through without the site changing: a wallet that imports a Safe and announces it over EIP-6963 (Rabby does this, according to its own documentation; I did not test it), or Safe's Transaction Builder with hand-built calldata.

Why Low and not Medium:
- Who is affected: only collectors who insist on bidding from a Safe or another contract wallet with no injected provider. Nobody can trigger it against anyone else.
- What is lost: no ETH, motif or 1/1 is at risk. The contracts accept a Safe at every step, as the finding itself shows: the refund at EnglishAuction.sol:244 with REFUND_GAS, and prize delivery to a Safe in PrizeGasBudget.t.sol:334-335. Refunds can always be withdrawn later.
- What it costs: reach, and a possible bad bid. A collector may skip the auction, or build bid() by hand with a gas estimate that leaves too little gas for the refund. Such a bid reverts on the contract's InsufficientGas check before anything changes, so it costs gas and the bid is lost, but no funds.
- The documents: line 190 is true for the contracts but misleading for the site. Line 123 is a planned rehearsal step that would fail and surface the gap before launch. The register gate needs 100 wallets, so a few Safe users being shut out is unlikely to stall it.

So the impact is reduced reach plus a document that overstates the site, not loss of value.
