findings.title: Counterfactual smart accounts (W4) are routed to the sponsored signature they cannot pass; the site has no direct register() choice and tells them to 'sign it again'
findings.description: register() in the site decides the path by hasCode(S.acct) alone (chain.js:819-823, 1039). A counterfactual ERC-4337 account (Coinbase Smart Wallet, Safe4337 before first use) has no code, so with a relayer configured the site asks for eth_signTypedData_v4 and posts the signature to the sponsor (chain.js:824-868). The contract takes the ECDSA path for an address without code (SignatureChecker.sol:49-51) and the account address is not the owner key's address (an ERC-6492 wrapper is not understood either), so registerFor reverts InvalidRegistrationSignature (EnglishAuction.sol:121-130). The site explains that as 'Sign it again from the wallet you want to register' (chain.js:955), or as a 'Sponsorship' error when the relayer's simulation rejects first. There is no button to register with a plain transaction instead, although 1-pre-deploy.md:148 requires 'Offer register() directly, also when a sponsor is configured (F-09)' and AUDIT.md:276 records that 'the site now routes such wallets to register()' (true only for wallets that already have code). The limitation is disclosed only in registration-relayer/README.md:20. Mitigation: the relayer 'is not activated' (NATIVE-ETH.md:131); with no relayer, register() goes through the account's bundler with initCode, deploys it and registers in one UserOp (EnglishAuction.sol:114-116, 136-145 check only the balance of the then-deployed account).
findings.scenario: Actor: a collector with a never-used Coinbase Smart Wallet holding 0.05 ETH, on a launch where the sponsor is switched on. Step: presses 'Register interest — gas sponsored'. Outcome: signs, the relayer or the contract refuses the signature, the page says to sign again; there is no path on the page to register with a transaction; the collector never counts toward the 100.
findings.evidence: chain.js:1039 `if (cfg.registrationRelayer && !(await hasCode(S.acct))) return sponsoredRegister(o);`; chain.js:821-822 `var code = await read.request({ method: 'eth_getCode', params: [address, 'latest'] }); return typeof code === 'string' && code !== '0x' && code !== '0x0';`; SignatureChecker.sol:49-51 `if (signer.code.length == 0) { (address recovered, ECDSA.RecoverError err, ) = ECDSA.tryRecoverCalldata(hash, signature); return err == ECDSA.RecoverError.NoError && recovered == signer;`; chain.js:955 `case 'InvalidRegistrationSignature': set('Signature not accepted', 'The registration message was not signed by this wallet, or was signed for another network. Sign it again from the wallet you want to register. Nothing was taken.', null, null); break;`; 1-pre-deploy.md:148 `Offer register() directly, also when a sponsor is configured (F-09).`; AUDIT.md:74 `| F-09 | Low | Wallets with code ... cannot use the sponsored path, and the site offers no direct register() button when a sponsor is configured. |`; AUDIT.md:276 `a wallet with code cannot use the sponsored signature and registers directly (the site now routes such wallets to register())`; registration-relayer/README.md:20 `Undeployed/counterfactual wallets are not supported.`; NATIVE-ETH.md:131 `It is not activated.`
findings.fix: Offer both actions on the page when a sponsor is configured (sponsored signature and 'register with a transaction'), or fall through to register() when the sponsored path returns InvalidRegistrationSignature; disclose in the site copy and NATIVE-ETH.md that undeployed accounts must register with a transaction.

The code path is described correctly, but the scenario only happens if a sponsor is switched on, and the launch configuration has no sponsor. Refuting points:

(1) The branch at /Users/orkhan/Documents/ChatGPT/kilim/site/chain.js:1039 is `if (cfg.registrationRelayer && !(await hasCode(S.acct))) return sponsoredRegister(o);`. Every built config has `"registrationRelayer":""` for mainnet (chainId 1) and Sepolia: /Users/orkhan/Documents/ChatGPT/kilim/site/index.html:840, site/src-auction.html:1219, site/afterglow.html:1056 and site/dist/orkhanart/afterglow.html:1069. An empty string is falsy, so the site always falls through to `simpleWrite('Register interest — no deposit; gas applies', cfg.auction, FA.register.encode([]), o)` at chain.js:1040.

(2) The docs say the sponsor is off. /Users/orkhan/Documents/ChatGPT/kilim/contracts/docs/NATIVE-ETH.md:129 ends with "It is not activated." /Users/orkhan/Documents/ChatGPT/kilim/registration-relayer/README.md:20 says "Undeployed/counterfactual wallets are not supported."

(3) With no sponsor, a counterfactual account calls register() through its own bundler. The contract checks only `wallet.balance < REGISTRATION_BALANCE` and `registered[wallet]` on msg.sender (/Users/orkhan/Documents/ChatGPT/kilim/contracts/src/auction/EnglishAuction.sol:114-116, 136-145), so a UserOp with initCode deploys the account and registers it. The collector the finding describes is not blocked.

(4) Even if a sponsor were turned on, nothing is lost: registerFor reverts before any state change (EnglishAuction.sol:121-130), and the error copy says "Nothing was taken" (chain.js:955). The user can still call register() directly from their own wallet. The cost is a UX dead end, not a loss of funds or a broken invariant.

(5) The missing direct register() button when a sponsor is configured is already recorded as F-09 (/Users/orkhan/Documents/ChatGPT/kilim/contracts/AUDIT.md:74) and is pinned in /Users/orkhan/Documents/ChatGPT/kilim/contracts/checklists/1-pre-deploy.md:148: "Offer `register()` directly, also when a sponsor is configured (F-09)."

The only new detail is that the hasCode routing does not catch counterfactual accounts, so the AUDIT.md:276 wording "the site now routes such wallets to `register()`" is incomplete. That only matters if the sponsor is ever switched on, and checklist item :148 already covers that case. Since the scenario cannot happen on the configured launch, this is not a live defect.
votes.fix: Nothing is needed for the launch as configured, because there is no sponsor. Before ever setting registrationRelayer, finish checklist item 1-pre-deploy.md:148 (F-09): offer a 'register with a transaction' button next to the sponsored one, or fall back to register() when the sponsored path returns InvalidRegistrationSignature. Also reword AUDIT.md:276 to say the routing covers only wallets that already have code; counterfactual accounts must register directly.
votes.covering_test: No existing test covers this. I checked the cited lines and they match what the finding says.

- /Users/orkhan/Documents/ChatGPT/kilim/site/auction.js:224: `try { await ensureConnected(); await CHAIN.withdrawRefund(undefined, { onStep: stepper('acctsteps') }); ...`. The button always passes `undefined` as the recipient.

- chain.js:1044: `withdrawRefund: async function (to, o) { ... FA.withdrawRefund.encode([recipient(to)]) ... }`.
- chain.js:960: `case 'EthTransferFailed': set('ETH payment failed', 'Your withdrawal remains available. Choose a recipient that can receive ETH.', null, null)`. The message tells the user to choose a recipient but gives no action and no field.
- /Users/orkhan/Documents/ChatGPT/kilim/site/auction.part.html:148: `<button class="ghost hidden" id="withdraw" disabled>Withdraw refund</button>` stands alone. The only recipient input on the page is `claimto` (line 152), and it belongs to the motif claim.
- /Users/orkhan/Documents/ChatGPT/kilim/contracts/src/auction/EnglishAuction.sol:155-163: `withdrawRefund(address to)` accepts any recipient that passes `_validateRecipient`, which rejects only zero, the auction itself and, through KilimAuction, the token contracts.
- EnglishAuction.sol:282-283: `_pay` does `(bool paid,) = payable(to).call{value: amount}(""); if (!paid) revert EthTransferFailed();`.
- EnglishAuction.sol:242-250: a refund is deferred when the push payment fails, whether from running out of the 150,000 REFUND_GAS or from a refusal.

So the claim holds. A wallet whose refund was deferred because it refuses ETH gets EthTransferFailed every time it presses the page's button. The page then tells it to choose a recipient, which the page does not let it do. That instruction is a false statement on the site. A wallet deferred only for gas is fine: the withdrawal runs with the whole transaction's gas and succeeds.

Impact:
- No ETH is lost. The refund stays in `refunds[msg.sender]`, and the contract call `withdrawRefund(to)` with another address works, for example from Etherscan's write tab or the wallet's own transaction builder.
- Only the bidder can trigger this, and only with a contract wallet that refuses plain ETH yet can connect to the site and call the auction. MetaMask's EIP-7702 delegate, Safe and Solady-style receivers all accept ETH, so on launch day this is unlikely and would affect a handful of wallets at most.
- The harm is a page that cannot complete its own advertised fallback and a message that misdirects. That is a usability and accuracy defect, not a funds or permanence issue, and it can be fixed after deployment because the site is off-chain. I rate it Low (it could also be argued down to Info). I accept the finding as real; it is distinct from F-19, which covers a contract that cannot call `withdrawRefund` at all.

I ran no empirical test: the behaviour follows directly from the code paths quoted above. I only read files and wrote nothing to the repository.

findings.title: The 'deployer must be a plain account without an EIP-7702 delegation' rule is enforced by nothing in the deploy script
findings.description: Checklist 1-pre-deploy.md:43 ('The deployer must be a plain account: a Safe or another contract wallet cannot be the deployer with this script'), :40 ('it has no contract code on Ethereum ... checked 2026-09-19') and :214 ('No key used for the launch may carry an EIP-7702 delegation') describe a precondition. The script checks the deployer's address (DeployKilim.s.sol:789), its latest nonce against the published one (451-457), that no transaction is pending (548-549) and that the contracts' code exists (502), but never `c.deployer.code.length` (grep for 'deployer.*code' and 'delegation' in the script: none). A delegation does not change the CREATE addresses (vm.computeCreateAddress at 459 and 499 is nonce-based) so the three creations would still land; the exposure is that the delegate's code may let a third party send from the wallet (consuming the published nonce, or creating a contract at n+2 that becomes both tokens' minter, the case PrizeGasBudget.t.sol:485-515 (b) demonstrates), and that a wallet UI sending a type-4 self-authorization consumes two nonces at once, invalidating the published nonce. The 2026-09-19 code check is a one-off hand check; a delegation can be added at any time before the deploy transaction and `--ledger` signing does not exclude it.
findings.scenario: Actor: the artist, with MetaMask having 'upgraded' orkhanart.eth to a smart account at some point before the deploy day. Step: runs the contracts phase. Outcome: the script passes every check and deploys from a delegated account; whatever the delegate permits (session keys, sponsored batches) can now also move the treasury's proceeds and royalties, and the runbook's statement that the deployer is a plain account was never verified by the tool that deploys.
findings.evidence: DeployKilim.s.sol:789 `if (c.deployer != LAUNCH_DEPLOYER) revert Refused("mainnet launch value: deployer");`; DeployKilim.s.sol:451-457 `uint256 nonce = vm.getNonce(c.deployer); if (c.deployerNonce != NO_NONCE_CHECK) { if (nonce != c.deployerNonce) { ... revert Refused("deployer nonce"); } _requireNothingPending(c.deployer, nonce); }`; DeployKilim.s.sol:459 `address predicted = vm.computeCreateAddress(c.deployer, nonce + 2);`; 1-pre-deploy.md:43 `The deployer must be a plain account: a Safe or another contract wallet cannot be the deployer with this script.`; 1-pre-deploy.md:214 `No key used for the launch may carry an EIP-7702 delegation.`
findings.fix: In deployContracts and runAuction, refuse when `c.deployer.code.length != 0` (a 7702 delegation shows as 23 bytes 0xef0100||address) and record the check in 2-deploy.md.

The factual claim holds. Grepping for "7702", "delegat" and "ef0100" finds nothing. deployContracts checks the nonce: lines 451-457 `uint256 nonce = vm.getNonce(c.deployer); if (c.deployerNonce != NO_NONCE_CHECK) { if (nonce != c.deployerNonce) { ... revert Refused("deployer nonce"); } _requireNothingPending(c.deployer, nonce); }`. _requireLaunchSettings checks the address: line 789 `if (c.deployer != LAUNCH_DEPLOYER) revert Refused("mainnet launch value: deployer");`. Neither looks at the deployer's code. The runbook states the rule only as hand items: /Users/orkhan/Documents/ChatGPT/kilim/contracts/checklists/1-pre-deploy.md:43 "The deployer must be a plain account: a Safe or another contract wallet cannot be the deployer with this script." and :214 "No key used for the launch may carry an EIP-7702 delegation." I could not refute the gap, but I downgrade it from Low to Info for three reasons.
(1) The harm in the scenario comes from the wallet's own delegation, not from the missing script check. A permissive delegate exposes the treasury and royalties whenever the delegation exists. Those funds only move at settle or withdrawProceeds, days after the deploy, and a delegation added after the deploy is untouched by any deploy-time check. So the fix covers one moment.
(2) The one deploy-time effect the finding names, a type-4 self-authorization using up an extra nonce, is already caught: the published-nonce check at 451-457 reverts with "deployer nonce".
(3) A third party sending from the wallet, or CREATE-ing at n+2 to capture the minter role, needs a delegate that lets outsiders act. A typical wallet "smart account" delegate only runs calls the EOA signed, so that case means the wallet is already compromised. Spotting it at deploy is defence in depth, not a contract flaw.

The fix is cheap and matches a documented precondition. It adds an automated check to an otherwise manual step; it does not close a vulnerability.

votes.reason:
I checked the cited lines and they say what the finding says. /Users/orkhan/Documents/ChatGPT/kilim/contracts/script/DeployKilim.s.sol:786-789 is `_requireLaunchSettings`. It checks only the deployer's address: `if (c.deployer != LAUNCH_DEPLOYER) revert Refused("mainnet launch value: deployer");`. deployContracts (444-478) adds two more checks. It compares the nonce with the published one (451-457) and refuses a pending transaction (548-549, via eth_getTransactionCount "pending"). It then predicts the addresses from the nonce alone (`vm.computeCreateAddress(c.deployer, nonce + 2)`, 459). A grep for code.length/7702/delegat in the script finds code checks only on store chunks (250, 280, 395, 775), on the token and auction addresses (502, 505) and on 921. None looks at the deployer.

The runbook states the rule. /Users/orkhan/Documents/ChatGPT/kilim/contracts/checklists/1-pre-deploy.md:214: "No key used for the launch may carry an EIP-7702 delegation." Line 43: "The deployer must be a plain account". Line 40 makes a factual claim: "checked 2026-09-19, it has no contract code on Ethereum".

I tested the empirical side with read-only calls. eth_getCode for 0xd6647Eeec0c8D810C546f2ab8e025D4664d833Ac at "latest" returned the same result on publicnode, mevblocker and drpc: `0xef010063c0c19a282a1b52b07dd5a65b58948a07dae32b`. That is an EIP-7702 delegation designator. The block number was 0x18f45ae and the nonce 0x61e (1566). The delegate 0x63c0c19a282a1b52b07dd5a65b58948a07dae32b has 11,185 bytes of code. Its eip712Domain(), NAME() and VERSION() calls return "EIP7702StatelessDeleGator" and "1.3.0", which is MetaMask's smart-account delegator.

So the wallet that will deploy, be the treasury and receive royalties is delegated today. The precondition in :214/:43 is already broken, and the claim at :40 is now false. As written, the script would pass every check and deploy from this account.

The three CREATEs would still land at the predicted addresses, because a delegated EOA still sends ordinary transactions and nonces advance as usual. So the auction, the motifs and the 1/1 contracts are not directly at risk. The exposure is to the launch key:
- While the delegation is in place, an off-chain signature can move the account's funds: a signed delegation redeemed through MetaMask's DelegationManager, or a signed UserOperation. One phishing signature could then take the withdrawn proceeds and the royalties, plus anything else in the treasury's balance.
- The treasury address is permanent in the contracts, which raises the stakes.
- Wallet UIs send self-sponsored type-4 transactions, both to upgrade the account and to switch it back. Each one uses two nonces, so doing it after the nonce is published would break the published nonce. The pending-nonce check would refuse, but the published addresses would be lost.

Part of the original scenario is less likely with this particular delegate. As far as I know, DeleGator executions are calls and do not CREATE, so a third party creating a contract at n+2 is unlikely here. Proceeds are pulled by the treasury itself through `withdrawProceeds` (EnglishAuction.sol:181-182, a full-gas `.call` at 282), so code at the treasury does not block payment.

Triggering a loss needs the artist to sign something malicious. But a decided security rule is broken right now, nothing in the tool that deploys catches it, and the runbook states something untrue. That puts it above the reported Low; I rate it Medium.
votes.fix:
First, revoke the delegation before the nonce is published. Send a type-4 authorization to address(0) and expect the nonce to move by 2 if the wallet sends it itself. Then confirm with `cast code 0xd6647Eeec0c8D810C546f2ab8e025D4664d833Ac` that the result is 0x.

In the script, add to `_requireLaunchSettings` (DeployKilim.s.sol, after line 789), or at the top of deployContracts, deployAuction and runStore:
`if (c.deployer.code.length != 0) revert Refused("deployer has code (EIP-7702 delegation or contract wallet)");`
Apply the same check to `c.auction.treasury`; at launch it is the same address.

In the runbook, correct the stale claim at 1-pre-deploy.md:40. In 2-deploy.md, add a "(script)" line: deployer and treasury have no code.

Also add a fork smoke test pinned to the current mainnet block. It should show that the script refuses the live deployer today, since the address is delegated as of block 0x18f45ae.

findings.known: R-08 (AUDIT.md:257, stale numbers) / AUDIT.md:332 and :410 record the coupling
findings.title: No test ties the site's fixed gas limits (bid 1,500,000, settle 1,200,000) to the contract's private gas floors
findings.description: The auction refuses an outbidding bid unless `gasleft() >= REFUND_GAS + REFUND_GAS/63 + DEFERRED_REFUND_RESERVE` (EnglishAuction.sol:243) and refuses a settle unless `gasleft() >= PRIZE_GAS + PRIZE_GAS/63 + 50_000` (KilimAuction.sol:195). All three constants are `private` (EnglishAuction.sol:21, :26; KilimAuction.sol:48), so no test reads them. The site hardcodes `BID_GAS = 1500000n, SETTLE_GAS = 1200000n` (site/chain.js:18) and AUDIT.md:151 and the site comment (chain.js:13-17) present those as sufficient. No forge test asserts that an outbidding bid against an armed gas-burning leader succeeds with a 1,500,000 call gas limit, or that `settle()` with 1,200,000 delivers to a heavy winner. The only ceiling the suite pins is implicit: `_estimate` in GasFloors binary-searches with `hi = 2_000_000` (GasFloors.t.sol:91) and `testLeaderCannotMakeARivalsBidRunOutOfGas` would fail only if the floor passed 2,000,000. There is precedent for the constants moving late: `DEFERRED_REFUND_RESERVE` went 60,000 -> 300,000 on 10 October (R-07, AUDIT.md:255) and checklists/1-pre-deploy.md:212 contemplates changing `PRIZE_GAS` after 1 November. A test pinning the two site numbers belongs in GasFloors.t.sol next to `_aliceBids` (L84-88): `_aliceBids(amount, 1_500_000)` against an armed `SwitchingLeader` must succeed, and `address(auction).call{gas: 1_200_000}(settle)` with `HeavyPoolWinner` must deliver.

votes.reason: The scenario's load-bearing step is false: "site tests green (they never call the contract with those limits)". The site tests run the real site/chain.js adapter against the real compiled contracts on a local anvil (site/test/chain.test.mjs:1 "The chain adapter (site/chain.js) against a real local anvil, driven exactly as the pages drive"; site/test/helpers.mjs:3-4,15-23 start anvil and deployLocal; contracts/scripts/dev/deploy.mjs:199-214 deploy the forge artifacts of KilimMotifs, KilimOneOfOne, KilimAuction). The page's fixed limits are what those transactions carry: chain.js:705 puts `gas: BID_GAS` on every bid call and chain.js:1045 `Object.assign({ gas: SETTLE_GAS }, o || {})` on settle; txOf (chain.js:537-541) copies `c.gas` into the eth_sendTransaction params; the dev wallet only estimates when `!tx.gas` (site/dev/devwallet.js:59-63) and otherwise forwards the transaction unchanged to anvil. So chain.test.mjs:94 "ETH bids: one payable transaction each, the clock starts at the first, then the minimum ladder" sends 12 consecutive outbidding bids at exactly 1,500,000 (lines 130-146, asserting at :146 "every outbid bid went back"), and chain.test.mjs:406 "settlement: anyone settles after the close, which sends the 1/1 to the winner" calls settle() at exactly 1,200,000 and asserts `prizeClaimed === true` and the 1/1 owned by the winner (:422-426); chain.test.mjs:450 does the same settle against a rejecting vault. The contract floors are leader/winner-independent (EnglishAuction.sol:243 checks gasleft() before the refund call, which gets a fixed REFUND_GAS; KilimAuction.sol:195 checks before deliverPrize{gas: PRIZE_GAS}), so an outbid of an EOA exercises the same floor an armed SwitchingLeader would. Had PRIZE_GAS or DEFERRED_REFUND_RESERVE been raised past the page's numbers, these site tests would fail with InsufficientGas, not stay green. The orchestrator's context records site tests 87/87 today. Two further errors in the finding: (a) proposed fix (2) is wrong by design: HeavyPoolWinner's hook needs about 670k but delivery is capped at PRIZE_GAS=500,000 (KilimAuction.sol:196), so settle at any outer gas limit leaves prizeClaimed false and emits PrizeDeliveryFailed, which test/GasFloors.t.sol:172-177 already asserts; (b) the citation AUDIT.md:151 is K-07; the quoted sentence is at AUDIT.md:332 (and :410). What remains true is that the forge suite alone pins only an implicit 2,000,000 ceiling (GasFloors.t.sol:91) and that the end-to-end pin lives in the site suite without a test named for it; that is a labelling point, not a launch risk under the measured margins (523,590 vs 1,500,000; 585,900 vs 1,200,000) and the checklist's explicit re-measure step (checklists/1-pre-deploy.md:212, chain.js:17).

The finding's scenario rests on "site tests green (they never call the contract with those limits)", and that is false. The site suite drives the real compiled contracts on anvil with the page's own gas limits: site/chain.js:705 `return { calls: [{ label: 'Bid ' + fmtEth(q.amount), to: cfg.auction, value: q.amount, gas: BID_GAS,` and :1045 `settle: ... o = Object.assign({ gas: SETTLE_GAS }, o || {}); return simpleWrite(...)`; :540 `if (c.gas) tx.gas = hex(c.gas);` puts it on the eth_sendTransaction; site/dev/devwallet.js:59-63 only estimates `if (!tx.gas)` and otherwise forwards the transaction unchanged (`return rpc('eth_sendTransaction', [tx]);`). site/test/helpers.mjs:1-4,18 deploys from `contracts/scripts/dev/deploy.mjs`, whose `artifact()` (deploy.mjs:106-111) reads the forge `out/` build, and contracts/package.json:8 runs `forge test` (a build) before `node --test "../site/test/*.test.mjs"` (test:site at :10 runs `forge build` first). So site/test/chain.test.mjs:134-146 sends twelve outbidding bids (`bidUnits(who, next)`, each refunding an EOA leader through `_refundOutbid`'s `gasleft() < REFUND_GAS + REFUND_GAS/63 + DEFERRED_REFUND_RESERVE` check at EnglishAuction.sol:243) with a call gas of exactly 1,500,000, and chain.test.mjs:422 `await carol.settle(); ... assert.equal(carol.auction().prizeClaimed, true)` and :459 `const settled = await alice.settle(); ... PrizeDeliveryFailed` settle with exactly 1,200,000 through KilimAuction.sol:195's floor. If PRIZE_GAS or DEFERRED_REFUND_RESERVE were raised past the page's limits, those calls would reject with `InsufficientGas` (`rejectsWith` would not see BidTooLow/AuctionNotEnded etc.) and `pnpm test` would go red before deployment. The floor checks compare gasleft() against constants independent of the leader's or winner's code, so the EOA leader in the site test exercises the same check an armed `SwitchingLeader` would. What is true in the finding: no forge test hardcodes 1_500_000/1_200_000 (grep of contracts/test confirms), the coupling is exercised rather than asserted, and neither suite prices Glamsterdam (anvil runs default pricing), but the proposed forge test would not cover the repricing either; the pre-deploy checklist already carries "Re-measure the page's bid and settle gas limits" on Sepolia (checklists/1-pre-deploy.md:212) and chain.js:17 "Re-measure on Sepolia before launch". Two record points for the orchestrator, Info at most: (a) AUDIT.md:257 still says "R-08 (low), fixed in the site. The page sets the gas limit itself for a bid (800,000) and for settle (900,000)" while the page has sent 1,500,000/1,200,000 since commit 1a1a9534 (10 Oct); AUDIT.md:332 and :410 ("The site sends 1,200,000 and 1,500,000") are current. (b) The finding cites AUDIT.md:151 for the measured floors; that line is the K-07 heading; the quoted text is at AUDIT.md:332.

Citations verified. /Users/orkhan/Documents/ChatGPT/kilim/contracts/src/auction/EnglishAuction.sol:243 `if (gasleft() < REFUND_GAS + REFUND_GAS / 63 + DEFERRED_REFUND_RESERVE) revert InsufficientGas();` with both constants `private` (L21 `uint256 private constant REFUND_GAS = 150_000;`, L26 `uint256 private constant DEFERRED_REFUND_RESERVE = 300_000;`); /Users/orkhan/Documents/ChatGPT/kilim/contracts/src/KilimAuction.sol:48 `uint256 private constant PRIZE_GAS = 500_000;` and L195 `if (gasleft() < PRIZE_GAS + PRIZE_GAS / 63 + 50_000) revert InsufficientGas();`. /Users/orkhan/Documents/ChatGPT/kilim/site/chain.js:18 `var BID_GAS = 1500000n, SETTLE_GAS = 1200000n;` (also copied verbatim into site/afterglow.html:1098, site/src-auction.html:1261, site/afterglow.dev.html:1200). grep of contracts/test, src, script for 1_500_000/1_200_000/1500000/1200000 returns nothing; grep of site/test/*.mjs for BID_GAS/SETTLE_GAS/REFUND_GAS/PRIZE_GAS returns nothing. The only implicit ceilings: /Users/orkhan/Documents/ChatGPT/kilim/contracts/test/GasFloors.t.sol:91 `uint256 hi = 2_000_000;` in `_estimate` (so testLeaderCannotMakeARivalsBidRunOutOfGas at L104 would only fail if the bid floor passed 2,000,000, above the site's 1,500,000), and testLowGasSettleCannotSkipThePrize (L135-153) loops `gasLimit <= 700_000` and passes vacuously if every limit reverts, then calls `auction.settle()` with unlimited gas. So the gap is real: a constant raised late (precedent R-07, AUDIT.md:256, +240,000) with the site untouched leaves forge and site tests green. Severity is Low, not Medium, because (a) the current margins are large: bid floor ~524,000 vs 1,500,000 (2.9x), settle ~586,000 vs 1,200,000 (2x), so the drift would need a roughly 2x rise in a constant, and when R-07 was raised the site's limits were raised in step the same day (R-08, AUDIT.md:257) and again later; (b) the consequence is confined to the site: the contracts stay correct and any wallet/direct call with a higher limit bids and settles fine; (c) the site is not immutable, so the failure is recoverable by editing one line in chain.js and the three HTML copies after launch (the worst case is a window of reverted bids from the page with the misleading message at chain.js:959 'keep the gas limit this page sets'); (d) no ETH, 1/1 or motifs are at risk, and checklists/1-pre-deploy.md:212 already schedules re-measuring the page's limits on Sepolia. It is a legitimate test-coverage hole that would change nothing about launch unless a constant moves.

infos.title: The launch description cannot contain a line break or any control character: the packer refuses what the contract would accept and the deploy script pins the config text to the packed text
infos.description: KilimMotifs._escapeJson (src/KilimMotifs.sol:345, 357-364) accepts control characters and escapes them as \u00XX, so a multi-line collection description is valid on-chain. The golden path does not allow it: onchain/pack_motifs.py json_escape() raises PackError on any character below 0x20 (lines 189-190), the golden tokenURI is built from the packed description (lines 212-216), and script/DeployKilim.s.sol refuses a config whose collection description differs from the packed one (lines 307-309) and a tokenURI that differs from the golden (lines 733-736). The contract's escaping of control characters is therefore dead at launch, and the description the artist writes must be a single line with no tabs. Not a defect in the contract; a constraint on launch content that is written nowhere in docs/CONTRACTS.md or the checklists.
infos.fix: Write the rule into docs/CONTRACTS.md (KilimMotifs section) and checklists/1-pre-deploy.md: the collection description and external URL are one line of printable text, no control characters; or let the packer escape control characters exactly as the contract does (\u00XX) so both agree and multi-line text is possible. Either way the description should be fixed before the store is packed.

infos.title: tokenURI(1) on the current store is unmeasured (the dry run stops at the 1/1's deployment gas first); arithmetic puts it at about 5.6M gas, under both ceilings, and every published read-gas number and threshold still describes the smaller 10 October night store
infos.description: The store packed at 22:35 on 10 October (/Users/orkhan/Documents/ChatGPT/kilim/onchain/build-page/manifest.json: prefix 377,529 B in 16 chunks, head 197 B, tail 832,196 B in 34 chunks, still 283,014 B, pad 2, golden tokenURI 1,297,402 B) has never had its tokenURI(1) read gas measured by any tool: the dry run deploys the three contracts first and `_measured` reverts on the 1/1's 8,087,087 deployment gas (script lines 589-605, the known blocker) before `_checkGolden` (lines 727-749) reaches the tokenURI gas line, and the forge tests measure smaller pages (test/KilimOneOfOne.t.sol:335-364 uses a 70 KB prefix and a 600 KB tail; test/review/OneOfOneGridsSource.t.sol:246-266 a 100 KB still over an 808,872 B tail; test/review/OneOfOneStillSizeSweep.t.sol:20 REAL_TAIL = 808_872). Estimate from the code: ptr = 0x80 + 32 x (17 + 2 + 35) = 1,856 (the three chunk arrays copied to memory at lines 122-124); highest byte touched = ptr + 64 + total + 32 (line 327 `mstore(pos, 0)`) = 1,299,354, i.e. 40,605 words; memory cost 3 x 40,605 + 40,605^2 / 512 = 121,815 + 3,220,246 = 3,342,061. The non-memory part of the three recorded measurements is nearly constant (3,838,101 for 896,938 B: 2,214,412; 4,625,534 for 1,092,954 B: 2,237,388; 3,378,414 for 757,791 B: 2,208,351), so with the extra 8 chunks (8 x (2,600 + 200) extcodesize/extcodecopy + 8 x 2,100 SLOAD = 39,200) and 6,389 more copied words (19,167) the read is about 5,550,000 to 5,650,000 gas: under the 8,000,000 policy by roughly 2.35M to 2.45M and under the 16,777,216 cap by about 11.1M. Holding the non-memory part fixed, the 8M line is reached at an answer of about 1.70 MB (53,300 words). The sweep's 400,000-character case (OneOfOneStillSizeSweep.t.sol:61) produces a 1,296,663 B answer, 739 B short of the real one; its logged gas from today's run (not available read-only) would confirm the figure. Meanwhile STORAGE.md:11, :34, :36, :42, :82, :100, checklists/1-pre-deploy.md:30, :55, :57, :93, :139, :211, README.md:94, AUDIT.md:411-412 and ../onchain/ARTWORK-ONCHAIN.md:14, :36, :38 still give 4,625,534 gas / 1,092,954 B / 46 chunks / prefix 188,421 B / tail 816,856 B / still 141,183 B, and the RPC-probe rule of thumb at 1-pre-deploy.md:139, "anything below about 5M would blank the 1/1 (it reads at 4.63M)", is now wrong by about 1M: the line is about 5.7M. The contract itself is sound at this size: every invariant of the one-buffer assembly (sectionSize/copyChunks consistency, raw = piece + m/3, hex input word i at hexStart + 32768 + 32i read before output byte 64i + 64 reaches it for all i <= 1023, base64 block j written to piece + 32j ending below raw + 24j + 24 for j <= m/24 - 1, the 3-byte tail groups, the pad rule (3 - (len(HEAD) + 65,537) % 3) % 3 giving m = 65,736 and 4m/3 = 87,648, the total 27 + 377,529 + 87,648 + 832,196 + 2 = 1,297,402 equal to the manifest's golden, the zeroed last word and the canonical ABI return) holds by arithmetic.
infos.fix: After the still/deploy-gas decision is made and the store re-packed, run `pnpm -s deploy:dry` to get the real read figure and replace the 4,625,534 / 1,092,954 / 46-chunk / 188,421 / 816,856 / 141,183 numbers in STORAGE.md, 1-pre-deploy.md, README.md, AUDIT.md and ARTWORK-ONCHAIN.md; restate the probe threshold at 1-pre-deploy.md:139 as the measured read plus margin (about 6M today); optionally make the sweep's real-size case assert the ceiling.

infos.title: The still is PNG-only in the packer while the artist's chosen cover is the lossless WebP; the PNG-only rule is what makes the 1/1 creation exceed the 8M policy
infos.description: This answers the relayed user question ('we are not WebP cuz it's not working'): nothing in the repository records WebP failing anywhere. The art side chose WebP: TODO.md:27 'mint/still.webp as the cover', TODO.md:30 '`mint/still.webp`, 1536 × 2048, lossless WebP (111 KB; the PNG kept beside it)', and mint/still.json says 'the WebP decodes to the PNG pixel for pixel' (110,572 bytes vs. 283,014 for the PNG). The packer side accepts only PNG: pack_page.py:145-146 raises 'the still is not a PNG' on anything without the PNG signature, line 115 hard-codes `data:image/png;base64,`, stores.mjs:29 defaults to `mint/still.png`, page.test.mjs:89 asserts `meta.image.startsWith('data:image/png;base64,iVBORw0KGgo')`, STORAGE.md:130 says 'the still must be a PNG'. So the store was packed from the 283 KB PNG, PREFIX grew to 377,529 bytes / 16 chunks (manifest), and the 1/1 creation measures 8,087,087 in the dry run (the known blocker). With the WebP the still is 147,432 base64 characters, PREFIX about 147.6 KB in 7 chunks: nine fewer chunk transactions (about 50M gas less at ~5.4-6.0M each), a 1/1 creation of roughly 6.5M by the measured 7K gas per prefix KB (6,750,528 at 188 KB; 8,087,087 at 377 KB), and a tokenURI(1) about 230 KB shorter. Marketplaces and browsers render `data:image/webp;base64,` images; the contract itself never looks inside PREFIX beyond '#' and '%'. The only code that cares is the packer, its test and the docs. The docs also still describe the still as 1024 × 1024 / 141,183 bytes (STORAGE.md:34, 42; ARTWORK-ONCHAIN.md:14, 44) while the file is 1536 × 2048.
infos.fix: Decision for the artist: use `mint/still.webp` as the token image. Then in pack_page.py accept `RIFF....WEBP` (bytes 0-3 'RIFF', 8-11 'WEBP') alongside PNG and emit the matching MIME (`image/webp` / `image/png`) in prefix_json; record `still.type` in the manifest; make page.test.mjs:89 assert the MIME the manifest names; change stores.mjs's default and STORAGE.md:130, CONTRACTS.md:63/75 and ARTWORK-ONCHAIN.md to say 'PNG or lossless WebP'; re-pack, re-run test:pack/test:page/deploy:dry, republish `expected`.

infos.title: The still is accepted on an 8-byte signature and pinned to image/png; the WebP of the same frame exists at 39% of the size and nothing in the repo records a marketplace test against it
infos.description: pack_page.py checks only `still.startswith(PNG_SIGNATURE)` and writes `data:image/png;base64,` (line 115); a truncated or CRC-broken PNG with a valid signature is packed, hashed into `expected`, passes the dry run (the golden is computed from whatever bytes were given) and is stored for good. The current still is complete (72 chunks, IEND present, every CRC good, IHDR 1536 x 2048 8-bit RGB), so that path is not hit today. On the user's question: the repo has no record that a WebP token image 'does not work' anywhere; the only thing refusing WebP is this check. still.json records a lossless `still.webp` of 110,572 bytes that 'decodes to the PNG pixel for pixel' beside the 283,014-byte PNG; packed, the prefix would be about 147.5 KB (6 chunks) instead of 377,529 bytes (16 chunks), and the prefix size is what drives the KilimOneOfOne deployment gas and the 1/1 read size. Whether marketplaces render a `data:image/webp` image is an open rehearsal item (1-pre-deploy.md:72, 137, 218), not a tested fact. The documents still describe the previous still: ARTWORK-ONCHAIN.md:14 and :44 say 1024 x 1024 and 141,183 bytes, STORAGE.md:34/42 and 1-pre-deploy.md:30 say a 188,421-byte prefix, 8 prefix chunks and 46 chunks in all; the store packed at 22:35 today has 377,529 / 16 / 54. The 2 MiB URL check (lines 59, 159-161) is applied to the animation_url only; the whole tokenURI data: URL (1,297,402 bytes today) grows with the still and is bounded only by the 8M read-gas rule.
infos.fix: Record the still-format decision with its evidence (a marketplace or wallet rendering `data:image/webp;base64,` from a Sepolia token) or make the packer take `--still-type png|webp` with the matching signature (`RIFF....WEBP`) so the choice is a config value, not a hard-coded one. Parse the PNG (IHDR, chunk CRCs, IEND at the end) and write width/height into the manifest. Refresh the sizes in ARTWORK-ONCHAIN.md, STORAGE.md and 1-pre-deploy.md from the current manifests.

infos.description: `pack_page.py` refuses anything but a PNG (`if not still.startswith(PNG_SIGNATURE): raise PackError('the still is not a PNG')`) and writes `"image":"data:image/png;base64,` into PREFIX, so the image format is fixed by the packer and pinned into `prefixHash`, the 1/1 golden and `expected.still`. infos.title: 'The whole pool for gas' understates the realization cost: claiming 1,000,000 motifs is about 28G gas, more than the 93.9 ETH top bid at any gas price above about 3.4 gwei
infos.description: F-04/K-01 are disclosed as taking the pool 'for the cost of gas', meaning the ladder's bid gas (about 12.1M gas for 93 bids). Credits are worthless until claimed (NATIVE-ETH.md:96), and a claim costs 1,790,852 gas per 64 motifs (AUDIT.md re-measured), about 27,982 per motif: the full pool is about 28G gas, 28 ETH at 1 gwei, 140 ETH at 5 gwei, 560 ETH at 20 gwei, against a 93.862 ETH top bid. The farm is gas-bounded, which matters for the Kilim Bazaar's flooding analysis (KILIM-BAZAAR-RULES.md:63 '11,000 kilims from a 10 ETH auction'), and the disclosure should say that the cost is claim gas, not bid gas. Credits never expire, so the ladderer waits for cheap gas; the brake is real but soft.
infos.fix: Add the claim-gas figure to the F-04/K-01 disclosures and to the Bazaar supply estimate.

infos.title: NATIVE-ETH.md says a winning contract that cannot call claimPrize is 'therefore not left without the 1/1'; only true when its receiver merely needed more gas
infos.description: The sentence generalizes `deliverPrizeToWinner()` (KilimAuction.sol:229-236), which mints to `highestBidder` with the caller's gas and reverts if the wallet refuses. A winning contract with no `onERC721Received` (or one that rejects) and no way to call `claimPrize(to)` never receives the 1/1: `deliverPrizeToWinner` reverts every time and `claimPrize` requires `msg.sender == winner` (:216). F-19 and checklists/1-pre-deploy.md:185 state this correctly ('a winner that refuses NFTs outright still has to call `claimPrize(to)` itself'); this line contradicts them and is the bidder-facing document.
infos.fix: Qualify the sentence: 'A winning contract whose receiver only needed more gas is therefore not left without the 1/1; one that refuses ERC-721 tokens must call claimPrize(to) itself or loses it (F-19).'

infos.title: Gas constants and measured floors that depend on today's prices, and what must be re-measured for Glamsterdam (EIP-8037/8038, Last Call until 2026-11-01)
infos.description: Price-dependent values, all fixed at deployment: EnglishAuction.sol:21 `REFUND_GAS = 150_000` (forwarded to the refund; EIP-8038 raises the value-transferring CALL's ACCOUNT_WRITE from 6,700 to 9,000 and cold access 2,600 to 3,000, a few thousand gas of the allowance); :26 `DEFERRED_REFUND_RESERVE = 300_000` versus a deferred path projected at 225,840 after the fork (AUDIT.md:331; two new slots at 97,920 + 2,100 + 10,000 each), a 25% margin that AUDIT.md:287 already says a further ~40% rise would exhaust; :243 the InsufficientGas floor `REFUND_GAS + REFUND_GAS / 63 + DEFERRED_REFUND_RESERVE` = 452,381 is price-independent, but the gas a bid needs before reaching it is not (about 524,000 today; a first bid by a wallet writes roughly four new slots, so ~0.9-1.0M after, against the site's 1,500,000); KilimAuction.sol:48 `PRIZE_GAS = 500_000` (delivery projected 465,458 cold, leaving 34,542 for the winner's hook; V-15) and :195 the 50,000 settle reserve; settle() ~585,836 today against the site's 1,200,000. Reads: KilimOneOfOne.tokenURI(1) 4,625,534 gas; EIP-8038 adds WARM_ACCESS (100) for EXTCODECOPY's second read and raises cold access to 3,000, about 500 more per chunk for the ~55 chunks read, negligible, but the figure and the RPC eth_call caps (audit/rpc-gas-caps-*.txt) should be re-probed on Sepolia. The test EVM runs Cancun rules (foundry.toml:9) while mainnet has run Osaka/Fusaka since 2025-12-03 (EIP-7607 activation table), so EIP-7825's 16,777,216 cap and EIP-7623's calldata floor are not enforced in tests; neither changes opcode prices, so the suite's floors are valid for mainnet today but can only be projected, never measured, for Glamsterdam in forge 1.7.1 (see the Medium finding).
infos.fix: Keep the constants (they hold on the published Last Call values) and add the Sepolia measurements listed above to checklists/1-pre-deploy.md:212 before deciding PRIZE_GAS and the site's gas limits; record the Glamsterdam mainnet activation date next to the launch date once EIP-7773 fills it in.

infos.title: audit/build.txt and audit/gas-render.txt are stale evidence from 26 September describing contracts that no longer exist

infos.title: The Apache-2.0 license copy and NOTICE travel only with the repository, which is private; the explorer-verified source will carry only the SPDX line and header
infos.description: Apache-2.0 section 4 requires a copy of the License with any redistribution of the derivative (EnglishAuction.sol, and KilimAuction.sol which inherits it), retained attribution, and a prominent modification notice. The repository satisfies all of it: vendor/thirdweb/LICENSE (sha256 pinned by verify-upstream.mjs), vendor/thirdweb/NOTICE, EnglishAuction.sol:1 SPDX Apache-2.0 and :13-16 the adaptation notice naming thirdweb and the commit; the vendored snapshot's sha256 equals the raw file at the named commit (fetched today) and the 0xMacro A-15 page lists that sha256 and commit. But the repository is private (memory: private github.com/orkhanart/kilim since 2026-10-10), and Etherscan/Sourcify verification publishes only the .sol sources, so the only public distribution of the derived code would carry the SPDX identifier and header but no License text. checklists/2-deploy.md:65 ('source matches the tagged commit') presumes a public tag without saying so.
infos.fix: Add to checklists/2-deploy.md a step to make the tagged commit public (or publish vendor/thirdweb/LICENSE, NOTICE and src/auction/EnglishAuction.sol on the site) at verification time; a one-line pointer to the LICENSE URL in EnglishAuction.sol's header would make the verified source self-sufficient.

infos.title: F-27 is still listed Open although each of its mutants is now killed or equivalent
infos.description: AUDIT.md:85 keeps `F-27 | Info | Small surviving mutants: the deadline boundary, the Registered count, a 2,300-gas ETH payout, refund and collect order, the withdrawProceeds guard` in the Open table, and AUDIT.md:210 says `F-27 lists the mutants the October 9 audit found alive`. Tests added on 10 October kill four of the five: the deadline boundary by `testSignatureIsGoodThroughItsDeadlineSecondAndNotAfter` (AuditGaps.t.sol:318-331: revert at deadline+1, success at deadline); the `Registered` count by `testRegistrationStartAndSettlementEvents` (AuditGaps.t.sol:259-269: `vm.expectEmit(); emit Registered(registrant(0), 1)` and `Registered(registrant(99), 100)`); a 2,300-gas payout by `testAReceiverNeedingMostOfTheRefundCapIsStillPaid` (AuditGaps.t.sol:147-160: a receiver burning 120,000 is paid inside the bid, which a `transfer`-based `_pay` cannot do); the `withdrawProceeds` guard by `testOnlyTreasuryCanWithdrawOnlyAfterSettlement` (KilimAuction.t.sol:533: `vm.expectRevert(EnglishAuction.NotSettled.selector)` — without the guard the revert would be NothingToWithdraw). The fifth, swapping `_collectBid(amount)` and `_refundOutbid(...)` (KilimAuction.sol:128-129), is an equivalent mutant: `_collectBid` is a view check of msg.value and a mismatch reverts the whole transaction either way, with the refund call's effects undone and re-entry blocked by nonReentrant. AUDIT.md:260 already states 25 mutants were applied and all fail, but F-27 was not moved. The record a human auditor will read says mutants survive.
infos.fix: Move F-27 to 'Closed by tests added after the audit' (AUDIT.md:87-93) naming the four killing tests and stating the fifth is equivalent; or, if the intent is to keep it open until a tool-driven mutation run on the new contracts (AUDIT.md:418 says none has run), reword it to say so.

infos.title: Launch-day sequence contradictions: --block vs --tx, 'publish site/index.html' vs the orkhanart target, a share card that says COMING SOON while live, and no document names what publishes orkhan.art
infos.description: Four places give four different sequences. 1-pre-deploy.md 143 and README.md 57 instruct `pnpm -s site-config --chain <id> --auction <address> --block <deployment block>`; on the two public mainnet RPCs the --block path needs eth_getCode at an old block, which public nodes answer only for the last ~128 blocks (site-config.mjs 6-7, V-19), so an operator following the pre-deploy checklist on launch day gets 'this node does not answer for block'; 3-post-deploy.md 21 correctly says --tx. site-config.mjs 105 says 'publish site/index.html and auction.html', which are the local-target pages (relative links, Sepolia config, no newsletter endpoint), not the orkhanart target that orkhan.art serves; only the next sentence, for chain 1, points at the sync. build.py's docstring (10-12) and sync_orkhanart.py (11-13) both say the sync 'never deploys', and HOSTING-HEADERS.md covers headers only: no document in the repo names the command or pipeline that puts public/kilim on the Hetzner host, nor who can run it. The share card site/og.png (OG_IMAGE, build.py 90, 177, the same file for soon and live) reads 'COMING SOON / AUCTION + BIDDERS EDITION / ETHEREUM' (viewed), so every link shared during the live auction carries a 'Coming soon' card; the live-mode meta descriptions (META, 98-107) change but the image does not. The afterglow page's Google Fonts line in HOSTING-HEADERS.md 18 ('the auction and Afterglow pages') is also off: in the orkhanart build the stylesheet is on index and afterglow, not auction (grep of site/dist/orkhanart). None of these breaks the mint; each is a wrong step or a wrong public signal on the day.
infos.fix: Align 1-pre-deploy.md 143, README.md 57 and site-config's printed 'Next:' with 3-post-deploy.md 21 (--tx, orkhanart target, sync, commit, then the named deploy command on the host); add a live og.png (or a second OG_IMAGE for live) before launch.

infos.title: Counterfactual (undeployed) smart wallets cannot register by either path; the site asks them for a signature that can only fail
infos.description: OpenZeppelin's isValidSignatureNowCalldata branches on signer.code.length (SignatureChecker.sol lines 49-54): an address with no code is checked by ECDSA only, so an undeployed Safe's owner signature never recovers to the Safe address and registerFor reverts InvalidRegistrationSignature; register() cannot be sent from an address without code. The site's hasCode (chain.js lines 819-823) correctly treats any non-'0x' code, including an EIP-7702 designator 0xef0100.., as code, so a delegated EOA is routed to register() (tested at chain.test.mjs lines 80-91 with a deployed contract, not a designator, but the predicate is the same). A counterfactual Safe holding 0.01 ETH is routed to sponsoredRegister, prompted 'Sign registration — no payment', and then told 'Registration signature or wallet eligibility is invalid.' README line 20 says 'Undeployed/counterfactual wallets are not supported' only in the relayer's own README; neither the site nor checklist 1 line 123 ('with several wallets including a Safe') says the Safe must be deployed first, at the owner's expense, after which register() also costs the owner gas. No defect in the contract; a disclosure point for the launch decision. Matters only if activated.
infos.fix: Say on the site and in checklist 1 that a smart wallet must be deployed before registering, and make the relayer's 400 distinguish 'no code and ECDSA failed' from other failures.

infos.title: Glamsterdam refund arithmetic for a 7702 delegate with a storage-writing receive(): one new slot still fits the push, two are deferred; the site's 1,500,000 bid gas still covers the deferral
infos.description: The refund self-call gets exactly REFUND_GAS = 150,000 (EnglishAuction.sol:21, 244). Inside payOutbidRefund (255-258) the value call to the bidder costs cold account 2,600 (3,000 after EIP-8037/8038 per the suite's constants, PrizeGasBudget.t.sol:188-189) + 9,000 for value, and a delegated EOA adds one more cold access for the delegate's code; the callee receives (150,000 - ~400 - 11,600 - 2,600) x 63/64 + 2,300 = about 135,600 today and (150,000 - ~400 - 12,000 - 3,000) x 63/64 + 2,300 = about 134,800 after the fork. A new slot costs 22,100 today and 110,020 projected (AttackPatterns.t.sol:161; PrizeGasBudget.t.sol:187), so a receive() that writes one new slot is paid in both regimes (margin about 24,800 after), one that writes two (220,040) is paid today and deferred after the fork. Deferral records two new slots: 50,000 + 2 x 87,920 = 225,840 projected, inside the 300,000 reserve (AttackPatterns.t.sol:656-663; EnglishAuction.sol:26). The bid's own writes for a new bidder (three new slots: the CreditRange array length, its one packed slot, motifCredits; about six updates incl. the storage ReentrancyGuard, EnglishAuction.sol:4,17) add about 3 x 87,920 + 6 x 7,100 = 306,360 to today's roughly 545,000 transaction floor (1-pre-deploy.md:52): about 851,000, under the page's fixed 1,500,000 (chain.js:18, 705). The deferred bidder then withdraws from the page with the whole transaction's gas (auction.js:224 -> withdrawRefund(self)), which is the path that works for a gas-starved receiver. No forge test has a delegated receiver that writes storage; HostileWallet burns or reverts (AttackPatterns.t.sol:60-86) and the Safe-shaped mock is prize-only.
infos.fix: None needed in the contracts; add the two-slot delegated receiver to the Sepolia rehearsal list at 1-pre-deploy.md:212 so the deferral and the page's withdraw path are seen once on Glamsterdam prices.

spec.answer:
SUMMARY. I read the specs from ethereum/EIPs master (fetched 2026-10-11), the execution-specs branch forks/amsterdam (head 1689800091, 2026-10-06) and go-ethereum master and v1.17.7. I checked the numbers with read-only eth_call, eth_estimateGas and eth_createAccessList calls on Sepolia, which has run Glamsterdam since 2026-10-06. The deployment can be done. Every Kilim chunk and all three contracts fit in one transaction each, because the 16,777,216 cap now limits only execution gas. But each transaction must set a gas limit above 2^24, and costs are 4-8 times today's. The repo's 8M dry-run policy cannot hold under these rules.

1. COST OF DEPLOYING CODE UNDER GLAMSTERDAM (EIP-8037 + EIP-8038 + EIP-2780)
- CPSB is a constant, not dynamic. eip-8037.md L35: "| `CPSB` | 1530 |". The rationale (L306) says: "`CPSB` is a fixed parameter derived from a reference block gas limit ... If a future block gas limit increase materially changes the expected state growth rate, `CPSB` can be re-derived in a subsequent EIP." The code matches: execution-specs vm/gas.py L47 `COST_PER_STATE_BYTE ... = StateGasPerByte(Uint(1530))`, and geth params/protocol_params.go L226 `CostPerStateByte = 1530`.
- Code deposit, per byte. eip-8037.md L49: "| `GAS_CODE_DEPOSIT` | 200/byte | `CPSB` per byte | `6 × ceil(len/32)` (hash cost) |". That is 1,530 state gas per byte (7.65x the old 200), plus 6 execution gas per 32-byte word. Spec code: interpreter.py L370-379, `code_hash_gas = OPCODE_KECCAK256_PER_WORD * ceil32(len)//32` and `code_deposit_state_gas = ulen(contract_code) * COST_PER_STATE_BYTE`.
- New account. eip-8037.md L48: "| `GAS_CREATE` | 32,000 | `STATE_BYTES_PER_NEW_ACCOUNT x CPSB` | `CREATE_ACCESS` |", with `STATE_BYTES_PER_NEW_ACCOUNT` = 120 (L37). That is 183,600 state gas, charged only if the target does not exist (L137: "`(STATE_BYTES_PER_NEW_ACCOUNT + L) × CPSB` charged").
- CREATE_ACCESS. eip-8038.md L50 sets it to 12,000 execution gas (ACCOUNT_WRITE 9,000 + COLD_ACCOUNT_ACCESS 3,000). It replaces the 32,000 for CREATE and CREATE2 and for creation transactions.
- Creation transaction intrinsic cost. eip-2780.md L135: "| Create transaction, `tx.value` = 0 | `TX_BASE_COST + CREATE_ACCESS` / 0 | 0 / `STATE_BYTES_PER_NEW_ACCOUNT × CPSB` | 24,000 / 183,600 |". The old base was 53,000.
- Initcode, per byte: unchanged. Still 2 per word (gas.py L89 `CODE_INIT_PER_WORD ... 2`). CREATE2 still pays keccak at 6 per word (system.py L274-281). Standard calldata stays 4/16 per byte. The EIP-7976 floor rises to 64 per byte (eip-7976.md L41: "the floor cost is `64` gas per calldata byte").
- New storage slot. 64 x 1,530 = 97,920 state gas, plus 2,100 cold + 10,000 STORAGE_WRITE execution gas.

2. THE CAP, THE RESERVOIR AND BLOCK GAS_USED
- The 16,777,216 cap limits execution gas only. eip-8037.md L68: "the transaction gas limit set in EIP-7825 only applies to execution-gas, while state-gas is capped by `tx.gas`, which this proposal in turn caps at `TX_MAX_TOTAL_GAS_LIMIT`" = 4,294,967,295 (L40). Validity (L76): `tx.gas <= TX_MAX_TOTAL_GAS_LIMIT`. Also L77: `max(intrinsic_gas, calldata_floor_gas_cost) <= TX_MAX_GAS_LIMIT`.
- Funding works through a reservoir. L95-98: `evm_gas = tx.gas - intrinsic_gas; execution_gas_budget = TX_MAX_GAS_LIMIT - intrinsic_gas; gas_left = min(execution_gas_budget, evm_gas); state_gas_reservoir = evm_gas - gas_left`. L113: "State-gas charges deduct from `state_gas_reservoir` first. When the reservoir is exhausted, the remainder deducts from `gas_left`". L115: "`state_gas_reservoir` is passed to a child frame in full: the 63/64 rule applies to `gas_left` only."
- Block inclusion is checked per dimension. L78: `min(TX_MAX_GAS_LIMIT, tx.gas) <= execution_gas_available` and `tx.gas <= state_gas_available`. So tx.gas must fit inside the block gas limit (mainnet today 59,999,943 at block 26,166,705; Sepolia 199,804,498).
- Gas used. The user pays `tx.gas - gas_left - state_gas_reservoir` after refunds (L228). The block counts two counters, and the header gives L255: `gas_used = max(block_output.block_execution_gas_used, block_output.block_state_gas_used)`. The base fee uses this value. Each transaction's execution share is `max(tx_gas_used_after_refund - tx_state_gas, calldata_floor_gas_cost)` (L242).

3. MAXIMUM CODE SIZE: RAISED TO 65,536
EIP-7954 is scheduled for inclusion (eip-7773.md L30). eip-7954.md L25-26: "Update the EIP-170 contract code size limit of 24KiB (`0x6000` bytes) to 64KiB (`0x10000` bytes)" and initcode "48KiB (`0xC000` bytes) to 128KiB (`0x20000` bytes)". Spec code: interpreter.py L80-81 `MAX_CODE_SIZE = 0x10000`, `MAX_INIT_CODE_SIZE = 2 * MAX_CODE_SIZE`. EIP-7954 is in Last Call until 2026-11-01. EIP-7997, also scheduled, makes 0x4e59b448... a required CREATE2 factory.

4. STATUS
- Mainnet has no date. eip-7773.md L64-68: "| Sepolia | 353024 | 1791294816 (2026-10-06 13:53:36 UTC) |"; the Hoodi and Mainnet rows are empty. The EF blog (2026/09/17) says: "Hoodi and mainnet activation dates have not yet been decided ... it does not schedule a mainnet upgrade." Press reports a Q4 2026 target; that is not official.
- Sepolia activated 2026-10-06 13:53:36 UTC, epoch 353,024, slot 11,296,768.
- EIP-8037 is not Final. It is "status: Last Call / last-call-deadline: 2026-11-01". EIP-8038, EIP-2780, EIP-7954, EIP-7976 and EIP-7997 have the same status and deadline. EIP-7825 is Final. EIP-7773 is in Review. The last edit to EIP-8037 was 2026-10-06; I found no open PR that changes CPSB.
- Line 497 of EIP-8037 says the new-account charge is "added to intrinsic cost". That is out of date and contradicts L84 and EIP-2780, which make it a runtime charge.

5. ARITHMETIC (CPSB 1,530)
A) Full chunk via 0x4e59 CREATE2.
- Sizes: runtime 24,576 (0x00 plus 24,575 data). The initcode is 24,586, not ~24,590: DeployKilim.s.sol L898 prepends 11 bytes, `hex"61", uint16(data.length + 1), hex"80600a3d393df300"`. Calldata is 32 + 24,586 = 24,618 bytes, of which 34 are zero.
- Intrinsic (execution): 12,000 + 3,000 (cold factory) + 4 x (34 + 24,584 x 4) = 408,480.
- Factory ops before CREATE2: 20, plus CALLDATACOPY 3 + 3x769 + memory (3x769 + 769^2/512 = 3,462) = 5,772, plus 14. CREATE2 itself: 12,000 + keccak 6x769 + initcode 2x769 = 18,152.
- Child initcode run: 5,776. Deposit hash: 6x768 = 4,608. Factory tail: 51.
- Execution total = 442,866.
- State = (120 + 24,576) x 1,530 = 183,600 + 37,601,280 = 37,784,880.
- Gas used = 38,227,746. Geth's eth_createAccessList on Sepolia gives 38,228,130; the 384 difference is my random salt costing more calldata.
- Block execution share = max(442,866, floor 15,000 + 64 x 24,618 = 1,590,552) = 1,590,552.
- One transaction carries it: execution 442,866 is under 16,777,216, and the transaction is valid because tx.gas may go up to 2^32-1. But tx.gas must be about 38.5M or more, not 38.23M. The state gas that the reservoir does not cover is drawn from the create frame's own gas_left, and the factory keeps 1/64 of that. Under the spec the minimum is 16,777,216 + 21,705,873 = 38,483,089.
- Measured minimum gas limits on Sepolia (eth_call bisection, one-nonzero-byte salt):
  - spec model: 38,483,101
  - reth/publicnode: 38,483,301 (flaky across its backends)
  - drpc and Tenderly: 38,824,724 every time. That equals, within 1 gas, a model where the create frame gets only 63/64 of the reservoir.
  - eth_estimateGas returns 38,532,320, and that value reverts on drpc and Tenderly.
- Recommendation: set tx.gas to 38.9M or more. Better, set it to 54,562,096 or more (16,777,216 + 37,784,880) so the reservoir covers all state gas; unused gas is refunded.
- The same chunk as a plain creation transaction (24,586-byte initcode) needs exactly 38,214,154 (Sepolia matches to the gas).
- Whole store (54 chunks: 2 grids, 1 names, 16 prefix, 1 head, 34 tail): execution 22,617,658, state 1,932,333,390, total about 1.955B gas. With the 60M mainnet limit, two full chunks (75.6M) cannot share a block, so the store needs about 33 or more blocks.

B) Direct creation, runtime only. The formula is: execution = 24,000 + calldata(4/16) + 2·words(initcode) + initcode run + 6·words(L); state = (120 + L) x 1,530. I tested each case on Sepolia with a minimal 10-byte-prefix initcode (initcode = L + 10), and the minimum tx.gas equals the computed value exactly. The state part is about 99% of the total.
- 10,891 bytes: execution 203,421 + state 11,011 x 1,530 = 16,846,830 → total 17,050,251
- 9,981 bytes: execution 188,420 + state 10,101 x 1,530 = 15,454,530 → total 15,642,950
- 11,216 bytes: execution 208,774 + state 11,336 x 1,530 = 17,344,080 → total 17,552,854
- The 10,891 and 11,216 cases are above 2^24 in total, which was impossible before Glamsterdam. All three have execution far under the cap, and the top frame is the create frame, so no 63/64 margin is needed.

C) Estimates for the real contracts. These are my own estimates: I took the Cancun receipts from the local anvil run (AUDIT.md L418), repriced them, and counted the storage slots each constructor writes.
- KilimMotifs: 8 slots. State 17,630,190 + execution about 0.93M = about 18.56M.
- KilimOneOfOne: 59 slots (54 chunk-array slots, name, symbol, a 3-slot description). State 21,231,810 + execution about 3.69M = about 24.9M.
- KilimAuction: 1 slot. State 17,442,000 + execution about 0.65M = about 18.1M.
All three fit in one transaction each, with execution under the cap.

REPO CONSEQUENCES
- contracts/script/DeployKilim.s.sol L77-78: "Policy ceiling for every transaction ... well under the 16,777,216 cap." / `uint256 public constant MAX_TX_GAS = 8_000_000;`. - Full chunk: Sepolia 38,532,308; mainnet 5,467,182.
- Small chunk: Sepolia 522,523; mainnet 97,234.

Minimum gas at which eth_call succeeds (bisection, factory returns the expected address):
- Full: Sepolia 38,626,249; mainnet 5,457,524.

On Sepolia the full-chunk estimate is 93,941 gas below what eth_call needs. eth_call at exactly 38,532,308 gives "execution reverted", while 40,000,000 succeeds. A transaction sent at the raw estimate would revert. With gas = 16,777,216 the full chunk reverts on Sepolia, and estimate answers "out of gas: gas required exceeds: 16777216". The 8,000,000 and 30,000,000 attempts behave the same way. On mainnet every gas value from 5,467,182 up succeeds.

4. LATEST BLOCK:
- Sepolia: #11,889,191, gasLimit 199,999,809, baseFee 15 wei.
- Mainnet: #26,166,693, gasLimit 60,000,000, baseFee 61,881,297 wei.

5. PLAIN CREATION (no 'to'), stub 0x61 2a8b 80600a3d393df3 + 10,891 runtime bytes:
- Sepolia: estimate 17,186,750, min eth_call 17,050,263. At 16,777,216: "out of gas: gas required exceeds: 16777216".
- Mainnet: estimate 2,428,870, min 2,408,587.

For comparison, the 24,576-byte runtime: Sepolia 38,518,608 (min 38,214,154); mainnet 5,412,643 (min 5,368,866).

WHAT IT MEANS:
(a) One full chunk costs about 38.6M gas on Sepolia against about 5.46M on mainnet, a factor of about 7.05 to 7.08. Small chunk: about 5.4x. 10,891-byte creation: about 7.08x.

(b) The rise matches EIP-8037 (status Last Call; the spec file was last changed 2026-10-06T21:57:47Z). CPSB = 1530 gas per state byte replaces 200 per byte of code deposit, plus (120 + L) × CPSB for a new account. For L = 24,576: (24,576 + 120) × 1530 = 37,784,880 state gas. The measured marginal cost on Sepolia is (38,214,154 − 17,050,263) / 13,685 = 1,546.5 gas per byte, which is 1530 plus calldata. On mainnet it is 216.3 gas per byte, which is 200 plus calldata.

(c) A tx gas limit of 16,777,216 does NOT fit one full chunk on Sepolia, or even a 10,891-byte creation; both were measured to fail. Under EIP-8037 that cap (EIP-7825) applies only to execution gas. State gas is drawn from a reservoir, and tx.gas may go up to TX_MAX_TOTAL_GAS_LIMIT = 2^32 − 1. So a single transaction of about 38.7M+ gas should be valid on Sepolia (its block limit is 200M). eth_call cannot prove transaction validity: trivial calls with gas 30,000,000 succeed on both chains.

(d) On mainnet today a chunk fits easily: 5.47M, under both 16,777,216 and the script's 8M policy. If mainnet takes Glamsterdam before deploy, each full chunk needs about 38.6M. The script's ceiling, L78 `uint256 public constant MAX_TX_GAS = 8_000_000;` (checked at L925 `if (g > MAX_TX_GAS) revert Refused(...)`), would then refuse every full chunk.

There is a second problem. The script's dry run measures gas in forge's local EVM (foundry.toml evm_version cancun), and so does its `_intrinsic` (L929-934, 53,000 + 2/word + 4/16 per byte). That dry run would still report the old about 5.4M and pass, while the chain charges about 7x. I did not verify what gas limit forge sends at broadcast. Any limit below about 38.63M per full chunk would revert on chain and burn the gas. The Sepolia estimator itself comes in 94k short.

(e) Cost at the current mainnet baseFee (0.0619 gwei): about 0.00034 ETH per full chunk at today's pricing, about 0.0024 ETH at Glamsterdam pricing.

VERDICT: The PoC's finding holds. All five constants are correct, and its about 38.26M agrees with the Sepolia measurement to within 0.7%. Two things in it need fixing. First, its header numbers are stale. Second, its "need" is the gas a full chunk uses, not the smallest gas limit that works, so it understates the limit by 0.2-0.6M. Neither changes the verdict. The documented Sepolia rehearsal fails today on its first chunk.

I ran the PoC unchanged with forge 1.7.1, in a scratch copy of contracts/ and onchain/. Both tests FAIL, which is what the finding predicts:
- Full chunk prefix_00: Cancun simulation 5,394,342. Forge signs 7,012,644. The code deposit is 37,784,880 state gas. The PoC's "need" is 38,264,022.
- KilimMotifs: Cancun 3,210,558, signed 4,173,725, deposit 16,846,830.
- KilimOneOfOne: Cancun 2,514,621, signed 3,269,007, deposit 15,454,530.
- KilimAuction: Cancun 2,577,782, signed 3,351,116, deposit 17,344,080.
- Same chunk numbers with --evm-version osaka. forge 1.7.1 rejects "amsterdam" ("Unknown evm version: amsterdam"), which confirms PoC L49: forge has no Glamsterdam schedule.

(1) CONSTANTS
- CPSB 1,530 (PoC L62): correct.
  - eip-8037.md L35 "| `CPSB` | 1530 |", fetched again by me. The execution-specs (gas.py L47) and geth (protocol_params.go L226) agree.
  - Measured: Sepolia charges 1,546.5 gas per extra runtime byte, i.e. 1,530 plus 16 calldata. Mainnet charges 216.3, i.e. 200 plus 16.
- 120 bytes per new account (PoC L63): correct.
  - eip-8037.md L37 "| `STATE_BYTES_PER_NEW_ACCOUNT` | 120 |".
  - A creation transaction with a 24,576-byte runtime needs exactly 38,214,154 on Sepolia, equal to the spec formula.
- The cap limits execution gas only (PoC L64-65): correct.
  - eip-8037.md L68: "the transaction gas limit set in EIP-7825 only applies to execution-gas".
  - eth_call does not enforce the cap, so I checked mined transactions. Of the last 600 Sepolia blocks (head 11,889,266), 636 transactions had a gas limit above 2^24.
  - Tx 0x929a062a…9362, sent to the 0x4e59 factory: status 1, gasUsed 17,061,883.
  - Creation tx 0x209bb488…bb1f: limit 45,375,140, status 1, gasUsed 31,745,506.
- Forge's 130% multiplier (PoC L56-58): correct for the documented flags. From foundry v1.7.1 source:
  - script/src/lib.rs L151-153: `#[arg(long, short, default_value = "130")] pub gas_estimate_multiplier`.
  - transaction.rs L164-168: "We inflate the gas used by the user specified percentage", then `unsigned.set_gas_limit(result.gas_used * gas_estimate_multiplier / 100)`.
  - The simulation runs under the configured fork rules (lib.rs L792 `.spec_id(self.config.evm_spec_id())`), which foundry.toml L9 sets to `evm_version = "cancun"`.
  - eth_estimateGas is used only with --skip-simulation or on special chains. broadcast.rs L498-500: `estimate_via_rpc = has_different_gas_calc(chain) || ... || self.args.skip_simulation`. L142: `if !is_fixed_gas_limit && estimate_via_rpc`. Sepolia and mainnet are not in that chain list (cli/src/utils/cmd.rs L114+).
- Code deposit 200/byte today (PoC L60): correct.
  - Measured marginal cost on mainnet is 216.3 gas per byte.
  - My Cancun model of a full chunk, 5,379,462 gas used, plus the 63/64 margin (about 78k) matches mainnet's minimum eth_call gas of 5,457,524.

(2) DOES THE MEASUREMENT MATCH THE PoC'S ~38.26M? Yes, within 0.7%.
- Gas a full chunk uses:
  - spec model: 38,227,746 (spec agent) and 38,227,750 (mine)
  - geth eth_createAccessList on Sepolia: 38,228,130
  - PoC: 38,264,022, about 36k high. It keeps Cancun's 32,000 CREATE (Glamsterdam's CREATE_ACCESS is 12,000) and the 21,000 base (Glamsterdam: 12,000 + 3,000 cold). It also includes the script's own measurement overheads: the 2,600 cold CALL and 1,540 of initcode words counted twice (DeployKilim.s.sol L924 `g += _intrinsic(data) - 32_000;`, where `_intrinsic` at L930 adds `2 * words` again).
- Sepolia eth_estimateGas: 38,532,308 (measurement agent) and 38,532,320 (spec agent).
- The smallest gas limit that works is higher than gas used. Whatever state gas the reservoir does not cover comes from the create frame's gas, and the factory keeps 1/64 of that:
  - spec: 38,483,089
  - measured: 38,626,249 (measurement agent's bisection) and 38,824,724 (drpc and Tenderly). publicnode was flaky, between 38,483,301 and 38,585,163.
  - So the PoC's "need" is 0.22-0.56M too low as a gas limit. Its comment at L80-81, "the limit must cover their sum", should say: sum plus about 1/64 of the uncovered state gas, or at least 16,777,216 + state gas = 54,562,096.
- The raw Sepolia estimate is 93,941 gas below the measured minimum. eth_call at exactly 38,532,308 reverts. A transaction must never be sent at the raw estimate (`-g 100`).
- Stale PoC text: L35 and L42 say "about 6.0M" and "about 7.8M". The live run logs 5,394,342 and 7,012,644. The 6.0M looks like AUDIT.md L412 ("the largest 5,992,449"), from the 46-chunk store.
- The contracts test uses stand-in constructor arguments and a stand-in page (TestBase.sol L167-186). So the 1/1's Cancun gas is 2.51M there, against 6,750,528 for the real store (AUDIT.md L412). It also compares only against the deposit state gas. Both make the test conservative; the conclusion holds by a wide margin.

(3) WHAT THIS MEANS FOR THE LAUNCH
- Store total for 54 chunks (2 grids, 1 names, 16 prefix, 1 head, 34 tail):
  - today (Cancun/Osaka rules, gas used): 275,082,854
  - Glamsterdam: 1,954,951,264 (execution 22,617,874, state 1,932,333,390), about 7.11 times more. The spec agent got 1,954,951,048.
  - At the current mainnet base fee of 0.0619 gwei: about 0.017 ETH today, about 0.121 ETH on Glamsterdam, before priority fees.

  - Head chunk (197 B): needs at least 522,017.
  - With today's 60M mainnet limit, two full chunks (about 75.6M together) cannot share a block. 50 of the 54 chunks carry more than 30M state gas, so the store would need at least about 50 blocks. The spec agent's "about 33" assumes chunks can be split across blocks, which they cannot.
- Contracts versus the 8M policy (DeployKilim.s.sol L78 `uint256 public constant MAX_TX_GAS = 8_000_000;`):
  - Today all three pass: Cancun 3.21M / 6.75M / 3.40M (AUDIT.md L412).
  - On Glamsterdam each is about 18.1-24.9M, above both 8M and 16,777,216 in total, though execution stays under the cap.

- Do the documented commands sign gas limits that fail? Yes, on any Glamsterdam chain.
  - The commands (checklists/2-deploy.md L16-22) are `--broadcast --slow --timeout 600 --ledger`, with no `--skip-simulation` and no `-g`. So the limit is forge's Cancun simulation times 1.3:
    - full chunk: about 7.0M, against at least 38.5-38.8M needed
    - head chunk: about 125k, against 522k
    - KilimMotifs: about 4.2M, against at least about 17-18.6M
    - KilimOneOfOne: about 8.8M with the real store, against about 24.9M
    - KilimAuction: about 4.4M, against at least about 18.1M
  - checklists/2-deploy.md L43 is wrong for these flags: "the broadcast gas limit comes from Ethereum's own estimate plus margin". It comes from forge's local Cancun simulation (transaction.rs L164-168).
  - On mainnet today the same flags are fine: 7.0M is above the minimum of 5,457,524 for a full chunk, and the creations sit far under the cap.
- What the Sepolia rehearsal does today:
  - The script's dry run passes. It logs about 5.4M per chunk, "under 8M".
  - Forge signs the first transaction, grids chunk 0 (sections are ordered grids, names, prefix, head, tail; DeployKilim.s.sol L245), at about 7.0M.
  - With tx.gas under 2^24 there is no state reservoir (eip-8037 L95-98). The create frame runs out of gas at the code deposit, the factory reverts, and the receipt has status 0. Nearly 7M gas is burnt, which is negligible on Sepolia at a 15 wei base fee.
  - `--slow` then stops the run. foundry progress.rs L279 pushes "Transaction Failure", and L295 calls `eyre::bail!(error_msg)`.
  - No chunk lands. The store sender is not the deployer, so the deployer's nonce is untouched. runContracts then refuses with "store not deployed: runStore first".
  - If the store were deployed some other way, runContracts with the documented flags would fail on KilimMotifs at nonce n. That spends the published nonce, which voids the addresses and the motif layout (checklist L53-56).

(4) SAFEST PLAN
- Deploy everything on mainnet before Glamsterdam activates there: the store and, better, the contracts too.
  - No mainnet date is known. eip-7773.md L66-68 has the Sepolia row "353024 | 1791294816 (2026-10-06 13:53:36 UTC)" and empty Hoodi and Mainnet rows.
  - EIP-8037 is "status: Last Call", "last-call-deadline: 2026-11-01" (L7-8). The EF blog of 2026-09-17 says the mainnet date is not decided. Hoodi has to come first.
  - Under current mainnet rules the documented flags work, and every transaction passes the 8M policy. AUDIT.md L292 already says "deploy the data store before Glamsterdam reaches mainnet". checklists/1-pre-deploy.md L213 says the same.

Full chunk: 38,532,308 × 1.3 = 50,091,999, above the worst observed minimum of 38,824,724. Head chunk: 679k, above 522k. Contracts: estimate × 1.3. Never go below about 101%.

- The repo still needs, if this is accepted: a correction to the claim in checklist L43; the 46/252M figures updated to 54 chunks / 275M; and a Glamsterdam mode in the script's policy, or a stated rule that the 8M policy is valid only before Glamsterdam.
